docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Open-ALAQS are listed here. Format follows Keep a Changelog loosely; dates are ISO 8601.

Upgrading a 5.4.1 study: see Upgrading from 5.4.1. Results of the shipped examples and of the validation fixtures do not change (plugin, standalone and CAEP14 reference outputs identical to 5.4.1). The fixes below change results only for the cases they name.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Calculate Dispersion, Generate from OpenALAQS output: the emission settings (Method, Apply NOx Corrections, Atmosphere Aloft, BFFM2 Fuel-Flow Source, Source Dynamics) can be set as on the Configuration tab of Visualize Emission Calculation. The emissions were always recalculated with bymode, no NOx correction and no source dynamics, which stay the defaults. With BFFM2, all ticked pollutants are calculated as in any BFFM2 run, so CO2, SOx and PM10 change too (BFFM2 fuel flow).
  • Calculate Dispersion: Roughness Length, Displacement Height and Anemometer Height can be set in both Generate options; they were always 0.1 / 0.6 / 10.6 m. The defaults (0.1 m, 0, 0; 0 derives the value from z0) write the same austal.txt as before.
  • Calculate Dispersion, Generate from OpenALAQS output: flight segments and roadways are clipped to the calculation grid, as in the Dispersion Models tab; the emissions of segments beyond the grid were counted in the AUSTAL source rates. Results change for studies whose flight paths or roadways extend beyond the grid (for example NOx 1.775 to 1.770 g/s in one hour of the AIRPORT_A test study).
  • Calculate Dispersion: the receptor height (Receptors CSV column height, or the height stored with the inventory's receptor points) is passed to AUSTAL; every receptor was placed at 1.5 m. The receptor points stored in a study are now written to austal.txt; reading them failed for every study, so none were written.
  • Calculate Dispersion, Generate from CSV: a PM10 fine fraction field (default 0.9, as before).
  • Calculate Dispersion: with NOTALUFT ticked, the options string keeps SCINOTAT (NOSTANDARD;NOTALUFT;SCINOTAT;Kmax=1), as the standalone writes it. Output files of NOTALUFT runs are written in scientific notation (format only); the result windows read both notations.
  • Taxi: with only set_time_of_main_engine_start_before_takeoff_in_s set, single-engine taxi was applied to the end of the taxi, after the main engines start; it now applies before that point. Results change for movements that set this field (no shipped example does).
  • Taxi: with single-engine taxi set and no taxi segment inside the single-engine window, the start emissions of the single-engine-taxi engines were not counted; every engine now starts once per departure.
  • Taxi: with gate_emissions_code 0, the start emissions of the single-engine-taxi engines were still added; they are now left out, like the other start, GSE and GPU emissions.
  • Taxi: the queue of a departure with single-engine taxi was counted on the engine count of the last route segment, even when the main engines start during the queue. It is now split at the main engine start: before it on taxi_engine_count engines with taxi_fuel_ratio, as a single-engine segment, after it on all engines. Results change for departures with taxi_engine_count, a main engine start time and a queue (no shipped example sets these times).
  • Standalone (and the Dataiku library): single-engine taxi as in the plugin. The standalone ran all taxi on all engines and multiplied the whole route by taxi_fuel_ratio. It now reads taxi_engine_count and the three main engine start/off times, runs the route segments and the part of a departure's queue on the single-engine side of those times on taxi_engine_count engines with taxi_fuel_ratio, and everything else on all engines without the ratio; the taxi emission is placed on the route segments accordingly. taxi_fuel_ratio without a main engine time no longer has an effect, as in the plugin. Results change for movements with a main engine start/off time or a taxi_fuel_ratio other than 1 (none in the shipped examples); with them, plugin and standalone movement totals now agree to 1e-8 or better (they differed by up to 68 %).
  • Taxi with BFFM2: an engine without an emission index at the taxi thrust stopped the calculation with an error; the movement now gets no taxi emissions and the log names the missing index.
  • Engine tests with the BFFM2 thrust mode: the meteo row is the one nearest to the event midpoint; the plugin always used the last row of the meteo table. Results change for BFFM2 engine tests when the meteo table has more than one row. The standalone looks up the exact midpoint too; it rounded it down to the second, which picked the other row at a tie.
  • Movements file with a missing, misspelt or unknown header name: rows with 20 fields are read in the documented column order (with gate_emissions_code after apu_code) instead of being shifted from column 13 on, and the log names the unknown and missing headers. A header that ends with domestic (old files) keeps the old order: the 19 legacy columns, then gate_emissions_code when present. Files with a correct header are read as before.
  • Movements file without a header line: the first line was taken as the header, so the first movement was lost; the file check also left it out of the movement count and the study period. A first line that starts with a date is now read and checked as a movement, by position, with a warning.
  • Calculation settings: choosing a pollutant no longer resets Method from BFFM2 to bymode; after a pollutant without BFFM2, selecting CO, HC or NOx brings BFFM2 back. Loading a configuration replaces that remembered choice.
  • Standalone and CAEP14 reference: the meteo row of a movement is the one nearest to the start of its hourly period, and the LTO ceiling is 914.4 m when the row has no mixing height. This matches the plugin for a study with hourly periods: the standalone and the reference always use hourly periods starting on the hour, while the plugin uses the study's time interval. They took the latest row at or before the runway time and fell back to the study's vertical limit. Results change only with missing or off-hour meteo rows, movements before the first meteo row, or an empty mixing height with a study vertical limit other than 914.4 m.
  • Standalone: BFFM2 segments that fall back (ADS-B fuel flow above the plausibility ceiling, or no power and no fuel flow) are reported with one warning per movement, as in the plugin.
  • python -m austal_prep reads source_aggregation, source_offset_cells and max_receptors from config.json; the defaults always applied.
  • Gate emissions: the log warning for an aircraft group matched to a near gate profile group named the two groups the wrong way round.
  • Movements calculated together: the flight emissions are calculated once per group of movements with the same engine, profile, runway and taxi route, the taxi emissions once per group with the same engine, route and taxi settings, and the gate emissions once per gate, aircraft group and direction. Each group used the aircraft, the tow_ratio or the gate_emissions_code of its first movement. The aircraft type and tow_ratio are now part of the flight key, the aircraft type of the taxi key and gate_emissions_code of the gate key. Results change for a movement whose aircraft type shares an engine and a profile with another type of a different engine count in the same hour (in the default data 86 engine and profile pairs are shared by types with different engine counts, for example A4 with one engine and A6 with two on 07P05GE220 and JET-MEDIUM-D-1), for movements with different tow_ratio with the NOx correction, and for movements with different gate_emissions_code at one gate.
  • Movements calculated together, tracks: the flight key did not hold the movement's track (track_id, shapes_tracks) or its runway direction, both of which shape the trajectory at the runway, so a movement flown along a track took the trajectory of a group member without one (or the reverse). Both are now part of the key. Results change for studies with tracks: on the training study, an A20N departure along a turning track next to one without got 4.18 kg NOx (bymode) instead of its own 4.32 kg. The standalone does not follow tracks (see its README, Limitations).
  • BFFM2: a profile point with no power setting and a zero or negative fuel flow stopped the whole calculation (TypeError); the segment now takes the bymode index, as a point with neither value.
  • BFFM2 taxi: an engine_thrust_level_for_taxiing outside the range of the twin-quadratic fit (for example 7 given for 7 %) stopped the whole calculation; the taxi now takes the TX mode values, with an error in the log.
  • NOx correction: a tow_ratio of 0, a negative value or NaN is replaced by 1 with a warning, in the plugin and the standalone; 0 made the plugin's correction factor negative (NOx −2.36 kg for a departure of the training study). The standalone already used 1 for 0 and negative values, without a warning, and gave NaN NOx for NaN.
  • Standalone and CAEP14 reference aligned with the plugin on edge cases that the shipped fixtures do not reach: BFFM2 taxi at the movement's engine_thrust_level_for_taxiing (they used the idle fuel flow for any thrust), with the plugin's fallback for a thrust outside the fit; a flight segment with a power setting above 1.05 or below 0 and no supplied fuel flow takes the bymode index (the standalone kept the BFFM2 index, the reference extrapolated the fit and had no 1.0 to 1.05 clamp); a supplied fuel flow of 0 or below counts as none; a NaN tow_ratio counts as 1 in the standalone NOx correction.
  • BFFM2: the log message for a power setting outside the twin-quadratic range said "falling back to mode-anchor EI"; the segment takes the bymode index, and the message now says so. The fit's own error said "between 0.07 and 1.0", though 0 to 0.07 is accepted (extrapolated from the idle point); it now says "between 0 and 1.0".
  • Taxiway Routes Editor: the log warning "No routes defined" was written whenever the route list was refreshed without selecting a route, also when the study has routes; it is now written only when the study has none.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Reference data, default_airports (airport list of the ICAO lookup in the study setup): 5,035 airports instead of 5,060. 25 airports removed; 6 change their ICAO code, with the same name and position (SLCH to SLHI, SVAJ to SVNJ, VAHB to VOHB, WAJW to WAVV, WAMP to WAFP, WRKO to WATO); 55 elevations updated. Other rows unchanged. The table is not used by the emission calculation; new studies get it from the project template, and an existing study gets it with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py --refresh-reference-data (the table is in the default refresh set).
  • Study setup and calculation settings: the Vertical Limit fields are greyed out with a tooltip: they have no effect (the LTO ceiling is the hourly mixing height, or 914.4 m).
  • Gate emissions: aircraft of the group PROPELLER get no GSE or GPU emissions by design; this is now explicit in the code and the documentation (no change in results).
  • Documentation reorganised by reader (documents/user, methods, validation, developer), one page per topic, with an index, a glossary, input formats, troubleshooting, and a searchable site (tools/docs_site/mkdocs.yml); statements that disagreed with the code are corrected. tools/check_doc_links.py and .github/workflows/docs.yaml check the links on each pull request.
  • Documentation site published on GitHub Pages (https://eurocontrol-asu.github.io/open_alaqs/), one version per release (/<version>/, and /latest/ for the newest), built by .github/workflows/docs.yaml on each v* tag or when started by hand.
  • Toolbar: new Open ALAQS documentation button, and the About dialog links to the documentation; both open the site version of the installed plugin (/latest/ for a development version). The homepage in metadata.txt stays the EUROCONTROL page.
  • Dialog and form screenshots of the documentation retaken from the current forms with tools/docs_site/make_screenshots.py.
  • Aircraft emissions: a worked example runs one approach segment through bymode and the two BFFM2 fuel-flow sources, step by step (documents/methods/AIRCRAFT_EMISSIONS.md).
  • Training course slides (March 2026): an errata page lists where they differ from 5.4.1 (documents/user/TRAINING_COURSE_ERRATA.md).
  • Aircraft emissions documentation: where OpenALAQS differs from the published SAE methods, and by how much: the CO and HC curve between approach and climb-out (CAEP/14 rule, not SAE AIR 5715), no extrapolation below idle, the unscaled mode_anchor fuel flow (SAE AIR6183), the static conditions of the delta sqrt(theta) fuel scaling, the single NOx P3T3 exponent, and the taxi fuel flow (SAE AIR8035). The references to a "Doc 9889 Appendix 2" fuel-flow correction are replaced by SAE AIR 5715 (no change in results).
  • External links updated (ICAO Doc 9889, FOCA engine emissions, COPERT, QGIS installer).

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• scripts/update-strings.sh and scripts/compile-strings.sh: translation helpers for an i18n/ folder removed in 2021; the plugin has no translations.
  • scripts/run-env-linux.sh: QGIS 2 environment helper.
  • documents/developer/design/FUEL_FLOW_OPTIONS.md: design note based on non-public study material. What is implemented (the δ √θ fuel-flow scaling) is described in documents/methods/AIRCRAFT_EMISSIONS.md; the options not implemented are no longer documented.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • Regression tests for each fix above, and test_emission_calculation passes on QGIS 3.34 (the minimum version), where QGIS's own unordered layer comparison mis-pairs the fields.

Upgrading a 5.4.0 study: see Upgrading from 5.4.0 in the User Guide. Every BFFM2 inventory changes and should be recalculated; bymode inventories change only in the PM10 of segments above 3,000 ft (MEEM V1). No option gives 5.4.0 BFFM2 results back: ground_held restores the 5.4.0 ambient conditions only, the fuel-flow fix has no switch.

BFFM2 trajectory fuel flow and ambient conditions aloft. Results change for the BFFM2 methods. The fuel-flow fix (Fixed) changes bffm2_traj with ANP profiles (the fuel flow from the thrust share), the BFFM2 taxi fuel flow (bffm2_traj and bffm2_anchor) and BFFM2 engine tests in every study whose meteo is not ISA, and bffm2_traj in flight also at ISA (the e^(-0.2 M^2) term goes: +3 % at Mach 0.4). The atmosphere aloft (Changed) changes the BFFM2 indices of flight segments, the bffm2_traj fuel flow, the BFFM2 taxi and engine tests (station pressure) and, for every method including bymode, the MEEM V1 nvPM of segments above 3,000 ft (local T and p). bymode fuel, NOx, CO and HC are unchanged. Combined, on the example inventory (example/training, 13 movements): bffm2_traj NOx -11.3 %, CO2 -5.3 %, CO -1.7 %; bffm2_anchor NOx +0.3 %, CO -2.9 %, HC -4.9 %; bymode PM10 -0.01 %. Warm or windy studies should expect BFFM2 NOx changes above 10 %.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• scripts/migrate_alaqs.py: a 5.3.x study that had been edited in QGIS kept integer or text fields after the migration. QGIS writes per-column layer statistics (geometry_columns_field_infos) each time a layer is edited and, when they exist, types the fields from them rather than from the declared column types; the script rebuilt the shapes_* tables with REAL columns but left those rows, so the forms still refused a decimal with "Upgrade the study with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py" and the study still logged the unmigrated warning when opened. The rows of a rebuilt table are now removed, and a study retyped by the 5.4.0 script gets a ~ STATISTICS plan step that removes them (run the script again). QGIS then types REAL as Double on 3.34 and 3.44 and recomputes the statistics on its next edit; the layer's extent and row count are kept (tests/test_migrate_layer_statistics.py). The bundled example and test studies carry no such rows, which is why the 5.4.0 tests did not see it.
  • The fuel flow read on the ICAO curve at the thrust share is scaled to ambient with delta * sqrt(theta), the corrected-parameter scaling of gas-turbine performance (the corrected fuel flow, fuel flow / (delta sqrt(theta)), a function of the corrected thrust, thrust / delta, and Mach), in the plugin (Engine.getEmissionIndexByEngineState) and the standalone (compute_aircraft, taxi, compute_engine_test). It was delta / theta^3.8 / exp(0.2 M^2), the inverse of the BFFM2 conversion of a known fuel flow to reference conditions (SAE AIR5715), which is an emission-index step, not a fuel-flow model: the fuel flow fell with rising temperature (-12 % at 25 C, where the scaling gives +1.7 %). The emission indices are the standard BFFM2 lookup at the new ambient fuel flow, as for a supplied (ADS-B / CUSTOM) fuel flow. Training fixture (280.5-295 K, 99 400 Pa), fix alone: bffm2_traj CO2 -2.5 %, NOx -6.6 %; bffm2_anchor (taxi) CO2 -0.7 %, NOx -0.3 %, CO -2.9 %, HC -4.1 %. The CAEP/14 BFFM2 reference cases (index step) are unchanged; the CAEP14 reference implementation, the pinned plugin outputs and the training validation workbooks are updated. In the standalone austal pipeline (and the Dataiku recipe) engine tests are computed with the ICAO mode values ("snap") as in 5.4.0, so neither this fix nor the atmosphere option reaches them there; it applies to engine tests in the plugin and to direct calls of compute_engine_test_for_period with a database connection.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• AUSTAL site parameters: one default for the plugin's AUSTAL output module, the standalone (aircraft and austal subcommands), austal_prep and the Dataiku recipe (open_alaqs/core/tools/surface_layer_atmosphere.site_parameters): z0 0.1 m, the TA Luft (2021, Anhang 2) roughness length of airports; d0 6 z0 (0.6 m); ha 10 m + d0 (10.6 m), AUSTAL's own defaults. d0 and ha are derived from z0 whenever they are left empty (None, "", null; 0 in the plugin's spin boxes, which cannot be empty), so changing z0 alone keeps the three consistent. They were 0.2 / 1.2 / 11.2 m in the plugin (three independent fields) and 0.3 m / 4 z0 / 11.2 m in the standalone austal pipeline and austal_prep. Results change for the AUSTAL concentrations of studies that keep the defaults (dilution: AUSTAL derives its wind and turbulence profiles from z0, d0, ha and the hourly wind); studies with explicit values are unchanged. Emissions change only with the surface_layer atmosphere (not the default): on training_v3, bffm2_traj NOx -0.015 % against the old plugin defaults and -0.024 % against the old standalone defaults (CO2 -0.004 % / -0.007 %). How to choose the three values from the land cover (CORINE, TA Luft classes) and the anemometer site: user guide, "Roughness length, displacement height and anemometer height". The METAR converter still assigns the Obukhov length independently of z0 (a known limitation; a separate, later change).
  • Ambient conditions aloft (atmosphere_model; documents/ATMOSPHERE_ALOFT.md, open_alaqs/core/tools/surface_layer_atmosphere.py). The temperature, pressure and humidity of each flight segment are those at its start height, carried up from the hourly meteo row; until 5.4.0 the row was used at every height, with its sea-level pressure (QNH) as the ambient pressure.
  • standard_lapse (default): the station pressure from QNH and the airport elevation and the 2 m temperature, carried up with the ISA lapse rate and the hydrostatic law; humidity ratio of the ground air kept.
  • surface_layer (option): the boundary-layer temperature profile of AUSTAL 3.3 (BlmTemp, TalBlm.c) from the hour's wind, Obukhov length and mixing height, T* from the hour's temperature, without AUSTAL's -30/+40 C limits, the stability term up to the mixing height (stable hours: at most AUSTAL's stable mixing height, getHm; a missing, NaN or non-positive mixing height keeps that cap), -8.5 K/km above. The surface sensible heat flux implied by the row's wind and Obukhov length is bounded at 600 W/m2 (unstable) and 100 W/m2 (stable), OpenALAQS engineering limits: above them L is replaced by the value that gives the bounded flux, with a warning (the AUSTAL time series keeps the row's L for those hours).
  • ground_held: the hourly row at every height, the 5.4.0 ambient conditions (the fuel-flow fix still applies).
  • Checked against the De Bilt radiosondes of 2025 (450 soundings; the hourly METAR-derived rows of an airport about 50 km away as input; within the emission ceiling): T(z) - T(surface) bias / RMS for standard_lapse -1.3 / 2.9 K at 100 m, +0.3 / 1.4 K at 300 m, +2.0 / 3.1 K at 900 m; surface_layer -1.5 / 2.8, -1.2 / 1.7, -2.7 / 3.5 K (too cold, not more accurate). The fuel-flow factor delta sqrt(theta) at height is within 0.3 to 0.7 % RMS of the soundings for both, against 1.2 % (100 m) to 12.9 % (900 m) for the ground row held. standard_lapse is therefore the default (an earlier candidate had surface_layer). In summer the AUSTAL profile is the closer one above 300 m (July and August, 600 m: 1.5 K RMS against 3.0 K, on 15 soundings); see documents/ATMOSPHERE_ALOFT.md, section 6.
  • Applies to the Mach number, the bffm2_traj fuel flow, the BFFM2 indices and the MEEM V1 non-LTO ambient (all methods, bymode included; MEEM V1 then uses the local T and p instead of the method's ISA + delta T, and the delta T is not used) of flight segments; the BFFM2 taxi and BFFM2 engine tests use the station pressure. The ICCAIA NOx correction keeps the hourly row. ISA meteo (standalone --isa-meteo, or a period without a tbl_InvMeteo row) stays ISA at every height.
  • A temperature or sea-level pressure that is not a positive number, a profile temperature outside 180 to 340 K, or invalid site parameters (z0 <= 0, d0 < 0, ha <= d0) stop the run with an error naming the meteo row's date.
  • Limitations: the humidity ratio is kept aloft, so the relative humidity passed to BFFM2 can exceed 1 (in a layer that would be saturated, where the lapse rate also stays dry or ISA); not validated against measured fuel or NOx.
  • Options: GUI "Atmosphere Aloft"; standalone --atmosphere-model, --z0, --d0, --ha (aircraft and austal subcommands; austal uses one setting for the AUSTAL config and the emissions; both default to the shared site parameters above, z0 0.1 m, d0 6 z0, ha 10 m + d0; the site parameters matter for surface_layer only); headless runner (scripts/emissions_austal) keys atmosphere_model, atmosphere_z0_m, atmosphere_d0_m, atmosphere_ha_m, bffm2_ff_source; Dataiku recipe-config keys atmosphere_model, z0, d0, ha.
  • Training fixture (training_v3, MixingHeight 914.4 m), standard_lapse against the ground row: bffm2_traj CO2 -1.4 %, NOx -2.9 %, CO +1.0 %; bffm2_anchor NOx +1.2 % (per movement: bffm2_traj NOx down to -4.2 %, bffm2_anchor up to +4.3 %). The two BFFM2 methods can move in opposite directions: bffm2_anchor keeps the ICAO anchor fuel flow and converts it to reference conditions with theta^3.8, so on a steep NOx curve colder air lowers the index more than the ambient factor raises it (with surface_layer, which is colder, bffm2_anchor NOx is -1.0 %). bymode totals unchanged on that fixture (no segment above 3,000 ft). Plugin, standalone and CAEP14 reference agree; the surface_layer formulas agree with AUSTAL's C code to 7e-5 K (tests/test_surface_layer_atmosphere.py; bounds and degenerate inputs in tests/test_atmosphere_review_541.py).

Upgrading a 5.3.x study: see Upgrading from 5.3.x in the User Guide: which results change for which studies, and how to bring a study's own engine, aircraft and profile tables up to date (a project .alaqs keeps its own copies, which are copied into every new inventory).

Runway placement of flight profiles. Results change for every study with ANP arrivals or block and runway times on arrivals: emissions move along the runway, arrival rollouts that ran past their exit are shorter, and arrival taxi times lose the landing roll. Plugin and standalone share the rules (open_alaqs/core/tools/runway_placement.py).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• default_aircraft_engine_ei: the 32 FOCA engines (P001 to P004, P011, P111, P121, P131, PF01 to PF14, B601 to B603, B004, B134, T601 to T603, T717, T790) come from ACT_PRF 2.6.3 (CAEP14 FOCA, 2026-10-09), source "ACT_PRF 2.6.3 (CAEP14 FOCA 2026-10-09)": fuel, gases, pm10_ei and pm10_nonvol unchanged; nvpm_number_ei within 0.42 % (3 significant digits in the file); B004 and B134 get the file's sulphate (0.04896 g/kg) and organic vPM, which were 0 (pm10_sul_kg and pm10_organic_kg output columns); for B601, B602 and B603 the file's parts do not sum to its PMtotal (0.84 to 1.60 times, by mode), and they take the parts with pm10_ei (and p1_ei, p2_ei) = nvPM + volatile + sulphate (B601 approach 0.24 to 0.385 g/kg, taxi 0.23 to 0.294; B602 taxi 0.35 to 0.295). For the other FOCA engines pm10_ei is the FOCA total (the file has no parts for the pistons and turboprops). No bundled movement uses them, so no pinned output changes. In the CSV and the bundled .alaqs files (the old test fixtures tests/data/generic/generic_out.alaqs and gse_application/tests/example_db.alaqs have no FOCA rows). Results change for movements with B601, B602 or B603 (PM10; the default engine of 49 aircraft types, among them C25B, C56X and E55P) and with B004 or B134 (pm10_sul_kg, pm10_organic_kg), in a study whose engine table is refreshed (an existing study keeps its own copy).
  • default_aircraft_engine_ei: the FOCA turboprops T601, T602, T603, T717 and T790 had fuel_type AvGas; they are now Jet Fuel, so sox_ei 0.75834 g/kg instead of 0.2 (no turboprop of the table is AvGas any more). In the CSV and the bundled .alaqs files (not in generic_out.alaqs and example_db.alaqs, which have no FOCA rows); no bundled movement uses them. Results change (SOx) for movements with these engines (the default engine of 30 aircraft types), in a study whose engine table is refreshed.
  • Training example ADS-B tracks (example/training/training_ads_b_data.csv and its copy in validation/data/source_csvs, the CUSTOM profiles of training_out.alaqs and training_v3*.alaqs): fuel_flow was 0.083 to 0.119 kg/s for PHBBA at power 0.40 to 0.92, below the A20N's idle; it is now 2 × the ICAO fuel flow of 01P20CM128 interpolated at the row's power_setting (0.65 to 1.57 kg/s; PHRTM, unused, the same curve with its power raised to idle, 0.18 to 0.21 kg/s). Example results change for bffm2_traj only, movement 11: NOx 0.244 to 1.504 kg (13 movements 17.461 to 18.721 kg), training_v3 15.2745 to 16.8743 kg; pinned bffm2_traj CSV and both validation workbooks regenerated.
  • ANP arrivals touch down at the landing threshold plus the runway's Touchdown Offset for that end, else the profile's own distance from its 50 ft (15.24 m) threshold crossing (Doc 29 approach profiles have x = 0 at the touchdown). They were placed with the touchdown on the taxi route's runway exit, which put approaches 60 to 90 m too high at a 2.2 km runway and rollouts past the runway end.
  • The arrival rollout ends at the taxi route's exit when the exit comes first: the first crossing past the touchdown at or below 50 kt (ICAO Doc 9157 Part 2, rapid-exit reference speed), else the first past the touchdown. An exit past the rollout end leaves a runway stretch that is taxied (all engines; 2 L / (v_end + v_x), v_x = min(v_end, 18 kt)); it shares the movement's taxi time with the route, queuing shrinks first.
  • Arrival runway time is the touchdown (A-CDM ALDT): the profile's landing roll is taken out of block time minus runway time. Departure runway time is the start of the take-off roll (unchanged).
  • ANP departures brake-release where the taxi route last meets the runway (line-up point), not at the centroid of the route/runway overlap; a route that backtracks along the runway lines up where it leaves it.
  • Taxi routes are read in the direction of travel whatever the listing order of their taxiways (turned by the stand).
  • ADS-B (CUSTOM) profiles and tracks are placed as before.
  • The plugin's runway trajectory cache moves to cache_runway_trajectories_v5; older cache tables are no longer read.
  • MEEM V2 is implemented in meem_v2.py but not used; its adoption is to be decided. The emission calculation runs MEEM V1 for any meem_version value and logs a warning when another one is requested (MovementSourceModule).
  • UI field names harmonised: one name per field in the forms, the attribute table and the documentation, Title Case with units as "Name [unit]" (for example Touchdown Offset, Runway 1 [m], Vehicles per Year for parkings and roadways, Runway Direction and Operation Type for tracks, Hourly Profile, Heat Flux [MW]). The names are set as attribute-table aliases from the new per-layer fields map in alaqs_config.py, applied each time a study opens (openalaqsuitoolkit.apply_layer_field_config); database column names are unchanged. New features get defaults (heights and touchdown offsets 0, profiles default, gate type PIER, in study 1); the attribute table hides the OID column and lists In Study last, as a check box ("1" / "0") on parkings, roadways, point sources and area sources, and hidden on the layers that do not use it (runways, taxiways, gates, tracks, buildings). OID and Heat Flux [MW] are read-only; the taxiway time column, which no calculation reads, is hidden and not in the form; the emission factors filled in by Recalculate and Method are no longer editable in the forms. Activity Unit (point sources) is filled in from the selected Type and can be overridden per source; an existing source keeps its stored unit. Validation messages of the parking and roadway forms use the field names. Typos fixed ("Buiding", "Mw", the building name tooltip).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• default_aircraft_engine_ei: 28 ACT_PRF engines that were missing and have no twin in the table (08P28CM141 to 08P28CM156, 08P28RR154 to 08P28RR163, EEA-J9, EEA-J10; 112 rows, composed as the other ACT_PRF rows, OPR and 5th nvPM point from ACT_PRF), so 1065 engines; with them 890 jet engines carry an OPR. EEA-J9 has no PM data in ACT_PRF (all PM values 0 there) and is kept as in the source: its PM10, nvPM and sulphate PM are 0, so a study that uses it reports no PM for it (no default aircraft uses it). The other 48 ACT_PRF engines missing from the table duplicate rows under other ids (FOCA-n, EEA-*, 01P21RR124) or, for EEA-J6, differ from 1RR016 only by a zero nvPM, and are not added. EEA-J10 (ACT_PRF "E190-A") is selectable for the E190; the E190's default engine in default_aircraft stays 11GE144 (EEDB CF34-10E, as in 5.3.6), in the CSV, the templates and every bundled study.
  • CAEP14 validation: the BFFM2 index step is pinned to two CAEP/14 BFFM2 reference cases, non-LTO lean burn and LTO (validation/tests/test_caep14_bffm2_reference_case.py).
  • CAEP14 reference tool: helicopter active mode cut at the mixing height and the grid on the FOCA flight path, as the plugin and the standalone do since 5.3.2 (validation/tests/test_helicopter_caep14_reference.py).
  • CAEP14 validation: pinned plugin outputs re-exported from the plugin of this version, headlessly (validation/tools/regenerate_plugin_csvs.py: the four method targets, the stationary sources); plugin = reference = standalone on 15 of 15 training movements for the three methods and for bymode with the NOx correction, study meteo applied (validation/tests/test_plugin_csv_vs_reference.py). The validation workbooks validation/data/training_validation_reference.xlsx and example/training/training_validation_reference.xlsx are rebuilt from them by the new regenerate_training_validation_xlsx.py (plugin beside reference per movement, hourly plugin emissions, helicopters); compare_inventory_to_reference.py reads it from its new location and no longer carries hard-coded helicopter values. See validation/tools/CAEP14_VALIDATION.md, "October 2026".
  • documents/FUEL_FLOW_OPTIONS.md: what an ADS-B comparison showed about the fuel-flow step of the BFFM2 trajectory method, and proposed changes, none implemented in this release (speed correction and similarity scaling of the ICAO-curve fuel flow, reduced take-off thrust, runway rule and plausibility floor for supplied fuel flows, fuel-flow source switch).
  • Runway: Touchdown Offset per end (touchdown for the first-named end, new touchdown_2 for the other; each independent, empty or 0 = the profile's own touchdown distance). Studies without the column still load (their second end uses the profile's own distance); scripts/migrate_alaqs.py adds it empty. The touchdown value was stored but not used before this release: check it in existing studies, since a non-zero value now moves every ANP arrival landing on the first-named end; for the same touchdown on both ends, enter it in touchdown_2 too. The bundled studies carry 250 m on both ends.
  • Standalone: route and profile check report (runway_checks, emissions_folder/runway_checks.csv): exit before the touchdown, exit above 50 kt, exit after the rollout end, rollout or lift-off past the runway end, intersection line-up, ADS-B start of roll or exit away from the route, each with the input change that fixes it. Never blocks the run. The plugin logs the exit findings.
  • ADS-B import: one warning per flight whose fuel_flow points are below the ICAO idle fuel flow of its engine (aircraft total), with the number of points; the values are imported unchanged.
  • OSM import: a log line with the number of buildings added and where their heights come from (OSM height column, else the layer default, 0 m; with the bundled osmconf.ini the tag is not a column, so 0 m).
  • rebuild_training_example_inventory.py: --input-dir and --end (defaults: example/training, 2025-12-03 09:00:00).
  • OSM import: one warning listing the imported gate names already in the Gates layer or repeated in the import; the features are kept as imported. With a duplicate name the movements use one of the gates only.
  • Gates: the gate form colours the name when another gate has the same name, with a tooltip saying why; advisory only (OK and the saved values are unchanged).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Standalone austal receptor clipping (since 5.3.6): receptors were clipped to 75 x 250 m around the grid reference whatever the study grid (--grid-size/--grid-step defaults), so receptors inside a larger AUSTAL grid were dropped (training example: grid 100 x 100 x 20 cells of 250 x 250 x 50 m, receptors 9.4 to 12.5 km out); every run also printed a "grid_size / grid_step_m ignored" warning. Receptors are now clipped to the study grid (grid_3d_definition, as the AUSTAL grid); --grid-size/--grid-step (and the recipe keys grid_size/grid_step, now null in recipe_config.example.json) only override that square. Bundled outputs unchanged. Results change for standalone austal runs with receptors outside that 75 x 250 m square and inside the study grid: they are now kept.
  • UTM zone and AUSTAL reference point (since 5.3.6): the standalone (geometry, both make_config, orchestrate, the CAEP14 reference script) chose the UTM zone by formula, make_config always in the northern hemisphere and with 32631 when the longitude was 0.0 (orchestrate --receptor-input then stopped), while the plugin's Grid3D queries the PROJ database; they disagreed in the southern hemisphere and on zone boundaries (Sydney 32656 against 32756, lon 0.0 32631 against 32630). All now call one QGIS-free helper, open_alaqs/core/tools/utm.py utm_epsg(lat, lon), the plugin's query (first result; no Norway 32V or Svalbard exceptions, the Grid3D docstring said otherwise); a missing coordinate is checked with is None. Both make_config and orchestrate took the AUSTAL config reference from the airport of user_study_setup while the emission grid is centred on grid_3d_definition reference_latitude/longitude, so with the two apart aircraft cells were shifted against stationary sources and receptors (1374 m for a reference 0.02 deg east of Rotterdam); they now use the grid reference (the airport only when the grid definition has none, with a warning). No bundled result changes: the training studies have both points equal, in zone 32631 either way. Results change for standalone runs (make_config, orchestrate, the CAEP14 reference) in the southern hemisphere, on a UTM zone boundary or at longitude 0.0, and for the standalone's AUSTAL inputs of studies whose grid reference differs from the airport position.
  • Aircraft SOx was zero: sox_ei was 1.0 g/kg in every row of default_aircraft_engine_ei until the 5.0.0 rebuild, which set it to 0.0 without a note. SOx (as SO2) now comes from the fuel sulphur, 1000 × FSC × (1 − ε) × 64/32 (open_alaqs/core/tools/fuel_sulphur.py): 0.758 g/kg for jet fuel (FSC 0.000383, ε 0.01, the ICAO vPM parameterisation example; the stored pm10_sul stays at the FOA3 value, FSC 680 ppm) and 0.2 g/kg for AvGas (FSC 0.01 %, no sulphate), by the row's fuel_type. The shipped table and the bundled .alaqs files carry these values, except the old test fixtures tests/data/generic/generic_out.alaqs and gse_application/tests/example_db.alaqs, whose AEM-era rows keep sox_ei 1.0 (only their 112 rows of the 28 added engines have 0.75834; the tests that read them do not check SOx); a 0 or empty sox_ei in an existing study is replaced by the fuel's value at run time. Helicopters (FOCA gives no SOx) get mode fuel × the value (PISTON: AvGas). Plugin, standalone and CAEP14 reference alike; the plugin/reference gate now compares SOx. APU and GSE keep their own tables. Results change: aircraft SOx goes from 0 to 0.758 g per kg of jet fuel (training example: 1.849 kg for the 13 movements, bymode). Docs: pm10_sul corresponds to FSC 680 ppm with SO4/S = 96/32 (the docs said 667 ppm).
  • MEEM V1 nvPM now follows the MEEM V1 method (ICAO CAEP/13-MDG) and reaches the output. Its result went to nvpm_g_kg / nvpm_number_kg, which no output column reads, and it interpolated log-log at the segment's ANP power setting below 3000 ft, used the ground ambient and a pressure-ratio thrust mapping above it, and a T3 ratio as enrichment factor. Now (open_alaqs/core/tools/meem_v1.py, Engine.getEmissionIndexByModeWithMEEM): at or below 3000 ft (914.4 m) above the aerodrome (segment start height, the ICAO LTO cycle) the nvPM EI is the certification value of the mode, unchanged; above, the MEEM V1 chain (ISA at the segment altitude above MSL, i.e. start height plus airport elevation, Mach from the segment TAS, phase "CLIMB TO CRUISE" for departures and "DESCENT TO APPROACH" for arrivals, P3/T3, ground-reference thrust from T3, linear interpolation of the EEDB nvPM points, × (P3/P3_GR)^1.35 × 1.1^2.5). The mass EI replaces pm10_nonvol and pm10, p1, p2 move by the same amount, so pm10 = nonvol + sul + organic still holds; nothing else changes. OPR is press_ratio, 30 when empty (the EEDB has no value for this case); the climb pressure coefficient uses a default cruise altitude of 38000 ft. The implementation matches a MEEM V1 reference example (0.944536653843135 mg/kg, 2.58597485320693e13 #/kg) and seven further reference cases to 1e-15 (tests/test_meem_v1.py). The standalone (shared module) and the CAEP14 reference (its own copy of the formulas) do the same (validation/tests/test_meem_v1_reference.py). Results change only for segments more than 3000 ft above the aerodrome, i.e. in hours whose mixing height (height above the airport, like the segment heights) is above 3000 ft (914.4 m). Training example (example/training, 1500 m on 2 December): the two departures of 2 December, one segment each (start 1285 m and 1251 m above the airport, 1280 m and 1246 m above MSL, CL): nvPM EI 1.235 to 1.524 mg/kg (A20N, id 6) and 53.30 to 66.64 mg/kg (E190, id 8); bymode pm10_nonvol +1.24 % and +1.69 %, pm10 +0.031 % and +0.81 %; 13-movement totals pm10_nonvol 31.456 to 31.724 g (+0.85 %), pm10 321.741 to 322.010 g (+0.084 %) (BFFM2 trajectory: +0.76 % and +0.060 %). training_v3, AIRPORT_A and ANP references: no change (no segment above 3000 ft).
  • nvpm_number_ei of default_aircraft_engine_ei held the ACT_PRF nvPM number rate of the mode (#/s) while the code reads it as #/kg; it is now #/kg (ACT_PRF rate / fuel flow, equal to the EEDB v31 nvPM number EI in #/kg; for the FOCA piston and ECTL engines, which are in neither, the stored value / fuel flow). In the shipped table and the bundled .alaqs files. No output column carries nvPM number, so no output changes; the MEEM V1 number EI and the 5th number point now have consistent units (training example nvPM number, bymode, computed internally: 2.01e17 to 4.61e17).
  • default_aircraft_engine_ei: 1ZM001 (D-36) TX had fuel flow 0 and all EIs 0 (EEDB v31 FF_ID is 0); it now has the ACT_PRF idle values (fuel 0.092 kg/s, NOx 5.5, CO 20.7, HC 5.4 g/kg, nvPM 0.0767 g/kg, 3.87e15 #/kg), composed as the engine's other modes. Results change for the taxi of movements with 1ZM001 (the default engine of A124, A225, A743, AN72 and YK42), in a study whose engine table is refreshed.
  • MEEM V1 inputs: press_ratio and the 5th nvPM point (meem_nvpm_m_i_f00_avg, meem_nvpm_n_i_f00_avg, nvpm_m_max_mgkg, nvpm_n_max_nkg) were empty in every row; they now come from ICAO EEDB v31, ACT_PRF for engines not in it: OPR for 863 jet engines at this step, 5th point for the 51 EEDB 5-point engines; with the ACT_PRF engines (see Added) the table now has an OPR for 890 jet engines (the others keep 30) and a 5th point for 77 engines (mass) and 75 (number). The bundled .alaqs files get the columns where they lacked them. Results change for segments more than 3000 ft above the aerodrome (hours whose mixing height is above 914.4 m), in a study whose engine table is refreshed (a 5.3.x engine table has no press_ratio, so MEEM V1 uses OPR 30).
  • MEEM V1 LTO / non-LTO cut: at 3000 ft (914.4 m) above the aerodrome (ICAO LTO cycle) in the plugin (Engine._meem_v1, new airport_elevation_m argument of getEmissionIndexByModeWithMEEM), the standalone (compute_aircraft._meem_v1_segment_ei) and the CAEP14 reference (_meem_non_lto); a development build compared the altitude above MSL, so at an airport above 914 m every segment, the take-off roll included, went through the non-LTO chain (01P20CM128 approach at 1655 m: nvPM 1.189 instead of the certified 2.989 mg/kg). The airport elevation still sets the ISA altitude of the chain. Bundled studies (about −5 m): no pinned output changes.
  • MEEM V1 above 3000 ft used ISA; it now uses ISA + ΔT, ΔT the temperature of the movement's meteo period (the one BFFM2 uses) minus ISA at the airport elevation (288.15 K − 0.0065 K/m × elevation), constant aloft (the temperature offset at 0 ft MSL). Without meteo the temperature is ISA sea level (288.15 K), so ΔT = 0.0065 K/m × elevation (10.76 K at 1655 m), 0 only at sea level. Plugin (Engine.getEmissionIndexByModeWithMEEM(delta_t=...)), standalone and CAEP14 reference alike; checked against two more MEEM V1 reference cases. Results change above 3000 ft only. Training example (283 K at −5 m, ΔT −5.18 K, with the OPR above): bymode pm10_nonvol id 6 +0.86 %, id 8 −0.20 %, 13-movement totals pm10_nonvol 31.724 to 31.695 g (−0.09 %), pm10 322.010 to 321.981 g (−0.009 %); BFFM2 trajectory pm10 291.630 to 291.611 g. The OPR alone moves pm10 by less than 1e-5. training_v3: no change.
  • Plugin: the ICCAIA NOx ambient correction (bymode, "Apply NOx corrections") was applied to every flight segment, approach included; it is defined for take-off and climb-out, which is what its module and the standalone do. Now gated on the segment mode (MovementEmissionCalculator.NOX_CORRECTION_MODES). Results change for arrivals with the correction on: their NOx is no longer scaled by the correction factor (1 to 6 % higher than before on the training fixture's days); departures unchanged.
  • ADS-B import: with heights taken above the airport elevation (5.3.4), a take-off roll reported a fraction of an altitude step above the field (e.g. −15 ft at a −5 m field, +0.43 m) became climb-out (CL). The run of points within half an ADS-B altitude step (12.5 ft) of the field elevation at the start of a departure, or the end of an arrival, is now the ground: height 0, mode TO for departures (ads_b._snap_ground_heights, tests/test_adsb_airport_elevation.py). Results change only in the vertical position of those points for ADS-B tracks imported at airports with a non-zero elevation; re-import to apply.
  • scripts/migrate_alaqs.py --refresh-include-user-extensible stopped with "CSVs missing" (it listed default_helicopter_engine_ei, removed in 5.x); it now refreshes default_helicopter and default_helicopter_engines.
  • tests/test_emission_calculation.py (slow): the vector-layer comparison never compared emission values (QGIS checkLayersEqual(unordered=True) pairs the result's value with the expected layer's skipped fid), and the four source-type cases selected nothing (class names instead of the dialog's module names) and ran on all sources. The test now compares every cell's value and fails on an unknown source type; the 16 references are regenerated with tools/test_fixtures/regenerate_emission_calculation_references.py (output grid in UTM since #316, 5.1.0; ANP CO2 and NOx moved with the vertical-limit clipping of 5.3.1, ANP HC with release 5.2.0, whose notes name the start-emission keying; AIRPORT_A with the runway placement above).
  • Example study: movement 11 flew 1677686160_DIETB, a track carried in training.alaqs, while training_ads_b_data.csv held two other tracks that nothing used. Movement 11 now flies 1764584438_PHBBA from that file (as training_v3.alaqs does), DIETB is removed from training.alaqs, and training_out.alaqs is rebuilt from training.alaqs and the CSVs with the settings of documents/TEST_CASE_STUDY.md (new tools/test_fixtures/rebuild_training_example_inventory.py). The shipped inventory had been made from an older training.alaqs (airport at 51.96 / 4.44 and elevation 0 instead of 51.9574278 / 4.4417028 and −5 m, no custom_hourly profile) on a 40 x 40 x 20 grid of 10 m layers (200 m high); the tutorial's grid is 100 x 100 x 20 cells of 250 x 250 x 50 m. Example results change (bymode CO2 of the 13 movements, with this release's code: 5291 kg on the old inventory, 7703 kg on the rebuilt one, from the airport position, the PHBBA track and the tutorial's larger grid); example/training/training_validation_reference.xlsx is rebuilt.
  • Tutorial study example/training/training.alaqs migrated to the current project schema with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py (engine_test_events, shapes_area_sources.is_test_site, and the three named point-source profiles the other bundled studies carry), so the "Engine Test Site" flag can be set and saved in the tutorial. No other table changes.
  • Validation fixtures training_v3*.alaqs and tests/data/AIRPORT_A/AIRPORT_A.alaqs migrated to the current schema (touchdown_2, engine_test_events, is_test_site, ...; runway capacity dropped) and reference data (scripts/migrate_alaqs.py, profiles with tools/test_fixtures/regenerate_default_aircraft_profiles.py, which keeps study rows and now lists the three training_v3 files); PHBBA and PHRTM re-imported into training_v3*.alaqs with the importer above. The pinned plugin outputs reproduce to 2e-14 on the migrated fixture.
  • documents/TEST_CASE_STUDY.md: airport elevation −5 m (the form converts the database's −15 ft), coordinates as populated, the ADS-B import step, and the CUSTOM track of movement 11.
  • BFFM2 segment Mach: the plugin, the standalone and the CAEP14 reference computed (TAS / a) · √(288.15 / T), which is not a Mach number away from ISA; they now compute the flight Mach TAS / a, as SAE AIR-5715, the CAEP validation and documents/BFFM2_validation/BFFM2.md do (validation/tests/test_segment_mach.py). Results change slightly for bffm2_anchor and bffm2_traj away from ISA (Mach enters only through exp(0.2 M²)): on the training fixture's days, at most 0.08 % on NOx (bffm2_anchor) and 0.02 % on CO2 and NOx (bffm2_traj); bymode unchanged. Pinned plugin outputs and both validation workbooks re-exported.
  • Speed of sound for that Mach: a = √(γ R T) (γ 1.4, R 287.05287 J/(kg K), ICAO Doc 7488), shared by the plugin and the standalone (open_alaqs/core/tools/bffm2.py::speed_of_sound_m_s) and written out independently in the CAEP14 reference, as in the CAEP/14 BFFM2 formulation. The linear form 331.3 + 0.606 (T − 273.15) was 0.03 % high at ISA and 0.16 % high at 243.6 K and at 307 K. Results change below 0.01 % for the BFFM2 methods; bymode unchanged.
  • CAEP14 reference tool (validation/tools/compute_caep14_reference.py): engines are matched on engine_name exactly (or engine_full_name for rows without a name), as the plugin and the standalone do, instead of engine_full_name LIKE %engine_name%, which skipped every movement of a study whose engine table holds the real designation in engine_full_name and let short names match several rows; helicopters are the types listed in default_helicopter, not the movements without a profile_id. No change on the training fixture; see CAEP14_VALIDATION.md.
  • Training example (EHRD) taxi routes: the six routes were drawn for runway 24 but also used by the runway 06 movements, and taxiway V stopped 84 m short of the V1/V3/Y junction, so departures lined up 757 to 2116 m along the runway and lifted off up to 1.2 km past its end, and two arrival routes met the runway only before the touchdown. Taxiways V0 (closing the gap) and V1E (V1 to the 06 threshold) added; twelve routes, one per gate, operation and runway direction; movements 6, 8 and 13 use the 06 routes. The runway checks report no errors or warnings. Example NOx totals +0.1 % (bymode, bffm2_anchor) and +0.2 % (bffm2_traj), all from movement 13; the training_v3 validation fixtures got the same routes (pinned outputs unchanged, 6e-13). training_out.alaqs and the example workbook rebuilt.
  • Point sources: the Type was never saved (the form combo box was named type, the column is point_type).
  • Taxiways: the form wrote the text "Calculated" into the DECIMAL time column; the Time field is removed from the form (the calculation takes the time from the taxiway length and speed). The value is cleared (NULL) in the bundled studies; it was not read by any calculation.
  • Runways: a new runway left at the default selection (01) had no Runway Name (it was only built when a combo box changed); the form now builds it (01/19) when it opens empty.
  • Runways: the touchdown offsets are INT columns but the form accepted decimals; it now accepts whole metres only.
  • Point sources: "1000_m3 (legacy default)" was saved into activity_unit when the emission factor row has no unit; it is now placeholder text only and the field stays empty.
  • OSM import: the attribute mappings of buildings, gates and parkings were written {ALAQS column: OSM attribute} while the import reads {OSM attribute: ALAQS column} (as runways, taxiways and roadways), so gate names from the OSM ref tag were never imported.
  • Forms of existing features showed the first entry of their combo boxes instead of the stored value: the profiles (parkings, roadways, point and area sources), the point-source Category and Type and the Gate Type (shown as "(CARGO)", which blocked OK). The stored values are selected now; for point sources without changing the stored parameters and emission factors.
  • A NULL name, shown by QGIS as "NULL" in a new feature's form, passed the validation; an empty or NULL name now blocks OK on every form.
  • In Study on parkings, roadways, point sources and area sources: the form check box was hidden and disabled, and its form code wrote the flag after QGIS had saved, so it had no effect; on the previous version the check box also showed a stored 1 unticked and unticking it saved nothing, and a new source drawn through the form got a NULL flag (left out of the calculation). The check box is now shown under the name and bound to the column: it shows the stored value, saves what is set, and is ticked for a new source. The attribute table shows the flag as true / false. Results change for studies with sources created or edited through the form in 5.3.x: a source with an empty flag is still left out until its box is ticked and saved, and a source unticked in 5.3.x may still be in the study; check the flag.
  • Area sources: ticking or unticking Engine Test Site in the form and pressing OK did not change is_test_site (written after QGIS had saved, like In Study); a stored value was shown correctly. The check box is now bound to the column ('1' / '0', '0' for a new source), and the blank Units per Year and emission rates are set to 0 when it is ticked, before the save (they were also filled after it). The other layers' forms no longer carry the ineffective in-study write. Results change for area sources whose Engine Test Site box was ticked or unticked in 5.3.x: check the flag, which decides whether the source emits its rates or its engine-test events.
  • Point sources: Activity Unit can be edited (per-source override of the emission factor row's unit); it is filled in when the Type changes and an existing source keeps its stored unit.
  • Combo boxes of an existing feature (Gate Type, the profiles, the point-source Category and Type, the track Runway Direction and Operation Type, the roadway Scenario) showed the stored value as "(value)" whenever QGIS refreshed the form, for example when editing was toggled in the attribute table's form view. These fields now have a value map in the field configuration, built when the study opens (fixed lists, the study's profiles, stationary categories and types, runway directions, plus any value already stored), so QGIS fills the lists, shows the plain value and saves the choice; the forms no longer refill or write them. The point-source Type list shows the types of the selected category, and a type's defaults are only filled in when the user picks a category or type.
  • The forms' OK button looked enabled while the form was invalid (the click was ignored); it is now greyed out until the form is valid, and its tooltip names the missing or invalid fields. New features start with an empty name instead of "NULL".
  • Removed a debug print from the track form; the OSM import warning for an invalid feature no longer fails on layers without full_id.
  • scripts/emissions_austal: smooth & shift spellings reach the module as smooth & shift (were smooth_shift, run without source dynamics) and unknown source_dynamics values are an error; should_apply_nox_corrections takes true/false, 1/0, yes/no in any case (only True enabled it) and errors otherwise; austal_settings is read as a JSON object (a txt value failed in dict.update). Results change for runs of the script with smooth & shift or with should_apply_nox_corrections given in another spelling than True: these settings are now applied.
  • Standalone austal --pollutants co2 stopped with KeyError: 'co2'; the stationary sources now contribute 0 (one info line) and the aircraft CO2 is written.
  • compute_caep14_reference.py puts the repository root (parents[3], was parents[1]) on sys.path, so it runs from any working directory.
  • OSM import: the building filter value "commerical" is now "commercial", so OSM commercial buildings are downloaded and imported.
  • Forms under a German or Dutch locale: a decimal such as "0.125" was read as 125 by the field check (the locale reads "." as a group separator) while QGIS saves 0.125. Numbers are now read as QGIS saves them (see the next entry), and the parking and roadway Recalculate use the checked values (the fleet mix as "12,5" raised).
  • Form number check: it still fell back to the tolerant reading of convertToFloat (and int()), so it accepted texts that QGIS saves differently or as NULL: German "1,234.5" checked as 1234.5 and saved as 1.2345, French "1.234,5" and "1_000" saved as NULL, English "30,3" checked as 30.3 and saved as 303, "nan" and "inf" stored as such. The check now uses QGIS's own rule (QgsField.convertCompatible) and disables OK when it fails or gives a non-finite value, so the checked value (also the one Recalculate uses in parkings and roadways) is the saved one. Whole-number fields must also read as an integer with the locale (group separators as QGIS shows them, "20.000" German, "20,000" English); "12.5", which QGIS would round, is rejected.
  • Decimals typed into the layer forms were rounded or stored as text: the numeric columns of the shapes layers (height, speed, distance, idle_time, temperature, diameter, velocity, the *_percentage columns, vehicle_year, the emission factors, gate_height, taxiway speed and time, receptor xcoord, ycoord, 65 columns of 8 tables) were declared DECIMAL, which the QGIS SpatiaLite provider does not map to Double: it types the column from its stored data, so a column of whole numbers was an integer field (a typed 2.5 was saved as 3, and as 25 under a German locale) and an empty layer a text field (the text "30,3" was stored). The templates now declare these columns REAL, typed Double with or without data (2.5 is saved as 2.5). instudy, the touchdown offsets (whole metres) and the year/text columns are unchanged. scripts/migrate_alaqs.py converts existing studies (the tables are rebuilt with the reference definitions, rowids, keys and geometry triggers kept; text values that read as a number, "2.5" or "30,3", become numbers; other text is reported and left), and every bundled .alaqs with layers is converted (values unchanged; results of the training studies byte-identical). Opening a study whose layers still have the old columns logs one warning naming the migration. The form check converts a number with the layer's own field when the layer is known (parse_number(text, integer, field), validate_field(widget, type, layer), else the attribute form's layer), so it equals the save on an unmigrated study too (2.5 checked and saved as 3 in an integer column); without a numeric field it uses a Double field as before. The project template is a fresh rebuild: default_vehicle_ef_copert5 and 17 cells of default_aircraft_engine_ei now equal the CSVs exactly (up to 1e-12 relative from the earlier values; the training studies carry their own tables and their results do not change).
  • Form number check, decimal separator (rc6 review F2): convertCompatible falls back to the C locale, so under an English locale "30,3" passed the check silently as 303 (which QGIS saves) and "1,5" as 15. A text that is not a number for the current locale (QLocale.toDouble fails) is now refused even when QGIS would save a number from it: the field is red and the tooltip names the decimal separator of the locale ("use the decimal separator of your locale (.)"). "30,3" stays 30.3 under a German, Dutch or French locale, and "0.125" under a German locale stays 0.125 as QGIS saves it (GitHub #159).
  • Form value lists on Windows: a study under an extended-length path (\\?\C:\..., as Path.resolve gives for a long path, or \\?\UNC\server\share\...) gave an SQLite URI with the "?" in the authority, so the runway and profile lists of the forms were empty. The prefix is now stripped before the URI is built.
  • Taxi route without segments (rc6 review M7): queuing, APU, engine start, stop-and-go and brake wear are added to the last segment of the route, so a route none of whose taxiways exists added nothing and the movement lost them silently. They are now placed at the gate on a stand-in segment of 0 m and 0 s, with a warning. Not reachable with the bundled studies.
  • Standalone, the same case (rc7 review R4): a route naming taxiways that do not exist in shapes_taxiways was treated as unresolved, so the movement's whole taxi time counted as natural taxiing (times taxi_fuel_ratio) and the mass went to the runway intersection, where the plugin counts the existing taxiways only, and with none the whole taxi time as queuing (no fuel ratio) at the gate. The standalone now does the same (compute_movements._build_natural_taxi_times, one warning per route naming the missing taxiways; distribute_to_grid puts the stand phases over the gate polygon). Results change, standalone only, for studies whose taxi routes name taxiways that do not exist; none of the bundled studies does.
  • Forms, a study not yet migrated (rc7 review R1): on a 5.3.x study whose numeric layer columns are still DECIMAL, QGIS types a column of whole numbers as an integer and saves "2.5" as 3; rc7 made the form check agree with the save, so the rounding stayed silent. A decimal typed into such a column is now refused, the field red with a tooltip naming the value QGIS would save and the migration (UnmigratedColumnError); a whole number is accepted. Studies migrated to REAL columns are unaffected.
  • Visualize Emission Calculation, Source type list (rc7 review R3): choosing "MovementSource" builds the movement store, which raises on the same input errors as the calculation (a runway designator matching several or no runway end, an unknown gate or engine); the slot let the exception out as a raw QGIS Python error. It is now reported in the message bar ("Invalid Study Input") with the names list left at "all".
  • Runway designator messages (rc7 review N1, N2): a designator with a letter that matches no runway end ("24C" on 06L/24R and 06R/24L) is reported as unknown ("matches no runway end of the study"), no longer as ambiguous with the advice to add a letter; the end is echoed normalised ("6" as "06") in the plugin and the standalone alike.
  • scripts/migrate_alaqs.py (rc7 review N4, N5): texts left in a retyped column are reported once per column with their count and three examples, not once per row; a text with a decimal comma and exactly three decimals ("1,234", which is also a grouped 1234) is left as text and reported instead of being read as 1.234. The migration also removes geometry_columns_auth rows of tables that no longer exist (an orphan shapes_aircraft_tracks row in three bundled fixtures), as it did for the other SpatiaLite metadata tables.
  • Runway form: a NULL Touchdown Offset (touchdown_2 is added as NULL when a 5.3.6 study is migrated), shown as "NULL", kept OK disabled ("Missing or invalid: Touchdown Offset, Runway 2 [m]"); it now counts as empty, like "". The area source form treats a NULL heat flux the same way.
  • An arrival whose block to runway time was no longer than its landing roll got a taxi time of 0 s and lost all its taxi emissions (queuing, stop-and-go, APU, brake wear) with the warning "taxi route not defined properly". The plugin now keeps a 0 s taxi time and these emissions, as the standalone does, with a warning naming the two times. Results change for such arrivals: APU, stop-and-go and brake wear are counted (movements whose block time equals their runway time: see below).
  • Aircraft movements take the airport altitude (NOx ambient correction, MEEM V1 ISA temperature, LTO cut) from the study's airport elevation (user_study_setup.airport_elevation), as the standalone and the CAEP14 reference do; it came from the grid reference altitude of the Dispersion dialog, which can differ. The grid altitude is the fallback for a study without an elevation. Results change for studies where the two altitudes differ (NOx correction; MEEM V1 above 3000 ft).
  • Runway placement: the taxi route is oriented by its own gate (user_taxiroute_taxiways.gate), as in the standalone and the CAEP14 reference; it used the gate of the first movement of the route, while the runway trajectory is shared (and cached) by every movement of the route whatever its gate. Results change (placement on the runway) where the first movement of a route is at another gate than the route's own.
  • Forms of a study whose path holds "#", "?" or "%" (since the value maps read from the study): the lists read from the study (point-source Category and Type, profiles, runway directions) were empty, because the read-only SQLite URI was not percent-encoded and opened the wrong file; the point-source Category and Type then offered only the values already stored. The URI is now built with Path.as_uri() (Windows drive and UNC paths included).
  • Results change for studies with movements whose block time equals their runway time: the plugin dropped all their taxi emissions (APU, stop-and-go, brake wear) with "no taxi emissions", while the standalone kept them (training_v3 movement 1 with block = runway time: PM10 0.0030 against 0.0320 kg). The plugin now keeps them. Rule (plugin and standalone): the taxi time is |block time - runway time|, less the landing roll for an arrival, not below 0 s; at 0 s the route segments and the queue get no time, while APU, stop-and-go and brake wear are counted as for any taxi time. A movement without a block time still stops the calculation in both.
  • Results change for studies with a movement whose taxi route is flagged for the other operation (a departure on an arrival route or the reverse) and meets the runway more than once: the plugin oriented the route by the movement's D/A, the standalone by the route's own user_taxiroute_taxiways.departure_arrival, so they could pick a different line-up or exit crossing. The plugin now uses the route's flag too (the runway trajectory is cached per route); the movement's flag only when the route has none.
  • runway_placement.split_taxi_time counts a negative total taxi time as 0 s (it returned a negative route time; both callers already clamp, so not reachable), and truncate_after with the cut exactly on a profile row ends at that row instead of appending a duplicate end row (a 0 m last segment). Bundled outputs unchanged.
  • Results change in the standalone for studies with parallel runways (06L/24R and 06R/24L): runways were keyed by the designator number, so both runways had the keys 6 and 24, the second row of shapes_runways won, and every movement was placed on it with its Touchdown Offsets. Runways are now keyed by the full designator (movements.runway_of), as in the plugin. The runway checks (runway_checks) use the same lookup.
  • Results change, parallel runways with a plain designator (rc6 review F3): a movement naming a plain "24" on a study with 06L/24R and 06R/24L was computed on the first runway by the standalone, and dropped silently by the plugin (it matched the first runway whose name contained "24", then "24" was not an end of it: "Could not find runway direction", the movement absent from the results); a "24R" on a plain 06/24 study was dropped silently by the plugin and fell back to 06/24 in the standalone. Both now stop the calculation with an error naming the movement ("movement id 1: A20N A 2025-12-01 06:05: runway '24' matches 06L/24R and 06R/24L; name the runway end with its letter", or "matches no runway end of the study"); in the plugin it is the "Calculation Failed" message of the inventory dialog. Movements that were silently dropped now stop the calculation until the runway is named fully. The ADS-B import's runway lookup (get_runway_by_direction) gives no runway for an ambiguous end instead of the first, and falls back to the closest track point. The standalone's runway dict has no plain-number keys any more.
  • Runway form: a negative Touchdown Offset was accepted, but the runway placement ignores values of 0 or less and silently used the profile's own touchdown distance. The form now rejects it (OK disabled); 0 or empty still means the profile's own distance.
  • OSM import: a NULL OSM attribute (a NULL QVariant, not None) counted as a value: with an OSM source that has a height column (custom osmconf.ini) the import log counted every building as having an OSM height. NULL attributes are now skipped before the feature is created (the layer default applies, as it already did in a headless check) and the log counts only real heights.
  • Plugin movement set-up (MovementStore.initMovements): the per-movement table was built with float64 columns, so every name or object put in it raised the pandas FutureWarning "Setting an item of incompatible dtype is deprecated" (an error in a future pandas), plus a "Downcasting object dtype arrays on .fillna" warning. The columns are now object columns; no warning, bundled outputs byte-identical.
  • Standalone and austal_prep make_config, and orchestrate, stop with a ValueError ("no reference point") when the study has neither a grid reference (grid_3d_definition reference_latitude/longitude) nor airport coordinates (user_study_setup); 5.3.6 silently used (0, 0) and EPSG:32631. orchestrate stops even without a receptor CSV.
  • Tutorial study example/training/training.alaqs: the area source's is_test_site is '0' (was NULL after the migration), as in the template and the other studies.
  • example/training/training_out.alaqs rebuilt from the final training.alaqs and the example's CSVs (tools/test_fixtures/rebuild_training_example_inventory.py): it now carries the study's five day, hour and month profiles (heating_season, cooling_season and business_hours were missing) and E190 default engine 11GE144; plugin results on it are byte-identical, and so is the content of example/training/training_validation_reference.xlsx (kept).
  • Test fixtures tests/data/AIRPORT_A/AIRPORT_A_out.alaqs and tests/data/ANP/ANP_out.alaqs no longer carry runway trajectory caches (cache_runway_trajectories, _v4, _v5), and tests/test_emission_calculation.py and tests/test_emission_calculator_service.py run on copies of their studies, so a test run no longer writes into tracked files nor reads a committed trajectory back (tests/test_bundled_fixture_hygiene.py).
  • scripts/migrate_alaqs.py --drop-extra-columns rebuilt the table from column names and types only, so PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL and defaults were lost (dropping capacity left shapes_runways.oid without its key, and a runway added in QGIS then got no oid). It now uses ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN (SQLite 3.35 or later); where SQLite refuses, the table is rebuilt with the reference definitions of the kept columns, rowids, indexes and triggers kept (tests/test_migrate_drop_columns_keeps_keys.py). shapes_runways.oid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL restored in validation/data/training_v3.alaqs, training_v3_gatemovements.alaqs, training_v3_multisource.alaqs and tests/data/AIRPORT_A/AIRPORT_A.alaqs (rows, geometry triggers and geometry registration unchanged).
  • openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/source_csvs/training_movements.csv was the example's movement set plus the two helicopters, not the movements of the validation fixtures: it is now the movement table of training_v3.alaqs (15 movements; runways, gates and routes differ from the example on 7 rows), described in openalaqs_standalone/USAGE.md and checked by validation/tests/test_source_csvs_match_fixture.py. The study description of the three training_v3*.alaqs files says 15 movements (was 13).
  • Template build (tools/template_build/generate_templates.py) reads the CSVs with float_precision="round_trip": a rebuild stores the CSV values exactly (the default parser was up to a few ulp off). The shipped templates are not rebuilt; tools/template_build/README.md lists what a rebuild changes (column order of shapes_runways, row order of the geometry metadata, timestamps, and in project.alaqs 1 to a few ulp in 26780 default_vehicle_ef_copert5 rows and 17 default_aircraft_engine_ei cells, where the shipped files are not the CSV text values).
  • validation/data/training_v3*.alaqs: the unused CUSTOM profile 1677686160_DIETB (9 rows, no movement uses it) removed. It stays in tests/data/AIRPORT_A/AIRPORT_A.alaqs, whose movement CSV (AIRPORT_A_movements.csv, row 12) and inventory use it.
  • Docs: scripts/emissions_austal/README.md describes the AUSTAL demo sample_data/Inventory.alaqs as it is (an early training inventory: old airport position, runway table and routes, six movements naming profiles absent from the file), not as derived from the current training_out.alaqs; example/training/training_engine_test_events.README.md no longer asks to migrate the training study, which ships with the engine-test-site schema.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • Runway Capacity (no code used it): removed from the form, the Runway object and the templates. Older studies keep the column; it is ignored.

Aircraft profile catalogue (default_aircraft_profiles.csv) and default profiles (default_aircraft.csv) corrected against ANP v2.2; BFFM2 plausibility limit on supplied fuel flows raised to 1.5 times the ICAO take-off value; pyarrow pinned below 26. Results change for movements without a profile_id, for the profiles listed below, for BFFM2 trajectory runs on propeller aircraft, and for ADS-B / CUSTOM points between 1.0 and 1.5 times the take-off fuel flow. Details and checks for the profiles: documents/AIRCRAFT_PROFILES_PROVENANCE.md.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• 47 ANP v2.2 type profiles were missing (every profile of GIIB, HS748A and PA30, and e.g. A321-232-D-1, CNA441-D-1, A330-301-A-1): commit ab42da5 had renamed them into the group profiles. They are back, as copies of their group.
  • 757300-A-1 had 4 points and started at 50 ft; restored to its 31 ANP fixed points.
  • power of the 17 CNT (%) aircraft (C130, DHC8, CNA172, DC3, ...) was a percentage divided by the static thrust (departures 0.01 to 0.33); now thrust / static thrust. RPM aircraft (CNA206, CNA20T, PA28, PA31) carried RPM / static thrust (up to 6.25); their power is now empty. Values above 1.0 are capped at 1.0. BFFM2 trajectory no longer falls back to the mode-anchor EI on 23 profiles.
  • CNA206-D-1 was the 3,600 lb departure; now the 3,000 lb one (stage-1 weight), like CNA20T-D-1.
  • Empty weight_kgs filled for 73 profiles (all 7378MAX and A350-941 profiles among them).
  • The ANP 2.1 profiles (COMJET, DHC-2FLT, GASEPF; 13 profiles) are removed: no type defaults to them and they had no weight or power. In a new study, a movement that names one of them gets the aircraft's default profile, with a warning. Existing studies keep their own copy.
  • Groups of the wrong propulsion class: PISTON-D-1 was a jet climb (ECLIPSE500), now CNA172; PISTON-D-2 was a turboprop (CNA208), now PA31; TURBOPROP-D-4 was a jet (IA1125), now EMB120.
  • requirements.txt: pyarrow<26. pyarrow 26.0.0 (released 2026-10-09) requires NumPy 2, and numpy is pinned to 1.26.4, so pyarrow failed to import and every parquet step (standalone AUSTAL runs) failed.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• default_aircraft.csv: 658 types now default to a type-specific ANP v2.2 profile (stage-1 departure, A-1 arrival) instead of a group: 184 through the ANP v2.2 substitution workbook, 474 through the nearest-MTOW ANP aircraft of the same propulsion and engine count. The other 1,261 types (mostly without an MTOW) keep their group. Mapping: tools/anp22_profiles/output/default_aircraft_mapping.csv.
  • BFFM2 trajectory: a supplied (ADS-B / CUSTOM) fuel flow is now rejected only above 1.5 times the engine's ICAO take-off fuel flow (ADSB_FF_CEILING_FACTOR), instead of above the take-off value itself. The ICAO value is a static, sea-level test-bed figure: in flight, a high-thrust climb point can burn a few percent more, and such points were replaced by the mode anchor (the climb value for climb points). Above the take-off point the BFFM2 indices stay bounded (NOx at its take-off value, CO and HC at the mean of the climb-out and take-off values), so no other guard is needed. The limit still catches wrong units, a total fuel flow entered per engine and a wrong engine count. Plugin, standalone and the CAEP14 reference tool use the same factor. The log message for rejected points now says that the mode-anchor fuel flow is used.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• tools/anp22_profiles/build_anp22_profiles.py: reproduces both CSVs from the 5.3.5 tables and the ANP v2.2 tables.
  • tools/test_fixtures/regenerate_default_aircraft.py.
