docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Short definitions of the terms and abbreviations used in the OpenALAQS documentation, in alphabetical order. Each entry links to the page that explains the term in full.

A · B · C · D · E · F · G · I · L · M · N · O · P · Q · R · S · T · V · Z

docs.title: A
docs.text:
.alaqs file: an OpenALAQS file (SQLite). The study file holds the geometry, the sources and the study setup; the inventory file (<name>_out.alaqs) is made from it by Calculate Emissions Inventory, with the movements and the meteorology. User Guide

Activity profile: hourly, daily and monthly factors that spread the annual activity of a stationary source over the year. User Guide, method

ADS-B: recorded flight tracks (position, height, speed, power setting or fuel flow) that replace the standard flight profile of selected movements. Format, method

ANP: the Aircraft Noise and Performance database (EUROCONTROL/EASA), source of the standard departure and arrival profiles. Flight profiles, provenance

APU: auxiliary power unit of an aircraft, set per movement with apu_code. Method, movements format

Atmosphere Aloft (atmosphere_model): how the temperature, pressure and humidity at each flight segment's height are derived from the hourly meteorological row: standard_lapse (default, ISA lapse rate), surface_layer (AUSTAL boundary-layer profile) or ground_held (ground values at every height). Ambient conditions aloft

AUSTAL: the Lagrangian dispersion model of the German TA Luft, used by OpenALAQS for concentrations. Installation, use

docs.title: B
docs.text:
BFFM2: Boeing Fuel Flow Method 2 (SAE AIR 5715). It derives the NOx, CO and HC emission indices from the fuel flow, corrected for ambient conditions. BFFM2

bymode: the method that uses the ICAO engine emission indices and fuel flow of each LTO mode. Methods

docs.title: C
docs.text:
CAEP14 reference: the project's independent implementation of the CAEP/14 engine emissions calculation, used to check the plugin and the standalone pipeline. CAEP14 reference validation

COPERT: the EU road-transport emission model; OpenALAQS uses its emission factors (with the EMEP/EEA Guidebook) for roadways and parkings. Method, data

CUSTOM profile: a flight profile made from an ADS-B track. ADS-B

docs.title: D
docs.text:
d0: displacement height of the wind profile, in m. See Site parameters.

δ, θ (delta, theta): ambient pressure and temperature divided by their ISA sea-level values; the fuel flow derived from a power setting (BFFM2 trajectory source, taxi) is scaled with δ√θ. Fuel flow

docs.title: E
docs.text:
EEDB: the ICAO Aircraft Engine Emissions Databank: certified fuel flow, emission indices and nvPM of each engine and LTO mode. Reference data

Engine test site: an area source flagged as a run-up pad; its emissions come from a list of engine test events instead of emission factors. User Guide, method, format

docs.title: F
docs.text:
FOA3: the ICAO First Order Approximation for volatile particulate matter (sulphate and organic). Particulate matter

FOCA 2015: the Swiss Federal Office of Civil Aviation guidance on helicopter emissions, used for helicopter movements. Helicopters

Fuel-flow source: for BFFM2, where the fuel flow of a segment comes from: trajectory (from the segment's thrust, scaled to ambient) or mode_anchor (the EEDB fuel flow of the segment's mode). Fuel-flow sources

docs.title: G
docs.text: GSE, GPU: ground support equipment and ground power unit at the gate. Method

docs.title: I
docs.text:
ICCAIA NOx correction: the correction of the bymode NOx emission index for ambient temperature, humidity and take-off weight (tow_ratio) on take-off and climb-out (Apply NOx Corrections). NOx ambient correction

In Study: the attribute that includes a source in the calculation. User Guide

ISA: the ICAO International Standard Atmosphere (15 °C and 1013.25 hPa at sea level, 6.5 K/km lapse rate).

docs.title: L
docs.text: LTO cycle: the ICAO landing and take-off cycle below 3,000 ft (914.4 m) above the aerodrome, with the modes taxi (TX), approach (AP), climb-out (CL) and take-off (TO). LTO modes

docs.title: M
docs.text:
Mach number: the true airspeed divided by the speed of sound at the local temperature. BFFM2 uses the Mach number of each flight segment's start point to convert the fuel flow to reference conditions; taxi uses 0. BFFM2, step 2

Main engine start (MES): the emissions of starting the main engines, and the time of the start during taxi. Main engine start

MEEM V1: the ICAO CAEP/13-MDG method that gives the nvPM emission indices of the segments above 3,000 ft. MEEM V1

Mixing height: height of the atmospheric boundary layer, in m, from the meteo file. It is also the emission ceiling of each hour. Meteorology

docs.title: N
docs.text:
NOTALUFT: an AUSTAL option that writes per-hour concentrations, needed for time series and the compliance report. Calculate Dispersion dialog

nvPM, vPM: non-volatile (soot) and volatile particulate matter. Particulate matter

docs.title: O
docs.text: Obukhov length: a measure of atmospheric stability, in m, from the meteo file. Meteorology

docs.title: P
docs.text: Profile (flight profile): the sequence of points (distance, height, speed, power) that a movement flies; standard profiles come from ANP. Flight profiles

docs.title: Q
docs.text:
QNH: the sea-level pressure reported in METAR, given in the meteo file as SeaLevelPressure(Pa). Ambient conditions aloft

Quality level: the AUSTAL setting of the number of particles (qs); a higher level lowers the statistical uncertainty and lengthens the run. Calculate Dispersion dialog

docs.title: R
docs.text: Receptor point: a point where AUSTAL writes a concentration time series. Format

docs.title: S
docs.text:
Site parameters: the roughness length z0, the displacement height d0 and the anemometer height ha written to AUSTAL. Site parameters

Smooth & Shift, source dynamics: spreading of the aircraft emissions over a volume around the flight path, to represent the initial spread of the exhaust plume (options none, default, smooth & shift). Source dynamics

Standalone pipeline: openalaqs_standalone, the QGIS-free implementation of the calculation for batch runs. Running without the QGIS window

docs.title: T
docs.text:
TA Luft: the German Technical Instructions on Air Quality Control, which define AUSTAL and its default parameters. Dispersion modelling with AUSTAL

Time in mode: the duration of each LTO mode of a movement. Methods

docs.title: V
docs.text: Vertical limit: a field of the study setup and of the calculation settings that the plugin does not use; the LTO ceiling of each hour is the meteo mixing height, or 914.4 m when there is none. LTO ceiling

docs.title: Z
docs.text: z0: roughness length of the land cover, in m See Site parameters.

docs.title: AUSTAL installation
docs.text:
This page explains how to install AUSTAL for use with OpenALAQS and which files of this folder to copy into the AUSTAL installation. It is for users who want to run dispersion from the plugin. How to prepare, run and view a dispersion run is in Dispersion modelling with AUSTAL.

AUSTAL is a dispersion model and the reference implementation of Annex 2 of the German Technical Instructions on Air Quality Control (TA Luft). The German Environment Agency (UBA) publishes it free of charge under the GNU Public Licence.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Open the AUSTAL download page of the UBA.
  2. Download the base package for your operating system. The plugin's help names the AUSTAL 3.3.0 packages:
  3. Windows: AUSTAL_3.3.0_Windows.zip
  4. Linux: AUSTAL_3.3.0_Linux.zip
  5. Extract the package to a folder of your choice.
  6. Replace austal.settings in that folder with the copy in this folder (see Configuration files).
  7. If the English language files are not in the AUSTAL folder, copy them from this folder.
  8. In QGIS, open Calculate Dispersion and select austal.exe (Windows) or austal (Linux) in section 1, AUSTAL Executable. The plugin remembers the path. See Calculate Dispersion dialog.

The AUSTAL Help button in that section repeats these steps and links to the files of this folder on GitHub, since the plugin package does not contain them.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text: File Purpose What to do austal.settings AUSTAL's system and substance settings, with the sections OpenALAQS needs added Replace the file of the AUSTAL folder with this copy AST_en@latin1.nls English assistant messages Copy into the AUSTAL folder if missing DIA_en@latin1.nls English diagnostic messages Copy into the AUSTAL folder if missing

docs.title: austal.settings
docs.text:
austal.settings contains:

  • [.system]: deposition parameters of the five aerosol groups;
  • [.astl]: the standard substance properties (units, concentration factor, reference values, deposition settings), the NO to NO2 conversion times and the odour threshold;
  • one section per substance ([SO2], [NOX], [NO2], [PM], [ODOR], ...) with its units, assessment values and, where relevant, deposition and washout parameters.

The OpenALAQS copy adds four substances that OpenALAQS writes to AUSTAL and that are not among AUSTAL's standard substances: [SOX], [HC], [CO2] and [CO]. They are gaseous (aerosol group 0) passive tracers with no deposition or washout, reported in µg/m³ (CO2 in mg/m³). Without them, AUSTAL cannot handle these pollutants.

The file does not hold the grid, meteorology, receptors or sources of a run. OpenALAQS writes those for each run; see AUSTAL input files.

docs.title: Language files
docs.text: AST_en@latin1.nls and DIA_en@latin1.nls make AUSTAL write its messages in English (Latin-1 / ISO-8859-1 encoding). They are part of the separate AUSTAL language pack ("Sprachpakete DE/EN, UTF-8/ISO-8859-1") on the same UBA page. The copies in this folder save that download.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Dispersion modelling with AUSTAL
  • AUSTAL documentation (UBA)
  • Janicke Consulting, the developers of AUSTAL

docs.title: Aircraft profile catalogue: provenance (ANP v2.2)
docs.text: This document records where the rows of open_alaqs/database/data/default_aircraft_profiles.csv and the default profile columns of open_alaqs/database/data/default_aircraft.csv come from, what was corrected against the 5.3.5 tables, and how to reproduce it.

docs.title: 1. Sources
docs.text:
• ANP database v2.2 (EUROCONTROL, release of 22 February 2018): aircraft, default weights, fixed-point profiles, procedural steps, engine coefficients and the substitution workbook "ANP v2.2 Aircraft substitutions - jets & heavy props (22022018)". No other ANP release is used.
  • ECAC Doc 29, 5th edition, Volume 2, Appendix B: the performance model behind the procedural profiles (used here to check the table, not to recompute it).
  • The 5.3.5 tables (git revision c8a55cd), and the history of the profile CSV, in particular the version before commit ab42da5 (2024-09-26).

The table carries no build tool from before 2026. Its x, z and TAS were produced from ANP v2.2 at ISA, sea level, 15 °C, no wind, with an implementation of Doc 29 Appendix B, as these checks show:

Check Result Fixed-point profiles: x, z, TAS and power against Default_fixed_point_profiles.csv (ft x 0.3048, kt x 0.514444, power = setting / static thrust) 76 profiles exact (to 1e-6); 757300-A-1 exact against the pre-ab42da5 table Jet departures: brake-release power against (E + 15 H) / static thrust 382 of 524 within 0.001, 95% within 0.005 Lift-off TAS against C·√W (take-off flap, stage weight, sea level) 311 of 322 within 1 kt Departure thrust at every point against eq. B-9 (jets) and B-12 (propellers), ISA 114 aircraft, 5,240 points: median ratio 1.0001 (TO), 0.9997 (CL); every aircraft within 1% except ECLIPSE500 (0.982) 7378MAX and A350-941 procedures departures follow ICAO_A; A350-941-A-1 follows DEFAULT1 Stage M stored as -D-0 (7373B2, 737400, 737500, 7378MAX, A350-941) Departure weights equal the v2.2 stage weight (lb x 0.453592) wherever present Arrival weights equal the v2.2 stage-1 departure weight (134 of 134 arrivals that had one)

The geometry is therefore kept as it is; the corrections are only those listed in section 2.

docs.title: 2. Corrections to the 5.3.5 tables
docs.text:
1. Type profiles restored. Commit ab42da5 created the 48 group profiles (JET-*, PISTON-*, TURBOPROP-*) by renaming type profiles. The table before that commit holds each source with identical rows. The 47 type IDs that disappeared (including every profile of GIIB, HS748A and PA30) are restored as copies of their group, placed just before it. The two A330 arrivals: JET-LARGE-A-1 = A330-343-A-1, JET-MEDIUM-A-1 = A330-301-A-1. The full list is GROUP_SOURCE in the builder.
  2. 757300-A-1 restored. Commit e9b087b renamed its first 27 rows, so it started at 50 ft. It is rebuilt from the v2.2 fixed points (31 points), identical to the pre-ab42da5 rows.
  3. CNA206-D-1. In ANP v2.2 the CNA206 DEFAULT fixed-point departure, labelled stage 1, is point for point the 3600LB departure (stage 3, 3,600 lb, = CNA206-D-3), while the stage-1 weight is 3,000 lb. The old row set was the DEFAULT profile. It is rebuilt from 3000LB, as CNA20T-D-1 already was.
  4. Power (power = corrected net thrust / max sea-level static thrust):
  5. CNT (% of Max Static Thrust) aircraft (17): the stored value was the percentage divided by the static thrust. It is multiplied by static thrust / 100. Checks: the departures then match eq. B-12 (median ratio 0.997), and the approach decelerate points equal the ANP Start Thrust / 100 for all 17 aircraft.
  6. RPM aircraft (CNA206, CNA20T, PA28, PA31): the stored value was RPM / static thrust. Power is left empty. The plugin then uses the by-mode emission index for those segments (BFFM2 trajectory) and does not read power otherwise.
  7. Values above 1.0 are capped at 1.0 (196 points in 110 profiles; the largest were propeller thrust at low speed, up to 1.51 for DHC830, and 777300 at brake release, 1.14). Before, BFFM2 trajectory mode rejected the 23 profiles with values above 1.05 and fell back to the mode-anchor emission index.
  8. Weights filled where empty (73 profiles), with the v2.2 stage weight for departures (M for -D-0) and the stage-1 weight for arrivals.
  9. Groups. Every group keeps its ID and is a copy of its source after the corrections above. Three groups had a source of another propulsion class and now copy a same-class profile: PISTON-D-1 = CNA172-D-1 (was ECLIPSE500, a jet), PISTON-D-2 = PA31-D-1 (was CNA208, a turboprop; PA31 is an RPM aircraft, so this group has no power), TURBOPROP-D-4 = EMB120-D-1 (was IA1125, a jet).
  10. Type defaults (default_aircraft.csv, columns departure_profile, arrival_profile). Before, every type pointed to a group. Now:
  11. (a) 184 types in the substitution workbook ("by ICAO code" tab): the ANP_PROXY. For the 21 codes with variants, the variant that matches the type's default engine when the engine identifies one, otherwise the first row (VARIANT_CHOICE in the builder gives the basis per code).
  12. (b) 474 other types with an MTOW, a fixed-wing class (first letter L, A or S) and propulsion J, T or P: the ANP v2.2 aircraft with the same engine type and engine count (the engine_count column; VC10 has 4 there and 2 in its class string) and the nearest MTOW.

  13. (c) 1,261 types keep their group: 1,252 have no MTOW, the rest have no same-class ANP aircraft (single-engine jets, a three-engine piston) or are not fixed-wing. Departures use stage 1 (<proxy>-D-1), arrivals <proxy>-A-1. Engines are not changed. The mapping, with rule and basis per type, is tools/anp22_profiles/output/default_aircraft_mapping.csv.

  14. ANP 2.1 profiles removed. COMJET, DHC-2FLT and GASEPF (13 profiles, 137 rows, course = ANP2.1) are not ANP v2.2 aircraft. No type defaulted to them, no committed .alaqs used them outside the profile table, and they had no weight and no power. Existing studies keep their own copy of the table; in a new study, a movement that names one of them gets the aircraft's default profile, with a warning.

Unchanged: all modes (except in the rebuilt CNA206-D-1, which keeps the old mode sequence), course (ANP2.2, now on every row), and every other profile ID that existed before.

docs.title: 3. Effect
docs.text:
• Profiles: 797 to 831 IDs, 8,806 to 9,218 rows (47 IDs restored, 13 ANP 2.1 IDs removed). The x, z, TAS and mode of every profile that existed are unchanged, except 757300-A-1, CNA206-D-1, PISTON-D-1, PISTON-D-2 and TURBOPROP-D-4.
  • PISTON-D-1 (in the 5.3.5 tables the default for most light aircraft) climbed like a jet: 94 s below 914 m. As CNA172 it takes 300 s.
  • Movements without a profile_id now get a type-specific profile for 658 types (rules a and b), e.g. B738 737800-D-1 instead of JET-SMALL-D-4 (A321-232 stage 1), C172 CNA172-D-1 instead of PISTON-D-1.
  • 196 types default to an RPM aircraft (PA28, CNA206, PA31), so their segments have no power and BFFM2 trajectory mode uses the by-mode emission index there, with a warning per segment.

docs.title: 4. Reproducing
docs.text:
python3 tools/anp22_profiles/build_anp22_profiles.py --anp-dir /path/to/anp_v2_2
python3 tools/test_fixtures/regenerate_default_aircraft_profiles.py
python3 tools/test_fixtures/regenerate_default_aircraft.py

The builder reads the 5.3.5 tables from git revision c8a55cd (md5 c15a3e26... and ad1c2604..., checked) and the ANP v2.2 tables from --anp-dir. The ANP tables are not in the repository. Output md5 for the inputs above: profiles 16160d7c..., aircraft 4e36bcc1.... Checks that need only the committed CSVs are in tests/test_default_aircraft_profiles_anp22.py.

The fixture scripts update the .alaqs files listed in them: ten for the profiles (including the three standalone validation databases openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3*.alaqs), seven for default_aircraft. They keep study-specific rows (CUSTOM ADS-B profiles, HELIPROF rows, extra types) and drop the removed ANP 2.1 profiles. The ANP and AIRPORT_A fixtures have their own default_aircraft (other engines and names), so only their profile tables are updated. The standalone validation databases get the profile table only.

docs.title: 5. Use of ANP data
docs.text: ANP v2.2 may be used for these profiles; ANP v2.3 may not. Nothing in the catalogue, the builder or its inputs comes from ANP v2.3, and tests/test_default_aircraft_profiles_anp22.py fails if an aircraft that exists only in later releases appears.

docs.title: 6. Open points
docs.text: • Modes of fixed-point departures are kept as they were (e.g. 777300-D-1 switches to CL at 1,565 ft, before its thrust cutback).

docs.title: Code structure and calculation flow
docs.text: This page is for maintainers. It maps the aircraft emission methods described in AIRCRAFT_EMISSIONS.md to the files and functions of the plugin, and says what to change to add a helicopter category. The method itself (equations, options, limitations) is documented there, not here.

docs.title: Files of the aircraft emission calculation
docs.text: File Role core/tools/bffm2.py BFFM2 formula: ambient corrections, log-log interpolation, CO/HC slope-to-mean-value rule, installation corrections (calculate_emission_index) core/tools/twin_quadratic_fit_method.py power setting to reference fuel flow by the twin-quadratic fit core/tools/meem_v1.py MEEM V1 nvPM index, MEEM V1 method (ICAO CAEP/13-MDG): mode value at or below 3000 ft; above, ISA + ΔT (or the segment's local T and p when passed), P3/T3, ground-reference thrust, linear interpolation and the (P3/P3_GR)^1.35 φ^2.5 correction; checked against reference cases by tests/test_meem_v1.py core/tools/meem_v2.py MEEM V2, implemented, not used core/tools/fuel_sulphur.py SOx index by fuel type core/tools/nox_correction_ambient.py ICCAIA NOx correction (bymode option) core/tools/surface_layer_atmosphere.py ambient conditions aloft (atmosphere models) core/tools/ads_b.py ADS-B file validation and import into default_aircraft_profiles (CUSTOM profiles) core/tools/runway_placement.py placement of the profiles on the runway, split of the taxi time core/interfaces/Engine.py (EngineEmissionIndex) steps 1 to 5 of BFFM2: twin-quadratic call, δ√θ scaling, cache, call to bffm2.py; getEmissionIndexByModeWithMEEM() applies MEEM V1 (_meem_v1) core/MovementEmissionCalculator.py (FlightEmissionCalculator) segment loop: reads profile points, computes Mach, chooses the fuel flow, calls _get_emission_index_bffm2, computes t_seg, calls Emission.add(); ICCAIA NOx correction (_apply_nox_corrections, modes in NOX_CORRECTION_MODES); local ambient per height (local_ambient_conditions, _LocalAmbient) core/MovementEmissionCalculator.py (module level) _meem_ambient(method_config, T_amb, p_amb): the local ambient passed to MEEM V1 core/MovementEmissionCalculator.py (TaxiingEmissionCalculator) taxi loop: taxi index (bymode TX with MEEM, or BFFM2 getEmissionIndexByEngineState() with PM, SOx and P1/P2 from the TX mode index; no index: no taxi emissions), APU (_apply_apu_emissions), single-engine taxi and engine start (_apply_single_engine_taxiing_emissions*, _do_apply_single_engine_taxiing_emissions, _apply_start_engine_emissions; gate_emissions_code 0 drops all start emissions), queuing, stop-and-go (AVERAGE_DURATION_OF_STOP_AND_GOS_IN_S), brake wear core/MovementEmissionCalculator.py (GateEmissionCalculator) GSE and GPU at the gate; _get_aircraft_group_match picks the gate profile group (exact, else difflib.get_close_matches, else none: no GSE or GPU, logged at debug level only; intended for PROPELLER) core/GeoTransformation.py (TrajectoryTransformer.runway_alignment) places ANP and CUSTOM profile points on the runway core/modules/MovementSourceModule.py process() sets max_height from ambient_conditions.getMixingHeight() (the vertical_limit_m fallback under except AttributeError is not reached, because getAmbientCondition always returns an AmbientCondition), builds the calc_method dict and creates the calculators core/EmissionCalculatorService.py passes method, meem_version, bffm2_ff_source to the source modules core/EmissionCalculation.py getAmbientCondition: meteo row nearest in time for each period; AmbientCondition() (ISA, mixing height 914.4 m) when the meteo table is empty core/interfaces/AmbientCondition.py meteo row values with their defaults (empty MixingHeight: 914.4 m)

docs.title: BFFM2 calculation flow
docs.text:
User clicks "Calculate" (BFFM2 selected)
    │
    ▼
EmissionCalculatorService.calculate_emissions()
    passes method = 'BFFM2', meem_version, bffm2_ff_source to the source modules
    │
    ▼
MovementSourceModule.process()
    builds calc_method = {
        'name': 'BFFM2',
        'config': {
            'ambient_conditions': AmbientCondition(...),
            'apply_nox_corrections': False,
            'bffm2_ff_source': 'trajectory',  # or 'mode_anchor'
            ...
        }
    }
    ├── TaxiingEmissionCalculator  (BFFM2 gas-phase FF; PM/SOx/P1/P2 from mode EI; APU added on taxi segments)
    ├── GateEmissionCalculator     (GSE and GPU)
    └── FlightEmissionCalculator
            │
            ▼
            for each (start_point_, end_point_) in trajectory.getPointPairs():
                │
                ├── Mach = TAS / SOS
                ├── method['config'].update({'mach_number': Mach})
                │
                ├── engine_thrust = start_point_.getEngineThrust()
                ├── fuel_flow     = start_point_.getFuelFlow()        # from fuel_flow_kgm
                │
                ├── if no engine_thrust and no fuel_flow:
                │       bymode EI for the segment (warning)
                │
                ├── if bffm2_ff_source == 'mode_anchor':
                │       use mode-anchor FF  →  getEmissionIndexByFuelFlow()
                ├── elif fuel_flow > 0:
                │       ff_per_engine = fuel_flow / n_engines
                │       if ff_per_engine ≤ 1.5 × Wf_TO (ADSB_FF_CEILING_FACTOR):
                │           use ff_per_engine directly  →  getEmissionIndexByFuelFlow()
                │       else:
                │           use mode-anchor FF (summary warning per movement)
                │
                ├── getEmissionIndexByEngineState(engine_thrust, fuel_flow)
                │       ├── Wf_ref  = twin_quad(engine_thrust, EEDB)
                │       ├── Wf_amb  = Wf_ref × δ × √θ
                │       └── getEmissionIndexByFuelFlow(Wf_amb)
                │               └── calculate_emission_index(pollutant, Wf_amb, EEDB, ambient)
                │                       ├── install corrections → shift EEDB breakpoints
                │                       ├── Wf_ref_BFFM2 = Wf_amb/δ × θ^3.8 × exp(0.2M²)
                │                       ├── log–log interpolation  →  EI_raw
                │                       └── ambient correction  →  EI_corr (NOx/CO/HC)
                │
                ├── _get_emission_index_bffm2(mode, emission_index_bffm2)
                │       ├── mode_ei = getEmissionIndexByModeWithMEEM(mode, ..., altitude MSL, TAS)
                │       │       └── MEEM V1: mode EI at or below 3000 ft; above,
                │       │               MEEM V1 → pm10_nonvol (= nvpm_g_kg),
                │       │               pm10/p1/p2 moved by the same amount, nvpm_number_kg
                │       └── inject into copy of BFFM2 result:
                │               pm10, pm10_nonvol, pm10_sul, pm10_organic,
                │               nvpm_g_kg, nvpm_number_kg (not read by Emission.add),
                │               sox, p1, p2
                │
                ├── d      = ellipsoidal_2d_distance(start_point, end_point)
                ├── t_seg  = 2 × d / (TAS_start + TAS_end)
                ├── eff_t  = t_seg × n_engines
                └── mass   = EI_corr × Wf_amb × eff_t / 1000   [kg]

The segment distance uses QgsDistanceArea.measureLine() with the ellipsoid set, so it is the geodesic ground distance whatever the CRS of the emission layer.

docs.title: Taxi flow
docs.text:
With BFFM2, TaxiingEmissionCalculator always calls Engine.getEmissionIndexByEngineState(engine_thrust_level_for_taxiing, method), which takes the power-setting branch (twin-quadratic fit, then ff_ref · δ · √θ) whatever bffm2_ff_source is. mode_anchor therefore changes only the flight segments.

Taxiing runs at Mach 0: TaxiingEmissionCalculator.calculate_emissions saves the Mach left in the shared method['config'] by the flight calculator, sets it to 0 for the taxi index, and restores it afterwards. The ground ambient (station pressure, 2 m temperature) is set with _LocalAmbient(config, 0.0) for the same block.

docs.title: Adding a helicopter category
docs.text:
If a future revision of the FOCA guidance introduces a new helicopter category (HELICOPTERS.md), three places change:

  1. The HelicopterCategory enum in core/tools/foca_heli.py.
  2. The derive_category() rule in the same file (the engine type, engine count and MTOM decision tree).
  3. A new entry in TRAJECTORY_PARAMS in core/tools/foca_heli_trajectory.py, and a matching table in HELICOPTERS.md with a source for each field.

The trajectory generator's general logic (climb to the LTO ceiling, two-segment approach, hover at both ends) is shared by all categories and needs no change unless the FOCA method itself is restructured.

docs.title: Road traffic / COPERT dataset provenance
docs.text: This document captures what is currently known and unknown about the road traffic emission factor data in OpenALAQS, the relationship between its CSV source and the embedded SQLite caches, and the procedure for a future refresh against a newer COPERT release. The intent is to make any future data maintenance easier and to be honest about gaps in the historical record.

docs.title: 1. The data file
docs.text:
Path: open_alaqs/database/data/default_vehicle_ef_copert5.csv

Rows: 46435

Schema (20 columns):

Column Type Description vehicle_category string Aggregate category: Passenger Cars, Light Commercial Vehicles, Heavy Duty Trucks, Motorcycles, Buses. fuel string Petrol or Diesel. No CNG, LPG, hybrid, PHEV, or BEV. euro_standard string Emission standard: Conventional, Euro 1...Euro 6 d (LDV); Conventional, Euro I...Euro VI D/E (HDV); various legacy classes for motorcycles. Does not include Euro 7 / Euro VII. country string 38 country aggregates. Includes EU27 and EU28 placeholders (see integrity note in §4). pollutant string CH4, CO, CO2, NH3, NOx, PM0.1, PM2.5, PM10, SO2, VOC. hot-cold-evaporation string One of: Hot, Cold, Evaporation. evaporation_split string For Evaporation rows only: Diurnal, Hot soak, Running losses. NULL for Hot and Cold rows. 10...130 float 13 columns, one per 10 km/h speed bin from 10 to 130. Units are pollutant-dependent (g/km for Hot and Cold exhaust rows; g/day-equivalent for Evaporation rows, with values speed-invariant per row).

docs.title: 2. Source COPERT version
docs.text:
Documented version: COPERT 5.4.52. Cited in the module comments of open_alaqs/core/tools/copert5_utils.py and in documents/methods/REFERENCE_DATA.md.

Source Guidebook: EMEP/EEA air pollutant emission inventory guidebook 2019, Update October 2020. Cited in the module docstring of copert5_utils.py. This is the generation of the Guidebook the bulk methodology in copert5*.py was implemented against. Specific items verified against the 2023 Update 2025 chapter are cited inline in copert5.py, copert5_utils.py, and STATIONARY_AND_ROAD.md using the uniform format EMEP/EEA Guidebook 2023 Update 2025, chapter <NFR-code>, §<section> (p.<page>).

Items not currently in the repo record:

  • The exact ingest date.
  • The provenance of the per-country aggregation: whether the values came directly from COPERT 5.4.52 software outputs run by a third party (e.g. Emisia), or whether they were derived from a separate per-country fleet composition layer applied to underlying Guidebook parameters, or some other path. The country-aggregated form of the data implies a fleet composition was applied at ingest time, but the composition itself is not stored or documented.
  • The reference temperature implicit in the Cold-cycle rows (Cold EFs in COPERT 5.9.1 are temperature-dependent via a polynomial; the 5.4.52 pre-computed values in this CSV imply a fixed reference temperature was used, but it is not recorded).

These gaps are not fixable from the data alone. A future refresh (see §5) is the right opportunity to re-record them.

docs.title: 3. Embedded SQLite caches
docs.text:
The CSV is the source of truth. Twelve tracked .alaqs files embed a copy of the table default_vehicle_ef_copert5 (all 46435 rows) and must remain consistent with the CSV:

.alaqs file Purpose open_alaqs/core/templates/project.alaqs Project template seeded into every new study. example/training/training.alaqs Training example, pre-run state. example/training/training_out.alaqs Training example, post-inventory state. tests/data/generic/generic_out.alaqs Generic regression fixture. tests/data/ANP/ANP.alaqs ANP regression fixture, pre-run. tests/data/ANP/ANP_out.alaqs ANP regression fixture, post-inventory. gse_application/tests/example_db.alaqs GSE application test fixture. tests/data/AIRPORT_A/AIRPORT_A.alaqs AIRPORT_A regression fixture, pre-run. tests/data/AIRPORT_A/AIRPORT_A_out.alaqs AIRPORT_A regression fixture, post-inventory. openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3.alaqs Standalone validation database. openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3_gatemovements.alaqs Standalone validation database. openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3_multisource.alaqs Standalone validation database.

Two .alaqs files have the table schema present but with zero rows (treated as fresh templates filled at runtime): open_alaqs/core/templates/ inventory.alaqs and scripts/emissions_austal/sample_data/Inventory.alaqs. These are left alone during data refresh.

Parity with the CSV is checked only for project.alaqs (tests/test_database.py::test_template_data) and for example/**/*_out.alaqs (tests/test_database.py::test_example_csv). After any edit to the CSV, re-sync the caches with tools/data_integrity_fixes/sync_csv_into_alaqs_caches.py, which updates the first seven files of the table above (its TARGETS list); the AIRPORT_A and standalone validation files must be updated separately.

docs.title: 4. Data integrity status
docs.text:
Four data integrity items have been investigated. Status:

# Item Status 1 Suspected Switzerland 10× PM10 error Not reproducible. Switzerland PM10 rows are bit-identical to Germany/Italy/France/Austria/EU28. Closed. 2 PM10 < PM2.5 in 639 row pairs (2505 cells) Fixed via tools/data_integrity_fixes/fix_pm10_at_least_pm25.py. PM10[speed] = max(PM10[speed], PM2.5[speed]) per violating cell, satisfying physical constraint and Guidebook §1.1 PM10=PM2.5=TSP equality for road exhaust. 3 EU27/EU28 labelling mismatch (EU27 has 1137 rows across 9 pollutants but no PM10; EU28 has 118 rows, all PM10) Open. Caused by ingestion-layer artifact at the time the EU-aggregate rows were generated. Not fixable from the existing CSV alone (the missing PM10 rows for EU27 are not derivable without source data); deferred to a future data refresh. 4 NH3 values ~10× lower than EMEP/EEA Guidebook Tier 2 references (Table 3-17) Open. PC Petrol Hot NH3 at 50 km/h reads ~1.4 mg/km vs ~10-50 mg/km in the Guidebook Tier 2. Affects all PC Petrol rows checked; broader scope not characterised. Currently inert because NH3 is not exposed in the road traffic emissions output pipeline. Deferred to a future data refresh.

Items 2 and 3 have no effect on the road traffic PM10 output: the PM10 rows of the file are not read (PM10 is not in copert5_utils.POLLUTANTS) and road PM10 is taken from the PM2.5 factor ePM2.5 (copert5.py), since the EMEP/EEA Guidebook sets PM10 = PM2.5 for road exhaust. Item 4 is inert for the reason given in the table.

docs.title: 5. Refreshing to a newer COPERT release
docs.text:
The OpenALAQS dataset is in a country-aggregated form: per-country values pre-computed at 13 speed bins (10, 20, ..., 130 km/h) with a fixed reference temperature for cold-cycle rows. Newer COPERT releases (e.g. 5.9.1, October 2025) ship their underlying methodology data as per-(category, fuel, segment, technology, Euro standard) polynomial parameters with no country dimension, plus a separate fleet composition layer applied at COPERT software runtime. A refresh therefore involves both ingesting new parameters AND choosing how to produce the country aggregate that the OpenALAQS schema expects.

The expected refresh procedure, when undertaken:

  1. Source authoritative per-country EF aggregates for the target COPERT version. The recommended path is to run the licensed COPERT software (Emisia) for each of the 38 country aggregates, with national fleet composition inputs, and export per-(category, fuel, Euro standard, speed) emission factor tables.
  2. Validate one cell against the COPERT software UI before bulk reformatting, to confirm the export format and units.
  3. Reformat the exports into the OpenALAQS CSV schema documented in §1. Map any new fuels (CNG, LPG, hybrid, PHEV, BEV) and new Euro standards (Euro 7, Euro VII) to scope by either (a) extending the schema, (b) skipping them for minimal-effort refresh, or (c) handling them in a follow-on.
  4. Replace default_vehicle_ef_copert5.csv with the new file.
  5. Run tools/data_integrity_fixes/sync_csv_into_alaqs_caches.py to propagate the new data into the embedded .alaqs caches (the script covers seven of the twelve; update the other five as well).
  6. Re-run tests/test_copert5.py and tests/test_database.py; update expected values in the former where appropriate (numerical regressions will need new pinned values with documenting comments).
  7. Re-verify the four data integrity items above against the new dataset. PM10 < PM2.5 and Switzerland 10× should not recur in well-formed COPERT 5.9.1 data (Appendix 4 uses a single "PM Exhaust" label). EU27/EU28 labelling and NH3 magnitude should be checked explicitly.
  8. Update this document with the new version's provenance facts (exact COPERT version, ingest date, fleet composition source).

docs.title: 6. Guidebook citations in the code
docs.text: The original Tier 3 implementation (copert5_utils.py) cites the EMEP/EEA Guidebook 2019 (Update Oct. 2020) and its table numbers. Later design decisions are cited with chapter, section and page of the 2023 edition, in the format EMEP/EEA Guidebook 2023 Update 2025, chapter <NFR-code>, §<section> (p.<page>), with verbatim quotes where the decision turns on exact wording. When the next Guidebook update is published, re-check each cited reference in copert5.py, copert5_utils.py and STATIONARY_AND_ROAD.md, starting with its known limitations.

docs.title: 7. Out of scope for this document
docs.text: Other vehicle / aircraft / GSE emission factor datasets in open_alaqs/database/data/ (default_aircraft_engine_ei.csv, default_aircraft_apu_ef.csv, default_aircraft_start_ef.csv, default_helicopter.csv, default_helicopter_engines.csv, default_gate_profiles.csv, default_stationary_*.csv) are separately maintained and are not part of the COPERT road traffic data. See DEPRECATIONS.md for aircraft engine EI column-level deprecations.

docs.title: Database schema deprecations
docs.text: This document tracks fields in database/data/*.csv that are retained for compatibility but are unused at runtime. They are scheduled for removal in a future schema-v2 migration.

docs.title: default_aircraft_engine_ei.csv: 12 of 37 columns deprecated
docs.text:
Columns dead at emissions-calculation runtime (populated by migration scripts, never read by the calculation engine), except fuel_type, which selects the SOx default (see the table):

Column Reason Kept for coolant Pass-through in Engine.py, never consumed Round-trip to user exports combustion_technology Pass-through only Round-trip to user exports technology_age Pass-through only Round-trip to user exports eng_type Only read by update_default_aircraft_engine_ei_csv.py migration Migration tooling bpr (bypass ratio) Only read by migration script Migration tooling remark Only written by migration scripts Manual annotation smoke_number Stored in default-dict, never read ICAO EEDB contract smoke_number_maximum Stored, never read ICAO EEDB contract status Zero runtime references Unused engine_name_type Populated by migration, never read Migration tooling fuel_type Read: selects the SOx default (AvGas or jet fuel) when sox_ei is 0 or empty (Engine.py, fuel_sulphur.sox_ei_g_kg); the shipped CSV has sox_ei set in every row SOx default for user tables without sox_ei manufacturer Engine table pass-through; the aircraft-table version is what's actually used Duplicate of aircraft-table field

Impact: 11 of 37 columns unread, plus fuel_type read only for the SOx default. Removing the 12 shrinks the CSV by ~7% (about 13% with nvpm_ei) and eliminates per-row setObject overhead.

docs.title: Additional finding: nvpm_ei redundancy
docs.text:
nvpm_ei is the 13th underutilised column but sits in a different category: not deprecated, just redundant.

  • nvpm_ei and pm10_nonvol are numerically identical in EEDB (both are the non-volatile PM mass emission index, in g/kg).
  • 3692 of 3692 rows in ANP_out.alaqs have non-null nvpm_ei.
  • nvpm_ei is declared in the schema dict, marked DEPRECATED (column list of EngineEmissionIndicesDatabase.__init__ in EngineDatabases.py), but no calculation reads it.
  • But production code reads the non-volatile PM mass EI via ei_.getObject("nvpm_g_kg"), and the key_mapping in Engine.py (EngineEmissionIndex) remaps nvpm_g_kg to the DB column pm10_nonvol. So the MEEM V1/V2 call path (Engine._meem_v1) gets the right value via pm10_nonvol.

Conclusion: no runtime impact today. The column is a CSV-export convenience and an ICAO EEDB round-trip convenience. When schema v2 lands, the choice is either drop nvpm_ei and keep pm10_nonvol as the single source of truth, or drop pm10_nonvol and keep nvpm_ei (matches ICAO EEDB 2021+ nomenclature). Current recommendation: drop pm10_nonvol and keep nvpm_ei to align with ICAO EEDB, but this is a naming choice that doesn't affect any calculation.

Migration plan: 1. schema-v1 (current): mark deprecated in EngineDatabases.py, document here. 2. schema-v2 (future release): - Drop columns from EngineDatabases.py schema dict: * all 12 deprecated columns and nvpm_ei (annotated DEPRECATED in the current schema, column list of EngineEmissionIndicesDatabase.__init__) - Regenerate default_aircraft_engine_ei.csv without these 13 fields (24 cols remaining). - Resolve the nvpm_ei vs pm10_nonvol redundancy (see the nvpm_ei finding above). Recommended: keep nvpm_ei, drop pm10_nonvol, update the Engine.py key_mapping from "nvpm_g_kg": "pm10_nonvol" to "nvpm_g_kg": "nvpm_ei". - Add a one-shot .alaqs file migration that rewrites the default_aircraft_engine_ei table in-place when an old-schema file is opened. SQLite doesn't support ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN before 3.35, so the migration must be CREATE TABLE tmp; INSERT ... SELECT <new cols>; DROP old; RENAME tmp. - Version-stamp the output files so downstream tools can detect schema. Proposed: write PRAGMA user_version = 2 on migrated files. - Update the 14 tracked .alaqs files that carry the table similarly. Regenerate any reference outputs whose numeric values shift (none expected with the shipped data: the dropped columns are runtime-dead except fuel_type, whose SOx default is not used where sox_ei is set).

Schema v2 entry points (for the future implementer): - Touch points in Python: EngineDatabases.py (schema dict), Engine.py (key_mapping if the nvpm rename is adopted, and the pass-through of coolant/combustion_technology/technology_age next to it). - Touch points in data: database/data/default_aircraft_engine_ei.csv, the 14 tracked .alaqs files that carry the table, possibly the open_alaqs/core/templates/inventory.alaqs generated by tools/template_build/generate_templates.py. - Touch points in docs: this file.

Why defer: - No runtime impact from current state (verified). The 12 deprecated columns are unread, read only by migration scripts, or (fuel_type) read only for the SOx default when sox_ei is 0 or empty; nvpm_ei data flows through pm10_nonvol via Engine.py key_mapping. - Schema v2 is a breaking change for external tools that consume .alaqs files. Shipping it should be coordinated with a release that already introduces other breaking changes, to avoid forward-compat churn for no immediate benefit.

docs.title: Related schema notes
docs.text:
• The CSVs in database/data/ are the source of truth, populated externally and shipped with the code; the repository has no pipeline to regenerate them.
  • The table default_helicopter_engine_ei is not part of the schema. Helicopters use default_helicopter and default_helicopter_engines with the FOCA 2015 LTO computation (open_alaqs/core/tools/foca_heli.py). For a study that still has the old table, pass --drop-extra-tables to scripts/migrate_alaqs.py to drop it, and --refresh-reference-data --refresh-include-user-extensible (or --refresh-tables default_helicopter,default_helicopter_engines) to fill the new tables from the CSVs. Without the refresh, Phase 1 creates them empty (scripts/migrate_alaqs.py: Phase 1 in the module docstring, USER_EXTENSIBLE_REFRESH_TABLES).

docs.title: Known regression patterns
docs.text:
For maintainers: the failure modes seen in earlier builds, with their symptom, root cause and the code to check. Read this when a validation of VALIDATION_GUIDE.md fails; these patterns cover most of the failures observed so far.

Contents:

  • 1. AUSTAL writer aborts mid-run with "Grid source NN not available"
  • 2. Aircraft has no attribute getStartEmissions
  • 3. default_aircraft.csv containing duplicate helicopter rows
  • 4. APU silent-zero emissions
  • 5. Standalone fails on an old inventory
  • 6. Other easy-to-regress fixes
  • 7. recipe_config.json parameter coverage

docs.title: 1. AUSTAL writer aborts mid-run with "Grid source NN not available"
docs.text:
Symptom: austal.exe aborts with 

*** Grid source "02" not available! (TalSrc.SrcCrtPtl.14)
typically at the second hour of the run.

Root cause: per-source rate transitions to exactly 0.000e+00 mid-run. AUSTAL refuses to instantiate the next-hour grid source for that slot.

Where to look: core/modules/AUSTALOutputModule.py, which must: - Floor every per-source rate at 1.0e-30 instead of 0.0 in the series.dmna writer. - Back-fill zero-mass hours with phantom single-cell Eq weight = 1.0 and reset self._start_time / self._end_time from _first_start_time + timedelta(hours=time_id ± 1) per back-filled e-file (otherwise AUSTAL rejects *** File "...e0001.dmna" [...] not valid at 00:00:00!). - Re-encode WindDirection == 0 with WindSpeed > 0 to the AUSTAL "missing" sentinel 999 to suppress the "Datenzeilen mit Windrichtung gleich 0 und Windgeschwindigkeit groesser 0" warning.

If a build aborts this way, check that all three are present in AUSTALOutputModule.py.

docs.title: 2. Aircraft has no attribute getStartEmissions
docs.text:
Symptom: plugin emission calculation crashes with 

AttributeError: 'Aircraft' object has no attribute 'getStartEmissions'.
Did you mean: 'getApuEmissions'?
in TaxiingEmissionCalculator.__init__ (MovementEmissionCalculator.py), where it reads self._aircraft.getStartEmissions().

Root cause: MovementEmissionCalculator.py calls self._aircraft.getStartEmissions() (aircraft-keyed start emissions, correct), but the Aircraft interface class is missing the getStartEmissions() method. Start emissions belong on Aircraft, not Engine, because an Engine instance can be shared across aircraft in different groups.

Where to look: core/interfaces/Aircraft.py must expose def getStartEmissions(self). The call in MovementEmissionCalculator.py and the method on Aircraft are paired: do not change one without the other.

docs.title: 3. default_aircraft.csv containing duplicate helicopter rows
docs.text:
Symptom: the plugin's helicopter feature emits zero (or duplicate) emissions; default_aircraft.csv has more rows than the expected 1919.

Root cause: helicopters live in default_helicopter.csv (60 rows, with variants per type), not in default_aircraft.csv. A default_aircraft.csv taken from an older source still carries the 61 helicopter rows (1980 rows in all), leaving duplicates across the two tables; it also lacks the APU backfills (pattern 4).

Where to look: the row count and the helicopter types of default_aircraft.csv; ship the file of this repository unchanged.

docs.title: 4. APU silent-zero emissions
docs.text:
Symptom: aircraft of certain ICAO types produce zero APU emissions even when apu_code = 1 (APU active) in the movement record.

Root cause: default_aircraft.apu_id IS NULL for that ICAO. The APU-emission lookup JOIN default_aircraft_apu_ef ON apu_id returns zero rows; no error is raised; emissions silently drop to zero.

Important: NULL apu_id has two meanings: (a) "the aircraft has no APU at all" - correct as zero (most Cessna Citation light jets, most King Air turboprops, PC-24, ATR family). (b) "we don't know the APU model" - INCORRECT as zero.

The apu_id values come from per-ICAO research (CHANGELOG.md [5.2.0] lists the ICAOs that received one). Do not backfill a group default ("most-common APU per ac_group"): it conflates the two meanings.

Current state: - Tier 1 (bulk per-ac_group rule): 6 ICAOs correctly NULL; 2 (CRJ9, LJ45) have a standard APU but the model is missing from default_aircraft_apu_ef. Both stay NULL pending an EF table extension. - Tier 2 (91 ICAOs reviewed): 7 backfilled (H25B, H25C, HA4T, BCS1, BCS3, B731, B74D). 23 future-EF (have APU, model not in EF table). 61 correctly NULL.

The shipped default_aircraft.csv has 162 of 1919 rows (8.4%) with populated apu_id and 1757 (91.6%) NULL. The NULL count should reduce further as the future-EF list is closed out.

docs.title: 5. Standalone fails on an old inventory
docs.text:
Symptom: python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft training_out.alaqs fails with 

OperationalError: no such table: default_helicopter

Root cause: openalaqs_standalone/movements.py queries default_helicopter to decide whether each movement is fixed-wing or helicopter. Inventories made by plugin versions before 5.2.0 (the FOCA 2015 helicopter release) have no default_helicopter table.

Where to look: movements.get_helicopter() and movements.get_helicopter_engine_type() check _table_exists(conn, ...) first and return None when the helicopter tables are absent, so every aircraft of such a study is treated as fixed-wing (which is correct). Any new query of the standalone on a table added by a later plugin version needs the same guard.

docs.title: 6. Other easy-to-regress fixes
docs.text:
If a build loses one of these, the symptom in the last column shows up:

Fix File Symptom if reverted COPERT 5 parking distance m → km core/tools/copert5.py All parking COPERT 5 emissions ~1000x too high ADS-B z_m <= 0 for mode classification core/tools/ads_b.py Sub-MSL airports (e.g. EHRD at -15 ft, -5 m) misclassify TO as CL (ground points are snapped to height 0 by _snap_ground_heights before the z_m <= 0 test) BFFM2 1.05 power-setting tolerance clamp core/tools/twin_quadratic_fit_method.py Small floating-point overshoots abort the whole movement BFFM2 ValueError fallback to mode-anchor EI core/MovementEmissionCalculator.py BFFM2 failures abort the study instead of degrading Geodetic length for MultiLineString core/tools/spatial.py Mass silently dropped for clipped polylines re-entering the same cell Empty tbl_InvMeteo warning core/EmissionCalculation.py BFFM2 silently uses ISA when meteo table is empty

docs.title: 7. recipe_config.json parameter coverage
docs.text:
The Dataiku recipe parses recipe_config.json via its _resolve_config(...) (in the recipe file openalaqs_standalone_recipe.txt of the Dataiku update package, not in this repository). A parameter that exists in the CLI but is not in _resolve_config will be silently ignored when set via the JSON (for example apply_nox_corrections accepted by the CLI but not read from the JSON). The recipe must handle all 26 keys documented in example/training/recipe_config.example.json (besides the _-prefixed comment entries; the recipe is not in this repository, so this cannot be checked here); a new CLI flag requires a matching entry in _resolve_config's return dict and a matching kwarg in the orchestrate() call site.

See also:

  • VALIDATION_GUIDE.md: validations V1 to V5, tolerances and failure triage
  • CAEP14_VALIDATION.md: the CAEP14 reference implementation
  • DEPRECATIONS.md: deprecated data and code paths

docs.title: Atmosphere aloft: validation evidence
docs.text: This page holds the checks behind the atmosphere models of ATMOSPHERE_ALOFT.md: the comparison with the De Bilt radiosondes and the validation of the code. It is for maintainers and reviewers; the models, their inputs and limitations are described on the methods page.

docs.title: Check against the De Bilt radiosondes (2025)
docs.text:
Method:

  1. Data. De Bilt (WMO 06260, IGRA2 station NLM00006260, the Netherlands) from the NOAA NCEI IGRA2 archive: 450 soundings of 2025 with a surface level and data above 1 km; 354 at 00 UTC, 88 at 12 UTC.
  2. Heights. Computed hypsometrically from pressure, temperature and dew-point depression. Checked against the geopotential heights reported at 925 and 850 hPa: mean −0.8 m, sd 2.4 m, at most 6 m.
  3. Observed values. T(z) − T(surface) at 100, 300, 600 and 900 m, interpolated between significant levels. WMO significant levels are chosen so that linear interpolation stays within about 1 K.
  4. Model. Each model driven by the hourly meteo row (converted from METAR) of an airport about 50 km from De Bilt, for the same UTC hour, with site parameters z0 0.3 m, d0 1.2 m, ha 11.2 m (not the current defaults of 0.1 / 0.6 / 10.6 m). The airport's 2 m temperature is on average 0.4 K warmer than De Bilt's surface (sd 1.6 K). The comparison uses differences from each site's own surface.
  5. Scripts. The check scripts are not part of the repository; the soundings are public (IGRA2).

Results within the emission ceiling (bias / RMS in K, model minus observed):

Height n standard_lapse surface_layer ground row held 100 m 450 −1.3 / 2.9 −1.5 / 2.8 −0.7 / 2.6 300 m 206 +0.3 / 1.4 −1.2 / 1.7 +2.3 / 2.7 600 m 67 +1.9 / 2.6 −1.9 / 2.6 +5.8 / 6.1 900 m 34 +2.0 / 3.1 −2.7 / 3.5 +7.8 / 8.2

By time of day (within the ceiling):

Time Height n standard_lapse surface_layer ground row held 00 UTC 100 m 354 −1.9 / 3.2 −1.7 / 3.0 −1.3 / 2.8 00 UTC 300 m 113 −0.5 / 1.2 −1.3 / 1.7 +1.4 / 1.8 12 UTC 100 m 88 +0.9 / 1.1 −1.0 / 1.5 +1.5 / 1.6 12 UTC 300 m 88 +1.4 / 1.7 −1.1 / 1.6 +3.4 / 3.5 12 UTC 600 m 65 +1.9 / 2.6 −1.9 / 2.6 +5.8 / 6.1 12 UTC 900 m 33 +2.0 / 3.2 −2.8 / 3.5 +7.9 / 8.2

By season (within the ceiling, RMS in K; n in brackets). The all-year result does not hold in summer:

Season 100 m: standard_lapse / surface_layer 300 m 600 m 900 m Winter (DJF) 1.9 / 1.8 (110) 1.3 / 1.8 (64) 2.1 / 3.6 (10) 1.5 / 2.0 (1) Spring (MAM) 3.8 / 3.7 (115) 1.7 / 1.4 (37) 2.7 / 2.1 (22) 3.0 / 3.8 (16) Summer (JJA) 3.0 / 2.9 (113) 1.7 / 1.6 (44) 3.0 / 1.9 (21) 3.6 / 2.3 (11) Autumn (SON) 2.4 / 2.3 (112) 1.3 / 1.7 (61) 1.9 / 3.1 (14) 2.4 / 4.5 (6) July and August only 2.9 / 2.8 (76) 1.7 / 1.5 (27) 3.0 / 1.5 (15) 3.8 / 1.6 (8)

In summer, and above all at 600 and 900 m in daytime convective hours, the AUSTAL profile is closer to the soundings (surface_layer closer in 81 to 93 % of those cases). The ISA lapse is then about 3 K too warm, because the convective layer follows the dry adiabat. In winter and autumn the ISA lapse is closer. The summer advantage rests on few soundings above 300 m (8 to 21); in fuel-flow terms it is worth at most 0.2 percentage points of RMS.

Fuel-flow factor δ√θ at height relative to the ground, model against observed, RMS within the ceiling:

Height standard_lapse surface_layer ground row held 100 m 0.5 % 0.5 % 1.2 % 300 m 0.3 % 0.3 % 4.1 % 600 m 0.5 % 0.5 % 8.5 % 900 m 0.6 % 0.7 % 12.9 %

Reading:

  • The main effect is confirmed. It is the pressure drop with height, from the station pressure and hydrostatics: the ground row held is off by 1 to 13 % in the fuel-flow factor.
  • The temperature shape is a second-order matter for fuel.
  • The AUSTAL profile is systematically too cold over the year.
  • The ISA lapse is too warm by day, when the convective layer is near the dry adiabat, and too cold near the ground at night (inversions).
  • Their all-year RMS errors are similar; in summer daytime aloft the AUSTAL profile is better, in winter and autumn the ISA lapse.
  • Neither meets 1.5 K RMS at 900 m over the year.
  • Choice of the default. standard_lapse was chosen on the all-year result, its smaller bias, and because it needs no stability inputs. A summer study with daytime traffic can justify surface_layer on the summer numbers above. The effect on fuel is below 0.2 points either way; on NOx it is larger (effect on BFFM2).
  • The 100 m errors are dominated by night-time surface inversions (+1.3 K observed on average at 00 UTC), which none of the models reproduces.
  • For NOx the temperature matters more. The BFFM2 ambient factor moves by about 0.6 % per K, and a bffm2_anchor take-off segment by up to 5 % per K (effect on BFFM2).

Limits of the check: - one station, about 50 km inland; - 78 % of the soundings at night, while most flights are by day; - interpolation between significant levels; - the airport's row and the De Bilt sounding describe slightly different air.

docs.title: Code validation
docs.text:
• AUSTAL C code. BlmTemp, getTheta, StdUuPrandtl and getHm, copied verbatim from AUSTAL 3.3.0 TalBlm.c and compiled, agree with the port to 7 × 10⁻⁵ K over 2,592 cases; that comparison harness is not in the repository. tests/test_surface_layer_atmosphere.py pins 4 of the C cases: u* to a relative 1 × 10⁻⁶ and the temperature at 4 heights each (16 values) to 2 × 10⁻⁴ K.
  • Hydrostatics. Against the analytic ISA solution: 1 × 10⁻⁸.
  • Parity. Plugin, standalone and CAEP14 reference agree to 4 × 10⁻¹¹ for every model.
  • Tests. Bounds, degenerate inputs and plumbing: tests/test_atmosphere_review_541.py.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: • Bounded hours from METAR meteo. scripts/metar_to_alaqs_meteo.py assigns the Obukhov length per Pasquill-Gifford class, independent of the wind, so the strongest winds of each unstable class can exceed the heat-flux bound of surface_layer (heat-flux bound). This is suspected as the main source of bounded hours; it has not been checked in the converter.
