docs.title: Meteorology
docs.text:
Hourly ambient conditions for the emission calculation (BFFM2, NOx correction, mixing height) and for dispersion. You select the file in Meteorological Table of the Calculate Emissions Inventory window. The file is optional: without it, ISA conditions are used.

Delimiter: comma, semicolon or tab, detected from the file.

Header: exactly the ten headers below, written as shown, units in brackets included. A missing, extra or differently written header is rejected with "Headers of meteo csv file do not match..". "yes (column)" means the column must be there; an empty value takes the default.

Column Unit Required Meaning Default when empty Scenario yes Label of the meteo set. The calculation uses every row, whatever the label. DateTime(YYYY-mm-dd hh:mm:ss) date and time yes Start of the hour. Temperature(K) K yes (column) Air temperature at 2 m (kelvin, not °C). 288.15 Humidity(kg_water/kg_dry_air) kg/kg yes (column) Humidity ratio. Not used by the emission calculation: the humidity is derived from the relative humidity. 0.00634 RelativeHumidity(0-1) fraction yes (column) Relative humidity, 0 to 1 (not percent). 0.6 SeaLevelPressure(Pa) Pa yes (column) Sea-level pressure (QNH × 100, not hPa). 101325 WindSpeed(m/s) m/s yes (column) Wind speed at the anemometer. 0 WindDirection(degrees) degrees yes (column) Direction the wind comes from (0 = north). 0 ObukhovLength(m) m yes (column) Atmospheric stability; 99999 is neutral. 99999 MixingHeight(m) m yes (column) Mixing height. Also the LTO ceiling for aircraft in that hour. 914.4

Each calculation interval uses the meteo row nearest to its start. A row whose temperature or pressure is not a positive number stops the calculation with a message naming the row's date. How the values are used aloft is described in Ambient conditions aloft. To build the file from METAR reports, see scripts/README_metar_to_alaqs_meteo.md.

Example (header and first two rows of example/training/training_meteo.csv):

Scenario,DateTime(YYYY-mm-dd hh:mm:ss),Temperature(K),Humidity(kg_water/kg_dry_air),RelativeHumidity(0-1),SeaLevelPressure(Pa),WindSpeed(m/s),WindDirection(degrees),ObukhovLength(m),MixingHeight(m)
default,2025-12-01 00:00:00,280.5,0.00446,0.68,97600,5.0,225,99999,914.4
default,2025-12-01 01:00:00,280.5,0.00446,0.68,97600,5.0,225,99999,914.4

docs.title: ADS-B tracks
docs.text:
Observed flight trajectories that replace the ANP profile of selected movements. You select the file in ADS-B Table of the Calculate Emissions Inventory window. The file is optional. The study must have at least one runway, otherwise the file is rejected ("To import ADS-B data, at least one runway should exist in the study!").

Delimiter: comma, semicolon or tab, detected from the file.

Header: column names as below. Other columns (callsign, registration, ...) are ignored.

Each flight_id becomes a flight profile of that name. A movement uses it when its profile_id in the movements file is that flight_id; the movement row also gives the runway and taxi route used to place the track, and the engine used to check the fuel flow. Whether a flight is an arrival or a departure is taken from its altitude: descending is an arrival.

Column Unit Required Meaning flight_id yes Groups the rows of one flight. Rows in time order. latitude degrees (WGS84) yes longitude degrees (WGS84) yes altitude ft above mean sea level yes The airport elevation is subtracted; points of the take-off roll and of the landing roll are set to the ground. tas kt yes True airspeed. power_setting fraction one of power_setting or fuel_flow in each row Engine power setting, 0 to 1 (values outside 0 to 1.5 are rejected). The old name thrust is accepted, with a warning in the log. fuel_flow kg/s, whole aircraft one of power_setting or fuel_flow in each row Fuel flow of all engines together. Values below the ICAO idle fuel flow are kept; the log names each such flight. timestamp YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS no For your reference only. The time of the flight comes from the movement's runway_time and block_time.

Do not include the ground taxi: taxi emissions come from the taxi routes, and taxi rows would be read as flight points at zero height. How ADS-B tracks are used in the emission calculation is described in Aircraft emissions: ADS-B.

Example (header and first two rows of example/training/training_ads_b_data.csv):

flight_id,timestamp,latitude,longitude,altitude,tas,power_setting,fuel_flow
1764584438_PHBBA,2025-12-01 10:20:38,51.96246,4.455433,-15.0,11.0,0.9239,1.5688
1764584438_PHBBA,2025-12-01 10:20:42,51.962556,4.455224,-15.0,25.0,0.8655,1.4512

docs.title: Engine test events
docs.text:
Engine run-ups on an engine test site (an area source with Engine Test Site ticked). You load the file with Load engine test events CSV... in the area-source form (see Engine test sites) or with the script scripts/import_engine_test_events.py.

Delimiter: comma. UTF-8 text.

Header: column names as below, in any order. Empty cells take the default.

Column Unit Required Meaning Default when empty source_id yes (optional when loaded from a source's form) Source Name of the test-site area source. From a source's form, rows for other sources are skipped and counted in the summary. the form's source start_datetime ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) yes Start of the test. end_datetime ISO 8601 yes End of the test; must be after the start. aircraft_type yes ICAO aircraft type designator. test_id no Your own reference. engine_uid no Engine identifier from the engine table. the aircraft's default engine engine_count engines no Engines tested (positive whole number). the aircraft's engine count t_TX_s s per engine no Running time at idle (taxi mode). 0 t_AP_s s per engine no Running time at approach power. 0 t_CL_s s per engine no Running time at climb-out power. 0 t_TO_s s per engine no Running time at take-off power. 0 instudy no 1 include the event, 0 leave it out. 1

The import rejects a row with an empty required value, a date that is not ISO 8601, an end not after the start, a negative or non-whole running time, an invalid engine_count or instudy, or the same source_id, start_datetime and aircraft_type as an earlier row. It warns, without rejecting the row, about an unknown source, aircraft type or engine, a source that is not a test site, and running times longer than the event (60 s tolerance). How the events become emissions is described in Engine test sites.

Example (header and first two rows of example/training/training_engine_test_events.csv):

source_id,start_datetime,end_datetime,aircraft_type,test_id,engine_uid,engine_count,t_TX_s,t_AP_s,t_CL_s,t_TO_s,instudy
TESTPAD_A,2025-01-15T09:00:00,2025-01-15T09:15:00,C25C,LOG-2025-001,,,600,0,300,0,1
TESTPAD_A,2025-01-15T10:30:00,2025-01-15T10:50:00,PC24,LOG-2025-002,,,900,180,0,0,1

docs.title: Receptor points
docs.text:
Points where AUSTAL writes a concentration time series (for Plot Time Series and Compliance Report). AUSTAL takes at most 20 receptors; further rows are dropped with a warning in the log. Two places accept a receptor file, and they read it differently.

In the Calculate Dispersion dialog (Receptors CSV, both Generate modes, see Calculate Dispersion dialog):

  • Delimiter: comma.
  • Header names are not case-sensitive; lon and lat are accepted for longitude and latitude.
Column Unit Required Meaning Default when empty longitude degrees or metres, per EPSG yes x coordinate. latitude degrees or metres, per EPSG yes y coordinate. EPSG no Coordinate system of the two columns, the same in every row. 4326 (WGS84) id no Receptor name. height m no Receptor height above ground, written to AUSTAL for each receptor. 1.5

On the Configuration tab of Visualize Emission Calculation (Receptor Points, used by the AUSTAL module of the Dispersion Models tab):

  • Delimiter: comma, semicolon or tab, detected from the file.
  • Header names are case-sensitive.
Column Unit Required Meaning Default when empty longitude degrees or metres, per EPSG yes, unless geometry is given x coordinate. latitude degrees or metres, per EPSG yes, unless geometry is given y coordinate. geometry WKT instead of longitude and latitude Point in WKT, for example POINT (4.44 51.96). EPSG (or crs) yes Coordinate system, the same in every row. Without it no receptor is written (warning in the log). altitude m no Receptor height above ground. 1.5 id no Receptor name.

No receptor file ships with the training example. This example (points near the training airport) works in both places:

id,longitude,latitude,EPSG
R1,4.4400,51.9600,4326
R2,4.4500,51.9700,4326

Receptors CSV in the dialog: which points are used.

  • With Generate AUSTAL Input Files from OpenALAQS Emission Inventory File: the Receptors CSV when it is given and readable. Otherwise the receptor points stored in the inventory, if it has any (points marked as not in study are skipped), each at its stored height (1.5 m when empty). The plugin has no receptor layer to draw such points: the inventory holds them only if they were added outside the plugin windows. Without points, AUSTAL runs without receptors.
  • With Generate AUSTAL Input Files from CSV: the Receptors CSV only.
  • A Receptors CSV that cannot be read (wrong delimiter, no longitude/latitude column) is skipped with only a warning in the log, and the inventory's points, or none, are used instead. If Plot Time Series stays disabled after a run with a Receptors CSV, check the log.

See Dispersion with AUSTAL for what the receptors enable.

docs.title: Training course: errata
docs.text:
The training course slides (March 2026) predate plugin 5.4.1. Where the slides and this documentation differ, the documentation is correct. The differences:

  • The plugin version shown (3.0.DEV) is outdated; see Installation.
  • The Vertical Limit fields are greyed out and have no effect. The LTO ceiling is the meteo mixing height, or 914.4 m without meteo; see LTO ceiling and segment clipping.
  • The Generate Emission Inventory window no longer has Advanced Options and has a new ADS-B Table field; see Calculate Emissions Inventory window.
  • The movements file is semicolon-separated, and its columns and apu_code values have changed; see Movements.
  • The meteo headers are RelativeHumidity(0-1) and SeaLevelPressure(Pa); the relative humidity is a fraction; see Meteorology.
  • Activity profiles are relative shapes. A zero moves emissions to other hours and does not lower the annual total; see Activity profiles.
  • The Configuration tab has new settings: Atmosphere Aloft (default standard_lapse), BFFM2 Fuel-Flow Source and Time Interval; see Calculate emissions and query results.
  • The AUSTAL site defaults are 0.1 m, 0.6 m and 10.6 m, not 0.2, 1.2 and 11.2 m; see Site parameters.
  • The Calculate Dispersion dialog now writes the AUSTAL inputs itself, with pollutants, receptors, NOTALUFT and emission settings; see Calculate Dispersion dialog.
  • The taxi routes editor has two tabs, Create new route and Edit route; see Taxi routes.
  • Road traffic emissions do not include tyre and brake wear; see Pollutant mapping.
  • Helicopters, engine test sites and the compliance report are not in the slides; see Helicopters (FOCA 2015), Engine test sites and The compliance report.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This page lists the error messages and symptoms users most often meet, grouped by step of a study, with the cause and the fix. Each entry links to the page that explains the topic in full. Search this page for the words of the message you see (Ctrl+F, or the search box of the documentation site).

Most messages are also written to the OpenALAQS log: toolbar button Review Open ALAQS logs (User Guide).

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Installation
  • Opening or updating a study
  • Input files
  • Emissions
  • Dispersion with AUSTAL
  • Running without QGIS

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
QGIS asks to install missing Python libraries when Open-ALAQS loads. The plugin needs libraries that QGIS does not ship. Accept the QPIP dialog, then restart QGIS once. Without QPIP, install requirements.txt in the QGIS Python. See Install the dependencies.

The plugin does not appear after installing from a clone. The plugin is the open_alaqs/ folder of the repository, not the repository root: metadata.txt must be directly inside the plugin folder. See Install Open-ALAQS.

docs.title: Opening or updating a study
docs.text:
A form field turns red with "Upgrade the study with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py", or the log says "QGIS types the numeric columns ... as integer or text". The study was made with an earlier version. Update it with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py, after a backup. See Upgrading.

The log says "default_helicopter table missing" and helicopter movements find no helicopter. The study predates the helicopter catalog. Run the migration with the reference data refresh. See Upgrading from 5.3.x.

Results differ from those of an earlier version. This is expected when a release changes a method or the reference data. Upgrading lists what changes, and the CHANGELOG gives the details.

The OpenStreetMap import is disabled, or does nothing. The import needs the QuickOSM QGIS plugin. Without the airport latitude and longitude in the study setup it silently does nothing. Without Also import the data into ALAQS database the data go only to an OpenStreetMap Layers group. See Import OpenStreetMap data.

docs.title: Input files
docs.text:
"Headers of meteo csv file do not match". The meteo file must have exactly the ten headers, written with their units in brackets, for example Temperature(K). A missing, extra or renamed header is refused. See Meteorology. scripts/metar_to_alaqs_meteo.py writes a valid file from METAR observations.

"Problem with movement file. See log file", or the movement columns are read in the wrong order. One bad row (date, fewer than 10 fields) refuses the whole file; the log names the row. One missing or misspelt header name makes the plugin read every column by position. Use the exact header names. See Movements.

"To import ADS-B data, at least one runway should exist in the study!" Draw the runways before selecting the ADS-B file. See ADS-B tracks.

The log says "Lack of profile_id" for a movement. The movement names a flight profile that is not in the study. The aircraft's default profile is used instead. Check the profile_id column of the movements file, or the profiles of the study. See Flight profiles.

Engine test events are skipped. When the file is loaded from one source's form, rows for other sources are skipped and counted in the import summary. Use scripts/import_engine_test_events.py to load a file for several sources at once. Column specification: Engine test events.

docs.title: Emissions
docs.text:
BFFM2 is not offered for a pollutant. BFFM2 gives emission indices for NOx, CO and HC only. For another pollutant Method shows bymode; when you return to CO, HC or NOx, BFFM2 comes back if you had chosen it. See Calculate emissions.

The NOx correction changes nothing. The correction applies to bymode only. BFFM2 includes its own ambient correction, and helicopters follow the FOCA method. See NOx ambient correction.

A stationary source has no emissions. Check that it is in the study (In Study ticked) and that its activity and profiles are not zero. See Point and area sources and Activity Profiles.

docs.title: Dispersion with AUSTAL
docs.text:
Each symptom below is explained, with its fix, in Common failure modes.

  • "No Executable Loaded" after picking AUSTAL.
  • The run fails, or some substances have no results.
  • "AUSTAL input files could not be created: the selected time period" when generating the input files.
  • A result button says "No emission calculation loaded".
  • Plot Time Series and Compliance Report stay disabled.

Two more:

The site parameters (z0, d0, ha) of the Dispersion Models tab are not in austal.txt. The Calculate Dispersion dialog writes its own Roughness Length, Displacement Height and Anemometer Height, not those of the tab. Set them in the dialog before Generate AUSTAL Input Files. See Site parameters.

The dispersion results do not match the emission method chosen for the study. The Calculate Dispersion dialog recalculates the emissions with its own emission settings (default bymode, no NOx correction, no source dynamics). Set them to those of the study in the inventory option. See Calculate Dispersion dialog.

docs.title: Running without QGIS
docs.text:
ModuleNotFoundError for open_alaqs... when running the standalone pipeline. Run it from the repository root with PYTHONPATH=.. See USAGE, Troubleshooting.

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'qgis' when running a script. scripts/emissions_austal, scripts/austal_from_csv and the GSE application need the QGIS Python (for example the OSGeo4W Shell). The QGIS-free alternative is the standalone pipeline. See Running without the QGIS window.

docs.title: Tutorial: a study of Rotterdam The Hague Airport
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through a complete OpenALAQS study of Rotterdam The Hague Airport (EHRD) with the training data shipped with OpenALAQS. It is for new users of the QGIS plugin. It gives the values to enter and the results to expect; what each window and setting does is explained in the User Guide and the pages linked from each step.

What you will build. A study of three days of operations at EHRD: 13 aircraft movements over three gates and both runway directions, plus a car park, an access road, a power plant and the terminal as stationary sources. You will create the emission inventory, calculate emissions with two methods and compare them, and run a dispersion calculation with AUSTAL.

Files used. The training files in example/training, listed in README, Quick start. training_out.alaqs is the finished inventory, to compare with yours; training_validation_reference.xlsx holds the reference emissions per movement, per hour and per source type.

Contents: - 1. Create the study - 2. Import OpenStreetMap data (optional) - 3. Aircraft sources - 4. Stationary sources - 5. Activity profile exercise - Generate Emissions Inventory - Calculate emissions - Dispersion with AUSTAL

To start from the finished study instead of building it, click Load an Open ALAQS project on the toolbar and open training.alaqs. It already holds all sources and the taxi routes: continue at Create the inventory.

docs.title: 1. Create the study
docs.text:
Click Create an Open ALAQS project and save the new study, for example as training.alaqs in a folder of your own. In the ALAQS Project Properties window enter (see Starting a study):

Field Value Project Name OpenALAQS Training Course Airport tab ICAO Code EHRD Name Rotterdam Country NL Latitude (decimal) 51.9574278 Longitude (decimal) 4.4417028 Airport Elevation AMSL -5 m Average Temperature 15 °C Roadways tab Average Fleet Year 2020 Country Netherlands

When you enter EHRD, the name, country, coordinates and elevation are filled in from the internal database (stored as -15 ft, shown as -5 m). Enter Average Temperature by hand. Leave Vertical Limit as it is: the plugin does not use it (LTO ceiling). Click Save. The source layers (Gates, Runways, Taxiways, ...) appear empty in the QGIS layers panel.

docs.title: 2. Import OpenStreetMap data (optional)
docs.text:
With the QuickOSM plugin installed, click Import OSM data. The aerodrome is found from the ICAO code and the coordinates of the saved study. Tick Selective import and choose Runways and Taxiways (unticked, every layer type is imported). Tick Also import the data into ALAQS database; without it the data only appear in an OpenStreetMap Layers group and the study layers stay empty. See Import OpenStreetMap data. Then check in the attribute tables that:

  • each taxiway has its own Taxiway Name;
  • every Speed [km/h] is between about 15 and 30;
  • the Runway Name is 06/24.

OSM data varies in quality: compare it with the aerodrome chart and fix duplicates or geometry. Or skip this step and draw the sources yourself as below.

docs.title: 3. Aircraft sources
docs.text:
Draw each source with the QGIS digitizing tools and fill in its form (Define emission sources). Turn on snapping so that gates touch taxiways and taxiway segments meet: gaps break the taxi routes.

Gates. Three polygons around the stands, each touching a taxiway:

Gate Name Gate Type Where G2 CARGO cargo apron, south of the terminal G4 REMOTE remote stand, reached by bus G7 PIER pier stand at the terminal

The gate type selects the ground support and ground power emission factors.

Runway. One line along the runway centreline over the full pavement, from one end to the other (the bundled geometry runs from the 24 end to the 06 end):

Field Value Runway 1 06 (Runway 2 = 24 and Runway Name = 06/24 are filled in) Touchdown Offset, Runway 1 [m] 250 Touchdown Offset, Runway 2 [m] 250

Each movement names the runway end it uses (06 or 24). With a touchdown offset of 250 m, arrivals cross the threshold at about 13 m on a 3° approach.

Taxiways. One line per segment along the centreline:

Taxiway Name Speed [km/h] B, F, N, V, V0, V1, V1E, V2, V3, V6, Y 15 Y1, Y2 30

V0 joins the end of V to the V1/V3/Y junction, and V1E continues V1 to the runway 06 threshold. Both are drawn for this example and are not on the aerodrome chart.

Tracks. Leave the Tracks layer empty. Twelve movements use standard ANP flight profiles; movement 11 uses the ADS-B profile 1764584438_PHBBA, imported with the inventory (see Create the inventory).

docs.title: 4. Stationary sources
docs.text:
Parking lot. A polygon for the car park next to the terminal:

Field Value Parking Name ParkingLot Vehicles per Year 20 000 Height [m] 0 Speed [km/h] 20 Travel Distance [m] 250 Idle Time [min] 0 PC (Petrol) [%] / PC (Diesel) [%] 35 / 30 LCV (Petrol) [%] / LCV (Diesel) [%] 10 / 5 HDT (Petrol) [%] / HDT (Diesel) [%] 3 / 2 Motorcycle [%] / Bus [%] 10 / 5

Click Recalculate on the Emissions tab. You should get:

Field Value CO [g/vehicle] 54.66 HC [g/vehicle] 4.05 NOx [g/vehicle] 95.82 SOx [g/vehicle] 0.286 PM10 [g/vehicle] 0.800

Roadway. A line for the access road from the motorway to the terminal, about 1025 m long:

Field Value Roadway Name Roadway Vehicles per Year 20 000 Height [m] 0 Speed [km/h] 30 PC (Petrol) [%] / PC (Diesel) [%] 35 / 30 LCV (Petrol) [%] / LCV (Diesel) [%] 15 / 5 HDT (Petrol) [%] / HDT (Diesel) [%] 3 / 2 Motorcycle [%] / Bus [%] 5 / 5

After Recalculate you should see CO [g/km] 0.181, NOx [g/km] 0.341 and HC [g/km] 0.0118. How COPERT factors are derived: Road traffic and parkings.

Point source. A point near the terminal for the power and heating plant (Point sources):

Field Value Source Name Power Category Power/Heat Plant Type Bituminous Coal : Pulverized (> 10^8 BTU/HR) Substance Solid Height [m] 20 Temperature [°C] 400 Diameter [m] 1 Gas Velocity [m/s] 15 Activity per Year 4380 (operating hours) Activity Unit hr

Keep the default emission factors of this type: CO 0.3002, HC 0.55, NOx 10.51, SOx 39.03, PM10 60.04 kg/unit. Only the unit differs from the shipped default (per 1000_kg): here one unit is one operating hour. 4380 of 8760 hours gives half the hourly factor in each hour.

Area source. A polygon over the terminal footprint (Area sources):

Field Value Source Name Terminal Units per Year 8760 (operating hours) Height [m] 10 CO [kg/unit] 0.1 All other factors 0

This gives exactly 0.1 kg CO in every hour.

Buildings. You may draw the terminal in the Buildings layer (Height [m] about 12). OpenALAQS does not pass buildings to AUSTAL yet, so this changes no result.

All training sources are in study and use the default activity profile (1.0 in every hour, day and month).

docs.title: 5. Activity profile exercise
docs.text:
Optional. Click Edit profiles and create an hourly profile parking_hours for a car park closed from 23:00 to 05:00 (Activity profiles):

Hour (local) Multiplier 00:00 to 04:00 0.0 05:00 to 22:00 1.0 23:00 0.0

Each hour runs to the next, so hour 04 ends at 05:00. Set it as the Hourly Profile of ParkingLot (Profiles tab). The results quoted below assume the default profile; remove the custom one again to reproduce them.

docs.title: Taxi routes
docs.text:
Click Define taxi routes and create twelve routes: for each gate G2, G4 and G7, one arrival and one departure route per runway direction. How the editor works is in Taxi routes. For every route use Instance 1 and move all Aircraft Groups to Selected. List a departure's taxiways from the stand to the runway and an arrival's from the runway to the stand.

Route Taxiway sequence Where it meets the runway G2/24/D/1 F → N → V → V6 line-up 82 m from the 24 threshold G4/24/D/1 Y1 → Y → V0 → V → V6 line-up 82 m from the 24 threshold G7/24/D/1 B → Y2 → Y → V0 → V → V6 line-up 82 m from the 24 threshold G2/24/A/1 V3 → V0 → N → F exit 1441 m from the 24 threshold G4/24/A/1 V3 → Y → Y1 exit 1441 m from the 24 threshold G7/24/A/1 V3 → Y → Y2 → B exit 1441 m from the 24 threshold G2/06/D/1 F → N → V0 → V1 → V1E line-up at the 06 threshold G4/06/D/1 Y1 → Y → V1 → V1E line-up at the 06 threshold G7/06/D/1 B → Y2 → Y → V1 → V1E line-up at the 06 threshold G2/06/A/1 V6 → V → N → F exit 2116 m from the 06 threshold G4/06/A/1 V6 → V → V0 → Y → Y1 exit 2116 m from the 06 threshold G7/06/A/1 V6 → V → V0 → Y → Y2 → B exit 2116 m from the 06 threshold

Each runway direction needs its own routes, because the route sets where a departure lines up and where an arrival leaves the runway.

docs.title: Create the inventory
docs.text:
Click Calculate Emissions Inventory and enter:

Field Value Directory a folder of your choice File Name training (the plugin adds _out.alaqs: the file is training_out.alaqs) Movements Table training_movements.csv Filter Start Date 2025-12-01 06:00:00 Filter End Date 2025-12-03 09:00:00 (the default: last movement's hour + 1 h) Meteorological Table training_meteo.csv ADS-B Table training_ads_b_data.csv X Resolution 250 m, 100 cells Y Resolution 250 m, 100 cells Z Resolution 50 m, 20 cells

The grid is 25 km × 25 km and 1000 m high, centred on the airport reference point. The dialog has no vertical limit field: for aircraft the ceiling of each hour is the MixingHeight of the meteorology (914.4 m on 1 December, 1500 m on 2 December, 600 m on 3 December).

Click Create Inventory. The two ADS-B tracks are imported as CUSTOM profiles: 1764584438_PHBBA, used by movement 11, and 1764583565_PHRTM, which no movement uses. They are illustrative: their speeds and climb are those of a light aircraft, and only their fuel flow follows the A20N's ICAO curve. See ADS-B and the ADS-B file format.

docs.title: Movements table
docs.text:
training_movements.csv (format: Movements) has 13 movements with runway times from 2025-12-01 06:05 to 2025-12-03 08:00. Five of them:

# runway_time aircraft gate op runway engine profile_id taxi route 1 2025-12-01 06:05 A20N G4 A 24 01P20CM128 (LEAP-1A26) JET-SMALL-A-1 G4/24/A/1 2 2025-12-01 06:15 A20N G4 D 24 01P20CM128 (LEAP-1A26) JET-SMALL-D-1 G4/24/D/1 3 2025-12-01 06:40 E190 G7 A 24 11GE144 (CF34-10E) JET-REGIONAL-A-1 G7/24/A/1 8 2025-12-02 07:30 E190 G4 D 06 11GE144 (CF34-10E) JET-REGIONAL-D-1 G4/06/D/1 11 2025-12-03 07:00 A20N G2 D 24 01P20CM128 (LEAP-1A26) 1764584438_PHBBA (CUSTOM) G2/24/D/1
  • 8 A20N (JET SMALL) and 5 E190 (JET REGIONAL) movements, each with its default engine.
  • 7 arrivals and 6 departures, in the early morning of each day. Rows 6, 8 and 13 use runway 06, the others runway 24.
  • All rows have apu_code = 0 and gate_emissions_code = 0, so the study has no APU and no gate emissions. Every row sets taxi_engine_count 2, engine_thrust_level_for_taxiing 0.07, taxi_fuel_ratio 1 and number_of_stop_and_gos 0.

docs.title: Meteorology
docs.text:
training_meteo.csv (format: Meteorology) covers 2025-12-01 00:00 to 2025-12-04 00:00. The row of 2025-12-01 06:00:

Parameter Value Temperature 280.5 K Humidity 0.00446 kg/kg Relative humidity 0.68 Sea-level pressure 97 600 Pa Wind speed 5 m/s Wind direction 225° Obukhov length 99 999 m (neutral) Mixing height 914.4 m

On 1 and 2 December the air is drier than the ISA reference (humidity ratio 0.00446 and 0.00381 kg/kg in the file, against 0.00634 kg/kg), so the BFFM2 humidity correction raises NOx; on 3 December (0.01463 kg/kg in the file) the factor is 0.85. The calculation derives the humidity from the relative humidity, temperature and pressure, which gives nearly the same values (0.0148 kg/kg on 3 December). See NOx ambient correction.

docs.title: Calculate emissions
docs.text:
Click Visualize Emission Calculation and open your training_out.alaqs (or the shipped one). On the Configuration tab (Calculate emissions and query results):

Setting Value Start 2025-12-01 06:00:00 End 2025-12-03 09:00:00 Method BFFM2 Apply NOx Corrections not ticked (no effect with BFFM2) Source Dynamics none Time Interval 1 hour

Method offers BFFM2 only while the pollutant is CO, HC or NOx. For another pollutant (for example PM10 in exercise 4) it shows bymode; when you return to NOx, BFFM2 comes back.

Exercises. The expected values come from training_validation_reference.xlsx.

  1. Parking CO. Select ParkingSource and CO, click View Emissions Table: 0.1248 kg CO in the 06:00 to 07:00 hour. Then click Plot Vector Layer to see it on the grid.
  2. NOx by method. Select MovementSource and NOx. Calculate with bymode, export the table, then with BFFM2, and compare the totals (BFFM2). Over the 13 movements NOx is 31.84 kg with bymode and 16.61 kg with BFFM2. BFFM2 gives 52 % less NOx on the six departures (41 to 60 % per movement) and 35 % less on the seven arrivals (19 to 45 %). On the arrivals it gives 8 % more CO (1 to 16 %).
  3. Differences by aircraft type. Split exercise 2 by aircraft. On the arrivals BFFM2 NOx is 43 % below bymode for the A20N and 23 % below for the E190: the difference depends on the aircraft, not only on the mode.
  4. PM10 parts. With MovementSource, compare pm10_kg with pm10_nonvol_kg + pm10_sul_kg + pm10_organic_kg. They are equal for departures. For arrivals pm10_kg is higher by the brake wear. p1_kg and p2_kg equal pm10_kg. See Particulate matter.
  5. Smooth & Shift. Set Source Dynamics to smooth & shift and plot the vector layer again. Taxi emissions are spread over a band 190 m wide for the A20N and 100 m for the E190, from the ground up to 50 m and 25 m. See Smooth and shift.

Log check. Open Review Open ALAQS logs. For this study it reports no ADS-B fuel flow above 1.5 times the EEDB take-off value and no taxi route that does not fit the runway.

docs.title: Dispersion with AUSTAL
docs.text:
Install AUSTAL first (AUSTAL installation). Here the input files are written from the BFFM2 calculation on the Dispersion Models tab, then AUSTAL runs from the Calculate Dispersion dialog.

  1. Keep the Configuration tab of Calculate emissions. Check that the pollutant is CO, HC or NOx and that Method is BFFM2. On the Dispersion Models tab set:
Setting Value Is Enabled ticked Title EHRD_training Roughness Length 0.1 m Displacement Height 0.6 m Anemometer Height 10.6 m Quality Level 1 Options String NOSTANDARD;SCINOTAT;Kmax=1

The site parameters are the defaults; for EHRD the emission-weighted roughness of the airport ground sources is 0.105 m, class 0.10 (see Site parameters). 2. Select source type all and NOx, click View Emissions Table, and choose an empty folder when asked. The input files are written there. 3. Click Calculate Dispersion. Select the AUSTAL executable, then Use Existing AUSTAL Input Files with that folder as Work Directory, and click Run AUSTAL. 4. In section 4, tick Grid Management and set File to training_out.alaqs. Choose Pollutant NOx and Averaging annual mean, and click Plot Vector Layer.

The map shows nox-y00a.dmna: the mean NOx concentration over the 51 hours from 2025-12-01 06:00 to 2025-12-03 09:00, not an annual mean. Compare the pattern with the wind during the movement hours: from 225° on 1 December, 270° on 2 December and 180° on 3 December. The aircraft operate only about two hours each morning, so these concentrations illustrate the method and cannot be compared with limit values.

The training inventory has no receptor points, so Plot Time Series and Compliance Report stay disabled. To try them, generate the inputs in the dialog with Generate AUSTAL Input Files from OpenALAQS Emission Inventory File, a Receptors CSV (for example the two points of the receptor example) and NOTALUFT ticked; see Results.

docs.title: Upgrading from an earlier version
docs.text:
This page is for users who open a study made with an earlier version of OpenALAQS. It lists which results change and how to update the study file.

  • Upgrading from 5.4.1
  • Upgrading from 5.4.0
  • Upgrading from 5.3.x

docs.title: Upgrading from 5.4.1
docs.text:
OpenALAQS 5.4.2 is a fix release. Studies need no migration, and the shipped examples give the same results as with 5.4.1. The full list is in the CHANGELOG.

Recalculate only a study that falls under one of these cases:

  • AUSTAL runs made with Calculate Dispersion, "Generate from OpenALAQS output". The emissions are recalculated with the emission settings chosen in the dialog (they were always bymode, without NOx correction or source dynamics), flight segments and roadways are clipped to the grid, and the receptor heights are passed to AUSTAL (every receptor was at 1.5 m).
  • Movements calculated together (same engine, profile, runway and taxi route in one period) that differ in aircraft type with another engine count, in tow_ratio with the NOx correction, in gate_emissions_code at one gate, or in track or runway direction: each movement now gets its own result.
  • Single-engine taxi with set_time_of_main_engine_start_before_takeoff_in_s, or a departure with a main engine start time and a queue.
  • Engine tests with the BFFM2 thrust mode when the meteo table has more than one row.
  • Standalone pipeline and Dataiku recipes: movements with a main engine start or off time or a taxi_fuel_ratio other than 1 (single-engine taxi now as in the plugin); BFFM2 taxi with an engine_thrust_level_for_taxiing other than 0.07; studies with missing or off-hour meteo rows, movements before the first meteo row, or an empty mixing height with a vertical limit other than 914.4 m.

Re-import a movements file whose header had a missing, misspelt or unknown name, or which had no header line: such files are now read in the documented column order, and a first line starting with a date is kept as a movement.

docs.title: Upgrading from 5.4.0
docs.text:
OpenALAQS 5.4.1 changes the BFFM2 fuel flow and the ambient conditions used at each flight segment's height. The full list is in the CHANGELOG; the atmosphere models are described in ATMOSPHERE_ALOFT.md.

Recalculate:

  • Every BFFM2 inventory (bffm2_traj and bffm2_anchor). The fuel flow read on the ICAO curve at the thrust share is now scaled with delta sqrt(theta), and each segment uses the temperature and pressure at its height (default standard_lapse). On the example inventory, bffm2_traj NOx falls by 11 % and CO2 by 5 %; warm or windy studies can change by more than 10 % in NOx.
  • bymode inventories with segments above 3,000 ft (hours whose mixing height exceeds 914.4 m), for PM10 only: MEEM V1 nvPM now uses the local temperature and pressure (-0.01 % on the example). Fuel, NOx, CO, HC and SOx of bymode are unchanged.
  • Engine tests computed with BFFM2 in the plugin (station pressure, fuel-flow scaling).
  • AUSTAL dispersion runs that kept the default site parameters. The defaults of the AUSTAL module changed (they were 0.2 / 1.2 / 11.2 m); the new defaults are in Site parameters. Studies that saved explicit values keep them.

No setting gives 5.4.0 BFFM2 results back. "Atmosphere Aloft" = ground_held restores the 5.4.0 ambient conditions (the hourly row at every height, the sea-level pressure as the ambient pressure) but not the old fuel-flow scaling, which was wrong and has no switch. Use ground_held to see how much of a change comes from the atmosphere.

The option "Atmosphere Aloft" is in the emission calculation dialog, see Calculate emissions and query results. Studies themselves need no migration.

A 5.3.x study migrated with the 5.4.0 script whose forms still refuse a decimal (field red, "Upgrade the study with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py"), or whose log still says "QGIS types the numeric columns ... as integer or text" when it is opened: run the script of this version on it once more (step 2 of How to update a study).

docs.title: Upgrading from 5.3.x
docs.text:
This section covers a study made with OpenALAQS 5.3.x. A study made with 5.0.x to 5.2.x is updated the same way, see step 2 of How to update a study. The full list of changes is in the CHANGELOG.

The changes of 5.4.1 apply too: a 5.3.x study opened in 5.4.1 also gets the BFFM2, atmosphere aloft and AUSTAL default changes listed there, so also read Upgrading from 5.4.0.

docs.title: Results that change
docs.text:
Recalculate a study after the upgrade if any of these applies to it:

Change Studies affected Runway placement of ANP profiles: arrivals touch down at the landing threshold plus the runway's Touchdown Offset (else the profile's own 50 ft crossing), departures start their take-off roll where the taxi route last meets the runway (see Runways) every study with ANP arrivals or departures The Touchdown Offset of the first-named runway end (touchdown) was stored but not used; it is now used, and the second end has its own offset (touchdown_2) studies with a non-zero touchdown Arrival runway_time is the touchdown (A-CDM ALDT); the landing roll of the profile is taken out of the arrival taxi time (block time minus runway time) every study with arrivals; check how runway_time was filled in A movement whose taxi time comes out at 0 s (block time equal to runway time, or an arrival whose block to runway time is no longer than its landing roll) keeps its APU, stop-and-go and brake-wear emissions; only the route and queuing get no time. It lost all its taxi emissions before studies with such movements Aircraft SOx comes from the fuel sulphur: 0.758 g/kg for jet fuel, 0.2 g/kg for AvGas (it was 0) every study with aircraft BFFM2 segment Mach is TAS / a, with a = √(γ R T) BFFM2 studies with meteo away from ISA MEEM V1 nvPM above 3000 ft above the aerodrome follows the MEEM V1 method of ICAO CAEP/13-MDG (OPR from press_ratio, ISA + ΔT) hours whose MixingHeight is above 914.4 m The NOx ambient correction (Apply NOx Corrections, bymode) applies to take-off and climb-out segments only; it was applied to every flight segment bymode with the correction on: arrival NOx goes up In Study (parkings, roadways, point and area sources) is saved from the form; a source drawn through the form in 5.3.x got an empty flag and was left out of the calculation, and unticking the box saved nothing studies with sources created or edited through the form Engine Test Site (area sources) is saved from the form; ticking or unticking it had no effect studies with engine test sites The airport altitude of aircraft movements (NOx correction, MEEM V1) comes from the study's airport elevation (user_study_setup), not from the grid reference altitude studies where the two differ A taxi route is oriented by its own gate, not by the gate of the first movement that uses it studies where movements use a route defined for another gate Engine data (default_aircraft_engine_ei): FOCA engines from ACT_PRF 2.6.3 (B601 to B603 PM10; turboprops T601, T602, T603, T717 and T790 now jet fuel, SOx 0.758 g/kg), 1ZM001 taxi values (were 0), OPR and 5th nvPM point for MEEM V1 studies with these engines, once the engine table is refreshed (see below) Standalone austal: receptors are clipped to the study grid (they were clipped to a 75 x 250 m square, which dropped receptors inside a larger grid); the UTM zone is the plugin's; the AUSTAL reference point is the grid reference, not the airport standalone runs with receptors outside that square, in the southern hemisphere or on a zone boundary, or with the grid reference away from the airport scripts/emissions_austal: smooth & shift and should_apply_nox_corrections are read as documented (they could be ignored before) runs of that script with these settings

docs.title: A study keeps its own engine, aircraft and profile tables
docs.text:
A project .alaqs carries its own copies of the reference tables, among them default_aircraft, default_aircraft_engine_ei and default_aircraft_profiles. Calculate Emissions Inventory copies them from the open project into every new inventory; the inventory template has none. A study made with 5.3.6 therefore keeps the 5.3.6 engine data after the upgrade:

  • press_ratio and the 5th nvPM point are empty, so MEEM V1 uses OPR 30 above 3000 ft;
  • the old FOCA rows (B601 to B603 PM10, turboprops as AvGas) and 1ZM001 with fuel flow and EIs 0 in taxi;
  • nvpm_number_ei in #/s instead of #/kg (no output column carries nvPM number).

Only a 0 or empty sox_ei is replaced at run time (by 0.758 g/kg for jet fuel, 0.2 g/kg for AvGas, from the row's fuel_type).

A study made with 5.3.0 to 5.3.5 also lacks the 5.3.6 corrections of default_aircraft and default_aircraft_profiles (the ANP v2.2 type profiles and default profiles, see the 5.3.6 entry of the CHANGELOG): refreshing the engine table alone (step 2, second command) is enough only for a 5.3.6 study; a 5.3.0 to 5.3.5 study needs the full refresh (step 2, third command), or at least those three tables (--refresh-reference-data --refresh-tables default_aircraft,default_aircraft_engine_ei,default_aircraft_profiles).

docs.title: How to update a study
docs.text:
1. For a new study, create a new project (Create an Open ALAQS project): it is made from the template of this version and has the current tables.
  2. For an existing study, update the .alaqs with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py. The script is not in the plugin zip: run it with Python 3 from a checkout of the repository at this version (it reads the templates and CSVs of that checkout). Close the study in QGIS first. The script writes a backup (<name>.bak-<timestamp>.alaqs) unless --no-backup is given.
  3. Schema only (adds touchdown_2, engine_test_events, is_test_site and the other missing tables and columns, empty, and the three named point-source profiles heating_season, cooling_season and business_hours in the month, day and hour profile tables, with the script's own values, unless a profile of that name exists; a new project has none of them; converts the numeric columns of the layers to REAL, see below): 
    python scripts/migrate_alaqs.py study.alaqs
    What the schema step does to the numeric columns of the layers (height, speed, fleet percentages, emission factors, ...):
    • In 5.3.x QGIS could round a decimal typed in a form (2.5 saved as 3) or store it as text ("30,3"). The script converts these columns to numbers. Values are kept; a text that reads as a number becomes that number.
    • Texts it cannot read are listed as WARNING: <table>.<column>: <n> value(s) are not numbers and are left as text: .... Correct them in QGIS. A text such as "1,234" is left too, since it could mean 1.234 or 1234.
    • A study already migrated with the 5.4.0 script needs this step once more; the plan then shows ~ STATISTICS <layer>.
    • Until the study is migrated, it opens and calculates as before, but the log says "Upgrade the study with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py", and a form refuses a decimal in such a field (field red, tooltip "QGIS would save this value as ...").
  4. Schema and the engine table (replaces every row of default_aircraft_engine_ei, including rows you added or edited): 
    python scripts/migrate_alaqs.py study.alaqs --refresh-reference-data --refresh-tables default_aircraft_engine_ei
  5. Schema and all reference tables, including the user-extensible ones (default_aircraft, default_aircraft_engine_ei, default_aircraft_profiles, default_aircraft_apu_ef, default_aircraft_start_ef, default_gate_profiles, default_helicopter, default_helicopter_engines): 
    python scripts/migrate_alaqs.py study.alaqs --refresh-reference-data --refresh-include-user-extensible
    This overwrites every row you added or edited in those tables, CUSTOM (ADS-B) profiles stored in the project's default_aircraft_profiles included (see scripts/README.md). Add --dry-run to see the plan first.
  6. A study made with 5.0.x to 5.2.x is updated the same way. The schema step creates its missing tables and columns empty (default_helicopter and default_helicopter_engines, the 5.2.0 columns of default_aircraft_engine_ei and default_stationary_ef, shapes_point_sources.activity_unit), so such a study needs the full refresh (third command) to get the current helicopter catalog, engine, aircraft and profile data; without it helicopter movements find an empty catalog (the log says "default_helicopter table missing" or lists no helicopters). The refresh reports row counts only ("9243 rows -> 9218 rows (-25)"), not which rows go: a movement file that names a removed CUSTOM profile falls back to the aircraft's default profile with a "Lack of profile_id" warning in the log, so export the profiles you added before refreshing.
  7. An existing inventory (<name>_out.alaqs) opens and calculates in Visualize Emission Calculation without migration (checked here for inventories made with 5.0.0 to 5.4.0; it keeps the engine and profile tables it was made with, and the results do not change with the migration). python scripts/migrate_alaqs.py <name>_out.alaqs updates it with the inventory template, selected from the _out.alaqs suffix; its grid_3d_definition and cache_runway_trajectories tables, which every inventory has and the template does not, are reported as extra and left in place.
  8. Check Touchdown Offset, Runway 1 [m] and Touchdown Offset, Runway 2 [m] of each runway (touchdown_2 is empty after the migration: each arrival profile's own distance), In Study of the stationary sources and Engine Test Site of the area sources.
  9. Generate the inventory again (Calculate Emissions Inventory) with the ADS-B file, if any: the ADS-B tracks are imported into the new inventory, and at an airport with a non-zero elevation the points of the take-off roll and of the landing are now set to the ground (height 0).
  10. Recalculate (Visualize Emission Calculation).

docs.title: OpenALAQS User Guide
docs.text:
This guide walks through the OpenALAQS plugin in QGIS: setting up a study, drawing the emission sources, generating the emission inventory and looking at the results. It is for airport air quality modellers who use the plugin. The input file formats are in Input file formats, the calculation methods in the methods pages, and dispersion in Dispersion with AUSTAL.

  • Introduction
  • Workflow at a glance
  • The OpenALAQS Toolbar
  • Starting a Study
  • Setup a new study
  • Open an existing study
  • Import OpenStreetMap data
  • Define emission sources
  • Add, edit and delete features
  • Visualize and Edit Attribute Values
  • Aircraft related Sources: Gates, Runways, Taxiways, Tracks, Helicopters
  • Stationary Sources: Parking Lots, Roadways, Point sources, Area sources, Engine test sites, Buildings
  • Activity Profiles

  • Calculate Emissions Inventory window
  • Calculate emissions and query results
  • PM10 output columns
