docs.title: Utilities and entry points
docs.text:
adapt_meteo.py         .alaqs (or external CSV) -> meteo.csv
adapt_receptors.py     external receptor CSV -> standard receptors.csv
make_config.py         scaffold a config.json from .alaqs metadata
orchestrate.py         builds the six-folder austal_prep structure;
                       the `austal` subcommand; callable as a Python
                       function for embedding in other pipelines
cli.py / __main__.py   `python -m openalaqs_standalone <command>`:
                       dispatches to `aircraft` or `austal`
runway_placement.py    placement of flight profiles on the runway (rules shared
                       with the plugin: open_alaqs/core/tools/runway_placement.py)
runway_checks.py       route and profile check report; also
                       `python -m openalaqs_standalone.runway_checks study.alaqs out.csv`

docs.title: Source coverage
docs.text: Source type ALAQS table Status Roadway shapes_roadways implemented (adapter) Parking shapes_parking implemented (adapter) Point shapes_point_sources implemented (adapter) Area shapes_area_sources implemented (adapter) Gate shapes_gates + default_gate_profiles implemented (movement-driven calculator) Aircraft movement user_aircraft_movements implemented (calculator, 3 methods) Helicopter movement user_aircraft_movements implemented (FOCA calculator) Engine test site engine_test_events + shapes_area_sources (is_test_site='1') implemented (calculator, 3 thrust modes)

docs.title: Running one module
docs.text:
Each compute module also has its own CLI entry point, useful for isolating one source type:

python -m openalaqs_standalone.extract_sources study.alaqs --out sources.parquet
python -m openalaqs_standalone.compute_road study.alaqs --year 2025 --out road.parquet
python -m openalaqs_standalone.adapt_meteo study.alaqs --year-shift-to 2025 --out meteo.csv
python -m openalaqs_standalone.adapt_receptors cimlk.csv \
    --source-epsg 28992 --target-epsg 32631 --out receptors.csv
python -m openalaqs_standalone.make_config study.alaqs --year 2025 --out config.json

docs.title: Prerequisite: the stationary EFs must already be in the .alaqs file
docs.text:
The stationary half of this pipeline does not run COPERT5 or compute emission factors. It reads the pre-computed nox_gm_km, pm10_gm_km, p1_gm_km (etc.) values already stored in the shapes_roadways and shapes_parking tables, then multiplies by distance, vehicle counts, and the temporal profile to produce hourly emissions.

So the .alaqs file fed to the stationary computes must have been produced by an upstream OpenALAQS plugin run that:

  • applied COPERT5 with the correct fleet composition and Euro standards,
  • applied any study-specific adjustments (cold-start at trip scale, non-exhaust EMEP/EEA Tier 2 factors, parking scaling, etc.),
  • wrote the resulting g/km and g/vh values back into the source tables.

The standalone stationary computes are faithful to whatever EFs are in the file: fixes the plugin applied when it wrote the EFs (such as the parking cold start at trip scale) carry through; EFs written by an older plugin give correspondingly older emissions.

The aircraft half is different: it is a real calculator and needs no pre-computed EFs. It reads the engine emission-index tables, the aircraft profiles, the gate profiles and the meteo directly and integrates the emissions itself.

docs.title: Workflow for the stationary inputs
docs.text:
1. Build the inventory in QGIS using the OpenALAQS plugin (5.0.0 or later, which applies the parking cold start at trip scale).
  2. The plugin's Recalculate button of the parking and roadway forms writes the EFs into shapes_roadways and shapes_parking.
  3. Save the resulting .alaqs file.
  4. Run the austal command against that file.

docs.title: Why the stationary half is structured this way
docs.text: The plugin's emission-calculation modules (RoadwaySourceModule.py, ParkingSourceModule.py) have QGIS dependencies mixed with the COPERT5 logic, so importing them outside QGIS is not straightforward. The stationary computes read the EFs the plugin already wrote rather than recomputing them. The long-term fix is to extract the pure-Python calculation logic into a shared core/tools/ and have both the plugin and the standalone import it; until then, the workflow above is the bridge. The aircraft half already follows that better pattern: it shares the QGIS-free open_alaqs.core.tools.* algorithm modules with the validation reference.

docs.title: Verifying your .alaqs has the right stationary EFs
docs.text:
For an EHRD study that is not shipped with the repository, the parking baseline with the trip-scale cold start is (computed with 5.2.0):

  • NOx 31.26 kg/yr
  • PM10 3.27 kg/yr
  • PM2.5 1.79 kg/yr (PM10/PM2.5 ratio 1.83)

and an inventory without the trip-scale cold start gives NOx around 20.25 kg/yr instead of 31.26. These figures do not apply to the bundled training study: its single ParkingLot (20 000 vehicles per year, NOx 95.82 g/vehicle) gives NOx 1916.33 kg and PM10 15.99 kg for 2025 (python -m openalaqs_standalone.compute_parking example/training/training_out.alaqs --year 2025 --out parking.parquet from the repository root).

docs.title: Source ID prefixes
docs.text:
Every source ID carries a type prefix, used by the by-type aggregation and to keep namespaces distinct in a combined sources.parquet:

  • road:<roadway_id>
  • parking:<parking_id>
  • point:<point_id>
  • area:<area_id>
  • engine_test:<oid> (an area source flagged is_test_site = '1'; its source_type is engine_test)
  • gate:<gate_id> (the gate geometry; gate emissions are folded into the aircraft movement totals)
  • aircraft:cell:<ix>_<iy>_<iz> (a synthetic per-grid-cell source for the gridded aircraft emissions, one per occupied 3D cell)

docs.title: Pollutants
docs.text:
The stationary computes support co, hc, nox, sox, pm10, pm25 (the constant STATIONARY_POLLUTANTS in _profiles.py), which is the default pollutant list for the stationary computes and for the austal command.

The aircraft core supports co, co2, hc, nox, sox, pm10, pm25. The stationary source tables carry no co2. When --include-aircraft is used, the aircraft emissions are filtered to the requested pollutant list so the combined emissions.parquet is coherent. --pollutants of the austal command accepts co2: the stationary sources contribute 0 for it (they are not asked for co2, and one info line says so), and with --include-aircraft the aircraft co2 is written to emissions.parquet and co2_emissions.gpkg.

austal_prep writes co2 to austal.txt and series.dmna as the substance co2 (source strength in g/s), the same name the plugin writes. co2 (like co, hc and sox) is not one of the substances of the standard AUSTAL 3.3 settings; it is defined in the austal.settings shipped with OpenALAQS (documents/AUSTAL/, section [CO2], concentration in mg/m3). Replace the austal.settings of the AUSTAL installation with that copy before running AUSTAL on these inputs (see AUSTAL.md).

austal_prep writes pm10 as two AUSTAL components, pm-1 (the fine fraction, pm10_fine_fraction) and pm-2 (the rest), which AUSTAL sums into substance pm; pm25 is written as pm25-1 (substance pm25).

docs.title: Emission factor columns (stationary)
docs.text:
The column that holds PM2.5 differs between the schema of each source type:

Source Total PM10 column PM2.5 column Road pm10_gm_km p2_gm_km (p1_gm_km is PM0.1) Parking pm10_gm_vh p2_gm_vh Point pm10_kg_k p2_kg_k (assumed; matches parking) Area pm10_kg_unit p2_kg_unit (assumed; matches parking)

The pollutant-column dict in each compute module encodes this. For point and area sources the p2_* = PM2.5 assumption is empirically unverified: the training study has one point source (Power, PM10 60.04 kg/unit but P1 and P2 0) and one area source (Terminal, no PM), so no bundled study has a PM2.5 factor for these types to test against. If a study uses these types and the PM10/PM2.5 ratio looks wrong, verify the upstream conventions.

docs.title: Activity profiles (stationary)
docs.text: _profiles.py builds an hourly multiplier array from a (hour_profile, daily_profile, month_profile) triplet, normalised so the mean over the year is 1.0; the per-hour emission is then (annual_kg / hours_in_year) * mult[h]. Missing or unknown profiles fall back to all-1.0. The hour count is leap-year-aware.

docs.title: Coordinate systems
docs.text:
• ALAQS internal: EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator). Geometries in the .alaqs database are stored in this CRS, and that is what extract_sources and the aircraft grid polygons output in their WKT.
  • AUSTAL local: a metric UTM zone, configured per study via utm_epsg in config.json. Reprojection from 3857 to the AUSTAL frame happens in austal_prep.
  • CIMLK receptors: EPSG:28992 (Dutch Rijksdriehoek). Reprojection to UTM happens in adapt_receptors.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The aircraft pipeline (per-movement core, gate emissions, time-and-grid distribution, parallel driver, AUSTAL and GeoPackage output) is complete, and the austal command joins the stationary and aircraft halves into one run.

What is not yet built:

  • MESO-NH export. An exporter to the MESO-NH ASCII emission formats (a ground-emissions case and an altitude-emissions case) is scoped but not implemented: a few conversion conventions still need to be confirmed (the molec/cm2/s conversion basis for the ground case, the multi-species column order, the altitude datum/sign convention).
  • Point and area PM column convention is assumed, not verified (see "Emission factor columns" above): no bundled study has a non-zero PM2.5 factor for those source types.
  • Hourly periods only. The standalone works in hourly periods that start on the hour; a movement takes the meteo row nearest to the start of its hour. The plugin uses the study's time interval, so the two agree for studies with hourly periods only.
  • Tracks are not followed. The plugin lays a movement with a track_id along its track (shapes_tracks): the trajectory points follow the track, which changes the segment lengths and so the emissions (on the training study, an A20N departure along a turning track gets 4.32 kg NOx instead of 4.18 kg with bymode). The standalone ignores track_id and shapes_tracks and always uses the profile along the runway axis, so results differ for movements with a track. ADS-B (CUSTOM) profiles are not tracks and are followed by both.
  • Engine tests in the austal pipeline are computed with the ICAO mode values ("snap"): compute_engine_test_emissions passes no database connection, so BFFM2 events fall back to snap there.
  • Shared-import refactor of the stationary half. The stationary computes still read pre-computed EFs rather than calling shared COPERT5 logic; see "Why the stationary half is structured this way".

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=. pytest openalaqs_standalone/validation/tests/ -q

A few more standalone tests live in the plugin suite under tests/; run the two suites separately (see VALIDATION_GUIDE.md). Together they cover, among other things:

  • source extraction: engine-test sites emitted as their own source type (test_phase1b_extract_sources_standalone.py) and missing shapes_* tables skipped (tests/test_extract_sources_missing_tables.py)
  • the plugin-output gate: the CAEP14 reference and the standalone reproduce the pinned plugin CSVs (validation/data/plugin_output/) for all 15 movements and the three methods, within 2e-4 relative (test_plugin_csv_vs_reference.py; the measured agreement is in Tolerances)
  • the CAEP14 reference itself (test_caep14_bffm2_reference_case.py, test_caep14_reference_lookups.py, test_helicopter_caep14_reference.py)
  • engine-start emissions and gate_emissions_code (test_start_gate_code.py; plugin parity in tests/test_zz_gate_code_start_parity.py)
  • engine-test event extraction and emissions, all three thrust modes (test_phase3_engine_test_standalone.py)
  • single-engine taxi (taxi_engine_count, main engine start/off times, taxi_fuel_ratio) and its split over the route segments (test_single_engine_taxi_split.py; plugin parity of the movement totals and of each taxi segment in tests/test_zz_single_engine_taxi_parity.py)
  • runway placement of flight profiles and the segment Mach number (test_runway_placement.py, test_segment_mach.py)
  • the grid distribution: taxi split by segment time, helicopter helipad cell, vertical layer fractions below ground (test_taxi_split_by_segment_time.py, test_helicopter_helipad_standalone.py, test_iz_layer_fractions_below_ground.py)
  • the per-pollutant GeoPackages (inventory_gpkg): area, engine-test and point sources are gridded along with the others, and the GeoPackage total equals the emissions.parquet mass (test_inventory_gpkg_all_source_kinds.py)
  • an austal --include-aircraft run on training_v3.alaqs through austal_prep: per-hour e-files for the aircraft sources, per-pollutant spatial weights, mass conservation (tests/test_austal_prep_hybrid_mode.py)

Tests that need mod_spatialite (the CAEP14 reference) or a fixture that is not present are skipped with a message.

docs.title: Validation harness
docs.text:
openalaqs_standalone/validation/ is the CAEP14 reference harness. It is kept up to date with the standalone's calculation paths and is the canonical test for any change to the emission code; extend it whenever you add a new emission path or a new validation target. Three subdirectories:

  • validation/data/: bundled fixtures. Three derived variants of the training study (training_v3.alaqs, training_v3_gatemovements.alaqs, training_v3_multisource.alaqs) plus the plugin's own outputs on training_v3.alaqs for the four comparison targets (bymode, bymode-with-NOx-correction, bffm2_anchor, bffm2_traj) and the stationary sources in validation/data/plugin_output/, and training_validation_reference.xlsx, plugin beside the CAEP14 reference per movement. The training_v3* files are evolved versions of example/training/training.alaqs carrying schema fixes and source variants that exercise the gate / multi-source code paths. validation/data/source_csvs/ holds their text inputs: training_movements.csv is the movement table of training_v3.alaqs (and of training_v3_multisource.alaqs), 15 movements with the two AS50 helicopters, in the plugin's import format; training_v3_gatemovements.alaqs differs from it in the gate and gate_emissions_code of movements 1, 2, 3, 5 and 14. It is not the example's training_movements.csv (13 movements, other runways and gates on some rows). training_meteo.csv and training_ads_b_data.csv are the example's files. The only code that reads this folder is the test validation/tests/test_source_csvs_match_fixture.py, which checks that training_movements.csv equals the movement table of training_v3.alaqs.
  • validation/tests/: pytest modules, among them test_plugin_csv_vs_reference.py (plugin = reference = standalone on the 15 movements), test_bffm2_ambient_propagation_regression.py (BFFM2 EI with pinned ambient inputs), test_runway_placement.py and test_segment_mach.py.
  • validation/tools/: the CAEP14 reference and its helper scripts, described in CAEP14_VALIDATION.md (how to run the reference, regenerate the pinned outputs and the workbooks).

See also:

  • USAGE.md: install, commands and options
  • CAEP14_VALIDATION.md: the CAEP14 reference implementation
  • VALIDATION_GUIDE.md: validating a build
  • WITHOUT_QGIS.md: which tool to run without the QGIS GUI

docs.title: openalaqs_standalone usage
docs.text:
How to run openalaqs_standalone from a terminal, from a fresh checkout to a working AUSTAL input set: install, commands, options, config.json, time window, parallel runs and output folders. It is for users; the architecture, conventions and limitations are in the package README.

Contents:

  • Install
  • Where the official test fixture lives
  • The two subcommands at a glance
  • Per-movement emissions: aircraft
  • AUSTAL-ready folders: austal
  • Selecting the emission method
  • The NOx ambient correction
  • Aircraft-only output
  • Reading config.json
  • Parallel runs
  • Restricting the time window
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The package is shipped as a top-level directory in the Open-ALAQS repository and imports BFFM2, FOCA and runway-placement code from the plugin tree (open_alaqs/core/tools/), so run it from the repository root with the root on PYTHONPATH:

cd /path/to/openalaqs/
PYTHONPATH=. python -m openalaqs_standalone --help

Runtime dependencies are numpy, pandas, pyarrow (parquet), shapely, and pyproj. The package never imports QGIS, PyQt, or mod_spatialite.

docs.title: Quick smoke test
docs.text:
From the repository root, the official training fixture should run end-to-end in under a minute. Expected aircraft NOx total (13 movements, year 2025):

--method value NOx (kg) bymode 31.841 bymode + --apply-nox-corrections 30.698 bffm2_anchor 30.141 bffm2_traj 16.615

(CO 22.414 / 22.414 / 21.313 / 22.943 kg; the same with --aircraft-only, since the example has no gate, APU or start emissions.)

python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft \
    example/training/training_out.alaqs \
    --out totals.csv --method bymode

If your numbers differ by more than rounding, something is wrong with the install (most often a stale .alaqs schema that has not been migrated; run python scripts/migrate_alaqs.py example/training/training_out.alaqs first).

docs.title: Where the official test fixture lives
docs.text:
The canonical training study used by the User Guide and the validation harness ships at the repository root under example/training/:

example/training/
├── training.alaqs                          project file (geometry, sources,
│                                           study setup)
├── training_out.alaqs                      inventory output (produced by
│                                           Generate Emission Inventory
│                                           in the QGIS plugin)
├── training_movements.csv                  aircraft movements
├── training_meteo.csv                      hourly meteorology
├── training_ads_b_data.csv                 ADS-B tracks, imported into
│                                           the inventory (movement 11)
└── training_validation_reference.xlsx      reference values for a
                                            self-check after running

Movement 11 flies one of the ADS-B tracks (details).

Every example in this guide uses example/training/training_out.alaqs as its input. From the repository root:

ALAQS=example/training/training_out.alaqs

docs.title: The two subcommands at a glance
docs.text:
python -m openalaqs_standalone <command> <study.alaqs> [options]
Command Output Use when aircraft one CSV of per-movement totals you want a movement-by-movement emission table for analysis austal a six-folder structure ready for an external AUSTAL pipeline you want AUSTAL-ready inputs (sources + emissions + meteo + receptors + config)

The austal command can also fold the aircraft compute into the same output structure with --include-aircraft, giving you one run that covers both the stationary and the movement halves of the study.

docs.title: Per-movement emissions: aircraft
docs.text:
Smallest possible call:

python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft example/training/training_out.alaqs \
    --out movement_totals.csv

This writes movement_totals.csv with one row per movement, seven pollutant columns (co_kg, co2_kg, hc_kg, nox_kg, sox_kg, pm10_kg, pm25_kg), plus metadata (oid, aircraft, departure_arrival, profile_id, method).

Add --method to pick the emission method (Selecting the emission method), --processes N to parallelise (Parallel runs), or --oids 4,12,73 to compute only a subset of movements. --austal-out DIR also writes the AUSTAL emissions.parquet + sources.parquet pair for the aircraft sources alone:

python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft example/training/training_out.alaqs \
    --out movement_totals.csv \
    --austal-out ./austal_aircraft/

docs.title: AUSTAL-ready folders: austal
docs.text:
The stationary half reads the emission factors the plugin wrote into the .alaqs file; it does not compute them (see README).

Stationary half only:

python -m openalaqs_standalone austal example/training/training_out.alaqs \
    --year 2025 \
    --out ./inputs/

With the meteo year shifted and the receptors written in UTM zone 31N (EPSG:32631), for a Rotterdam road and parking study:

python -m openalaqs_standalone austal \
    EHRD_roadways_2025_final_with_parking.alaqs \
    --year 2025 \
    --meteo-year-shift 2025 \
    --receptor-target-epsg 32631 \
    --title "EHRD road and parking" \
    --out ./inputs/

Stationary + aircraft halves in one run:

python -m openalaqs_standalone austal example/training/training_out.alaqs \
    --year 2025 \
    --include-aircraft --aircraft-method bymode \
    --out ./inputs/

This computes the aircraft movement emissions (including the movement-driven gate emissions) and folds them into the same sources.parquet and emissions.parquet as the stationary sources.

The AUSTAL grid is read from the study's grid_3d_definition. Receptors outside that grid are dropped (with their IDs in the log); --grid-size/--grid-step override only this clipping square, not the AUSTAL grid.

--pollutants defaults to the full stationary set (co,hc,nox,sox,pm10,pm25); pass an explicit comma-separated list to narrow it. co2 is also accepted; it comes from the aircraft only (see README).

docs.title: Output folders
docs.text:
inputs/
├── sources_folder/
│   └── sources.parquet          one row per source; schema: source_id,
│                                source_type, label, geometry_wkt,
│                                geometry_kind, height_m, extent_m2,
│                                length_m, in_study, extra_json
│                                (+ delta_z_m when aircraft sources are included)
├── emissions_folder/
│   ├── emissions.parquet        one row per (source, pollutant, hour);
│   │                            schema: timestamp, source_id, pollutant,
│   │                            kg_in_hour
│   ├── co_emissions.gpkg, ...   one GeoPackage per pollutant, polygon
│   │                            features per inventory grid cell
│   └── runway_checks.csv        route and profile checks (only with
│                                --include-aircraft); never blocks the run
├── receptors_folder/
│   └── receptors.csv            schema: name, x, y, z (in target UTM)
├── meteo_folder/
│   └── meteo.csv                hourly meteorology; schema: timestamp,
│                                wind_direction_deg, wind_speed_ms,
│                                obukhov_length_m, mixing_height_m
├── config_folder/
│   └── config.json              AUSTAL writer settings + grid + flags
└── austal_folder/               (empty; filled by austal_prep)

The pair sources.parquet + emissions.parquet is the input contract that the sibling austal_prep package consumes to produce austal.txt + series.dmna + per-source grid files for an actual AUSTAL run. That step is python -m austal_prep (see python -m austal_prep --help and the docstring of austal_prep/__init__.py).

docs.title: Selecting the emission method
docs.text:
Three methods are supported, all from the same trajectory and EI database:

--method value Fuel flow source Ambient correction bymode EEDB mode-anchor fuel flow at the segment's mode None by default; opt in with --apply-nox-corrections bffm2_anchor EEDB mode-anchor fuel flow, BFFM2 EI on the log-log curve BFFM2 SAE AIR-5715 (built-in) bffm2_traj Per-segment trajectory fuel flow via twin-quadratic fit BFFM2 SAE AIR-5715 (built-in)

The BFFM2 ambient correction uses the study meteo in tbl_InvMeteo by default (--use-meteo), as the plugin does; --isa-meteo (austal: --use-isa-meteo) forces ISA, for comparison with runs made at ISA.

docs.title: Atmosphere aloft
docs.text:
The hourly meteo row is carried to each flight segment's height with --atmosphere-model (both subcommands):

Value Ambient at the segment's height standard_lapse (default) 2 m temperature and station pressure (from QNH and the airport elevation) carried up with the ISA lapse rate and the hydrostatic law; humidity ratio kept surface_layer AUSTAL 3.3 boundary-layer temperature profile from the hour's temperature, wind, Obukhov length and mixing height; pressure and humidity as above. Implied heat flux bounded at 600 / 100 W/m2 (unstable / stable), with a warning. 1 to 3 K too cold against the De Bilt radiosondes of 2025 ground_held the hourly row at every height, the ambient conditions of 5.4.0 (the fuel-flow scaling is not switched back, so 5.4.0 BFFM2 results are not reproduced)

Site parameters: --z0, --d0, --ha (m), the AUSTAL site parameters. Both subcommands share one default with the plugin's AUSTAL module and austal_prep (open_alaqs/core/tools/surface_layer_atmosphere.site_parameters): z0 0.1 m (the TA Luft value for airports), d0 6 z0 (0.6 m), ha 10 m + d0 (10.6 m); d0 and ha are derived from z0 when not given. aircraft uses them for surface_layer only; austal writes them to the AUSTAL config and uses them for the emissions alike. How to choose them: Site parameters. With --isa-meteo (or no meteo row) the ambient stays ISA at every height whatever the model. A meteo row whose temperature or pressure is not a positive number stops the run with a message naming its date.

Engine tests in the austal subcommand use the ICAO mode values, so the method and atmosphere options do not reach them (see README).

python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft $ALAQS --out totals.csv \
    --method bffm2_traj --atmosphere-model ground_held   # the 5.4.0 ambient conditions

Set the method on the aircraft subcommand:

python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft $ALAQS --out totals.csv \
    --method bffm2_traj

Set it on the austal subcommand (only takes effect with --include-aircraft):

python -m openalaqs_standalone austal $ALAQS --year 2025 --out ./inputs/ \
    --include-aircraft \
    --aircraft-method bffm2_traj

bymode is the default and matches the QGIS plugin's bymode path to floating-point noise (see Tolerances).

docs.title: The NOx ambient correction
docs.text:
The ICCAIA / CAEP/14 NOx ambient correction at takeoff (TO) and climb-out (CL) segments. It reads ambient temperature, pressure and humidity from tbl_InvMeteo per inventory period, plus airport elevation from user_study_setup. The tow_ratio column from user_aircraft_movements is used as a weight when set (defaults to 1.0; 0, negative or NaN is taken as 1.0, as in the plugin).

Default: off, as in the plugin, so the default bymode output matches the plugin's. Opt in with --apply-nox-corrections:

python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft $ALAQS --out totals.csv \
    --method bymode \
    --apply-nox-corrections

python -m openalaqs_standalone austal $ALAQS --year 2025 --out ./inputs/ \
    --include-aircraft --aircraft-method bymode \
    --apply-nox-corrections

The flag is only effective with --method bymode (or --aircraft-method bymode). BFFM2 methods always include their own ambient correction; the flag is ignored for them and for helicopter movements.

When you pass --apply-nox-corrections to the austal subcommand, the value is recorded in config.json under the key apply_nox_corrections (boolean) so downstream consumers can replicate the choice.

docs.title: Aircraft-only output
docs.text:
By default, the pollutant columns (co_kg ... pm25_kg) of the aircraft subcommand's per-movement CSV hold the movement total: the trajectory plus gate (GSE + GPU) plus APU plus engine-start contributions per movement (the "what flew this hour, including everything that came with it" total). This is the right quantity for inventory totals and for studies where the trajectory + ground services are reported together.

For comparison with the plugin (validations V2 and V5 of VALIDATION_GUIDE.md), add --aircraft-only to the aircraft subcommand:

python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft $ALAQS --out totals.csv \
    --method bymode --aircraft-only

With the flag set, the standalone subtracts the gate, APU and engine-start contributions from each pollutant column per movement before writing the CSV. The resulting value per pollutant is directly comparable to the plugin's source_type = "Movement" rows in its per-source emissions CSV (which contain trajectory contributions only; gate / APU / start emissions are emitted as separate source types on the plugin side).

The flag affects only the per-movement CSV writer and the on-screen study-totals summary (labeled (kg, aircraft-only) when the flag is set, otherwise (kg, total)). It has no effect on the austal subcommand's emissions.parquet output, which always uses the full movement total.

docs.title: Reading config.json
docs.text:
config.json, written into config_folder/, is the metadata file that any downstream AUSTAL pipeline reads. The aircraft and austal subcommands write it and do not read it; python -m austal_prep --config config.json reads the keys marked in the table. An example:

{
  "title": "Rotterdam",
  "qs": 3,
  "z0": 0.1,
  "d0": 0.6,
  "ha": 10.6,
  "os_options": "NOSTANDARD;NOTALUFT;SCINOTAT;Kmax=1",
  "mixing_height_included": true,
  "grid_writer_mode": "hybrid",
  "source_offset_cells": 2,
  "max_receptors": 20,
  "source_aggregation": "by_type_per_pollutant",
  "apply_nox_corrections": false,
  "atmosphere_model": "standard_lapse",
  "grid": {
    "dd": 250.0,
    "nx": 104,
    "ny": 104,
    "x0": -13000.0,
    "y0": -13000.0,
    "sk": [0, 3, 6, 10, 16, 25, 40, 65, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500,
           600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1500],
    "reference_x": 599065.0372562435,
    "reference_y": 5757284.894734611,
    "utm_epsg": 32631
  },
  "selected_pollutants": ["co", "hc", "nox", "sox", "pm10", "pm25"],
  "start_dt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00",
  "end_dt": "2025-12-31T23:00:00"
}
Key Effect qs AUSTAL quality level (read by austal_prep) z0 roughness length (m); default 0.1 (TA Luft, airports) d0 displacement height (m); null or absent = 6 z0 ha anemometer height (m) for the roughness z0; null or absent = 10 m + d0 os_options AUSTAL os line (read by austal_prep) mixing_height_included feed mixing-height column to AUSTAL meteo (read by austal_prep) grid_writer_mode hybrid (default: one e-file per hour for aircraft sub-sources, one time-invariant e-file for stationary sources), time_indexed (one time-invariant e-file for all) or legacy (per-hour files for all) source_offset_cells offset of the source origin from the grid origin, in cells (2; read by austal_prep) max_receptors cap on the number of receptor points (20; null: no cap; read by austal_prep) source_aggregation by_type_per_pollutant (recommended), by_type (legacy) or none (one AUSTAL source per input source); read by austal_prep apply_nox_corrections record of the --apply-nox-corrections choice; not read by any command (the emissions in emissions.parquet already include it) atmosphere_model record of the --atmosphere-model choice (standard_lapse by default); not read by any command (as above) selected_pollutants pollutants of the run; not read by austal_prep, which takes --pollutants (default: all in emissions.parquet) grid.* AUSTAL calc grid: cell size, count, origin, vertical layers, ref pt (read by austal_prep) start_dt / end_dt run window (from --year or --start/--end); not read by austal_prep, which takes --start / --end

python -m austal_prep reads title, qs, z0, d0, ha, os_options, pm10_fine_fraction, mixing_height_included, grid_writer_mode (time_indexed when absent), source_height, source_offset_cells, max_receptors, source_aggregation, processes and grid.*. It ignores the other keys: it writes AUSTAL inputs from emissions already computed.

The emission method (bymode, bffm2_anchor, bffm2_traj) is not stored in config.json; it is a runtime CLI flag only. Pick it via --aircraft-method each time you run.

Override defaults at the command line; make_config.py is also callable as a Python function if you want to script the config generation:

from openalaqs_standalone.make_config import make_config
from pathlib import Path

make_config(
    Path("example/training/training_out.alaqs"),
    Path("./inputs/config_folder/config.json"),
    title="EHRD training",
    year=2025,
    apply_nox_corrections=True,
)

docs.title: Parallel runs
docs.text:
--processes N (N > 1) runs the aircraft movement compute across a process pool; the results are bit-identical to the serial driver. On the austal subcommand it takes effect only with --include-aircraft. The stationary compute is already numpy-vectorised and is not parallelised.

# 4 worker processes
python -m openalaqs_standalone aircraft $ALAQS --out totals.csv --processes 4

python -m openalaqs_standalone austal $ALAQS --year 2025 --out ./inputs/ \
    --include-aircraft --processes 4

Worth it for studies with hundreds or thousands of movements; not worth it for the training study.

docs.title: Restricting the time window
docs.text:
The austal subcommand accepts --start and --end (ISO format) to restrict the run to a window inside the inventory year:

python -m openalaqs_standalone austal $ALAQS \
    --year 2025 --out ./inputs/ \
    --include-aircraft \
    --start 2025-12-01 --end 2025-12-02

The window is half-open [start, end). Behaviour:

  • Stationary sources: hourly emissions are filtered to the window. The per-hour mass for kept hours is unchanged, so conservation against the same-hours slice of the full-year output holds exactly.
  • Aircraft sources: a movement is included if its start time is in the window, using block_time for departures and runway_time for arrivals (the direction-aware rule); for movements that straddle the window boundary, the per-segment emissions are also clipped to the window so the run only contains emissions that physically occur in [start, end). This is the dispersion-correct interpretation.
  • Meteo and config: meteo.csv is trimmed to the window; config.json's start_dt / end_dt reflect the window bounds.

The CLI rejects windows outside the inventory year (start must be in [year-01-01, year+1-01-01)) and start >= end.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'open_alaqs.core.tools.bffm2': the standalone imports BFFM2 from the QGIS plugin tree. Run from the repository root with PYTHONPATH=..

shapely.errors.GEOSException on a particular movement: likely a self-intersecting taxi route in the source .alaqs. Identify the offending oid via --oids bisection; fix the geometry in the plugin or strip the movement.

apply_nox_corrections had no effect: check that --method (or --aircraft-method) is bymode. The flag is silently ignored for BFFM2 methods (which include their own ambient correction) and for helicopter movements.

Output emissions.parquet is empty: usually means instudy is not '1' (for example '0') on every source, or a time window with no movements. Run with --year only first to confirm the study has emissions, then narrow.

See also:

  • README: architecture, conventions and limitations of the package
  • WITHOUT_QGIS.md: which tool to run without the QGIS GUI
  • DISPERSION_AUSTAL.md: running AUSTAL and reading its results
  • TROUBLESHOOTING.md: problems with the plugin

docs.title: CAEP14 reference validation
docs.text:
This page describes the CAEP14 reference implementation of the OpenALAQS aircraft emission calculations in this directory: what it implements, how it is run, and how it and the pinned plugin outputs are updated. It is for maintainers. What to run to validate a build, and how to judge the result, is in VALIDATION_GUIDE.md; the measured agreement is in its Tolerances section.

The reference covers the three calculation methods (bymode, bffm2_anchor, bffm2_traj), fixed-wing aircraft and helicopters. The training study is the canonical fixture: its inventory validation/data/training_v3.alaqs (15 movements, two helicopters included) for the pinned outputs, and example/training/training_out.alaqs (13 movements) for the user-facing workbook; the scripts work against any OpenALAQS inventory (_out.alaqs) database.

Contents:

  • Files
  • Running the reference
  • Updating the reference and the pinned outputs
  • Methods covered by the reference
  • Ambient conditions: ISA vs tbl_InvMeteo
  • Movement 11 (PHBBA, CUSTOM track)
  • Reference vs plugin: data flow
  • What the CAEP/14 reference cases cover
  • Use on other studies

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
File Purpose compute_caep14_reference.py The reference implementation. Produces per-movement CO, CO₂, HC, NOₓ, SOₓ, PM₁₀ totals for one method and either prints a table or compares against a plugin CSV. Flags: --method (bymode, bffm2_anchor, bffm2_traj; default bymode), --use-meteo (study meteo instead of ISA), --plugin-csv, --oid (one movement), --apply-nox-corrections (bymode: ICCAIA NOx correction on take-off and climb-out), --atmosphere-model (surface_layer, standard_lapse, ground_held; default standard_lapse), --z0, --d0, --ha (site parameters in m for surface_layer; empty gives 0.1, 6 z0, 10 m + d0), --verbose-diag. regenerate_plugin_csvs.py Runs the plugin's calculation service headlessly (QGIS bindings, no GUI) on the fixture, all source types, for the three methods and for bymode with the NOx correction, and writes the pinned CSVs (training_movements_*.csv, training_sources_bymode.csv). regenerate_training_validation_xlsx.py Reads the pinned plugin CSVs and runs the reference for the three methods and the NOx-correction run, then writes data/training_validation_reference.xlsx: plugin beside reference per movement, hourly plugin emissions of movements and stationary sources, the helicopter parameters. compare_inventory_to_reference.py Diffs an exported per-movement CSV (QGIS Table View, or the pinned files) against the reference column of the workbook for one method; the installation check of V1 in documents/validation/VALIDATION_GUIDE.md. Usage: compare_inventory_to_reference.py <csv> --method=bymode [<workbook.xlsx>] (default workbook example/training/training_validation_reference.xlsx). The method is accepted only in the --method=bymode form; --method bymode (with a space) is read as a file path. ../tests/test_bffm2_ambient_propagation_regression.py Pure-Python pytest module that pins the BFFM2 ambient-correction behaviour (ISA, cold-dry, warm-humid, per-segment Mach) so a future change in core/tools/bffm2.py will surface immediately.

The reference is dependency-light: it requires numpy, shapely, pyproj and openpyxl (the last only for the xlsx-regen script). It does not import QGIS and runs in any standard Python 3.12 environment.

docs.title: Running the reference
docs.text:
From the repository root, against the pinned plugin CSVs:

PYTHONPATH=. python3 openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/compute_caep14_reference.py \
    openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3.alaqs --method=bymode \
    --plugin-csv=openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/plugin_output/training_movements_bymode.csv

PYTHONPATH=. python3 openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/compute_caep14_reference.py \
    openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3.alaqs --method=bffm2_anchor --use-meteo \
    --plugin-csv=openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/plugin_output/training_movements_bffm2_anchor.csv

PYTHONPATH=. python3 openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/compute_caep14_reference.py \
    openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3.alaqs --method=bffm2_traj --use-meteo \
    --plugin-csv=openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/plugin_output/training_movements_bffm2_traj.csv

--use-meteo because the plugin applies tbl_InvMeteo (see Ambient conditions); bymode without the NOx correction has no ambient correction.

Each invocation prints a per-movement table with CO, CO₂, NOₓ and PM₁₀ from both reference (_ref) and plugin (_plg) plus a Δ% column. For this version every movement of training_v3.alaqs, movement 11 (PHBBA, CUSTOM) included, shows 0.00 % for all three methods; the measured differences are in Tolerances. tests/test_plugin_csv_vs_reference.py pins this (plugin against reference and standalone, 15 movements, the three methods and bymode with the NOx correction). Any plugin-vs-reference delta larger than these is a regression and should be investigated before release.

docs.title: Updating the reference and the pinned outputs
docs.text: The files in data/plugin_output/ are written by tools/regenerate_plugin_csvs.py, which runs the plugin's EmissionCalculatorService (the code path of the QGIS dialog) without a display: the three methods, bymode with the ICCAIA NOx correction (training_movements_bymode_nox_corr.csv) and the stationary-source rows (training_sources_bymode.csv), all with the study meteo. The workbook data/training_validation_reference.xlsx is rebuilt from them.

docs.title: Re-export the pinned plugin CSVs
docs.text:
Headless (the pinned files were made this way, with the QGIS Python bindings and no display):

QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3.12 \
    openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/regenerate_plugin_csvs.py

Or in QGIS: run Visualize Emission Calculation on openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3.alaqs with each of the three calculation methods and once with bymode and Apply NOx Corrections on, and export the per-movement emissions to CSV as in V1 of VALIDATION_GUIDE.md. Save them as training_movements_bymode.csv, training_movements_bffm2_anchor.csv, training_movements_bffm2_traj.csv and training_movements_bymode_nox_corr.csv (the file names the regen script expects by default). Only source_name and the *_kg columns are read; rows of one movement are summed.

On training_v3.alaqs the plugin runs with the inventory grid of the file, 50 × 50 × 20 cells of 250 × 250 × 50 m, mixing height 914.4 m (3000 ft), apply-NOₓ-corrections off (on for the _nox_corr file), and the bffm2_ff_source set to trajectory (the CAEP/14 default).

docs.title: Regenerate the validation workbooks
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=. python3 openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/regenerate_training_validation_xlsx.py

Reads the pinned plugin CSVs, runs the reference with the study meteo, and writes data/training_validation_reference.xlsx (sheets README, Summary, Movement, NOx_correction, Movement_Hourly, the four stationary-source sheets, Helicopter). The user-facing copy example/training/training_validation_reference.xlsx is made the same way from example/training/training_out.alaqs (13 movements, no helicopters). That inventory is itself rebuilt from training.alaqs and the example's CSVs (movements, meteo, ADS-B) with the settings of documents/user/TUTORIAL_ROTTERDAM.md:

QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3.12 tools/test_fixtures/rebuild_training_example_inventory.py
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3.12 openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/regenerate_plugin_csvs.py \
    --fixture example/training/training_out.alaqs --out-dir /tmp/ex
PYTHONPATH=. python3 openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/regenerate_training_validation_xlsx.py \
    --fixture example/training/training_out.alaqs --plugin-dir /tmp/ex \
    --out example/training/training_validation_reference.xlsx

The agreement of plugin and reference on that inventory is listed in Tolerances; this check is not part of the test suite.

docs.title: Run the regression test
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=. pytest openalaqs_standalone/validation/tests/test_bffm2_ambient_propagation_regression.py -v

Five tests must pass. These pin the BFFM2 module's ambient-condition plumbing against ISA / cold-dry / warm-humid / per-segment-Mach inputs and against the exact dict shape that Engine.getEmissionIndexByFuelFlow builds from method["config"]["ambient_conditions"].

docs.title: When a plugin change shifts the reference
docs.text:
If a future plugin change is intentional and shifts the reference output (e.g. a new CAEP edition, a different installation correction default, a fix in twin_quadratic_fit_method.py), the workflow is:

  1. Make the same change in compute_caep14_reference.py (and add a short comment pointing at the plugin commit hash that motivated it).
  2. When the plugin result itself changes, re-export the pinned plugin CSVs first (Re-export the pinned plugin CSVs). Then re-run the three invocations of Running the reference and confirm that 15 of 15 movements still match to 0.00 %; tests/test_plugin_csv_vs_reference.py checks this.
  3. Regenerate the validation workbooks.
  4. Update the pinned values in tests/test_bffm2_ambient_propagation_regression.py if BFFM2 itself was the change; otherwise the test should keep passing unchanged.
  5. Add a one-line entry to CHANGELOG.md recording the validation result.

docs.title: bymode
docs.text: CAEP14 LTO-mode look-up: per-segment fuel flow is the EEDB anchor for the segment's mode label (TX/AP/CL/TO) and the EI is taken directly from the engine's EEDB row. Identical to the plugin's bymode path once both apply identical grid-clipping, vertical clipping at 914.4 m + 1 µm tolerance, and identical brake-wear PM₁₀ for arrivals above 18 632 kg MTOW.

docs.title: bffm2_anchor
docs.text:
Fuel flow stays at the mode anchor as in bymode; the EI for NOₓ / CO / HC is replaced by the BFFM2-ambient EI computed at the anchor fuel flow with the segment's ambient conditions. Per-segment Mach is the flight Mach, start-point TAS over the speed of sound at the ambient temperature. PM₁₀ and SOₓ stay at the table EI.

The speed of sound is a = √(γ R T) with γ = 1.4 and R = 287.05287 J/(kg K) (ICAO Doc 7488), as in the CAEP/14 BFFM2 formulation. The plugin and the standalone share open_alaqs/core/tools/bffm2.py::speed_of_sound_m_s; the reference writes the formula out. test_segment_mach.py reproduces the two Mach values of the CAEP/14 reference cases to 10⁻⁹ (with their rounded 1.94384 kt per m/s).

docs.title: bffm2_traj
docs.text:
Per-segment fuel flow is resolved either from fuel_flow_kgm (CUSTOM / ADS-B profiles, divided by engine_count; above ADSB_FF_CEILING_FACTOR = 1.5 × the TO anchor fuel flow the segment falls back to the anchor fuel flow of its mode, as in the plugin) or from the segment's power setting via the piecewise three-point quadratic fit from core/tools/twin_quadratic_fit_method.py, then scaled to ambient fuel flow with the corrected-parameter scaling of gas-turbine performance (the corrected fuel flow, fuel flow / (δ √θ), is a function of the corrected thrust, thrust / δ, and Mach):

Wf_amb = Wf_ref * δ * sqrt(θ)

δ and θ (and the Mach number and the BFFM2 ambient corrections) are those at the segment's start height, from the period's meteo row with the atmosphere model of the plugin (--atmosphere-model, default standard_lapse: the row's 2 m temperature and station pressure, from QNH, carried up with the ISA lapse rate; surface_layer: AUSTAL's boundary-layer temperature profile; ground_held: the hourly row at every height, the ambient conditions of 5.4.0, not its fuel-flow scaling). The reference, the standalone and the plugin share open_alaqs/core/tools/surface_layer_atmosphere.py; the surface_layer formulas are checked against AUSTAL's C code in tests/test_surface_layer_atmosphere.py. The pinned outputs use the default standard_lapse. The shared site defaults are z0 0.1 m, d0 0.6 m, ha 10.6 m, used by surface_layer only.

BFFM2 (SAE AIR5715) converts a known fuel flow to reference conditions for the emission-index lookup; it is not a fuel-flow model, and its inverse, Wf_ref * δ / θ^3.8 / exp(0.2 M^2), is not used to scale the fuel flow to ambient (it lowers the fuel flow with rising temperature, −12 % at 25 °C, where the corrected-parameter scaling gives +1.7 %). The CAEP/14 reference cases take the fuel flow as an input and do not test this step.

EI for NOₓ / CO / HC is then the BFFM2-ambient EI at that ambient fuel flow. PM₁₀ and SOₓ remain at the table EI.

Only a positive fuel_flow_kgm is a fuel flow; zero or negative is taken as missing. A power between 1.0 and 1.05 is taken as 1.0. A segment without a positive fuel flow whose power is missing, above 1.05 or below 0 (piston and propeller profiles, whose power column is not a thrust fraction) takes the bymode index of its mode (EEDB fuel flow, unscaled), as in the plugin.

The reference's _twin_quadratic_ff_from_power reimplements the plugin's piecewise three-point quadratic (parabola through 0.07 / 0.30 / 0.85 below 85 % thrust, through 0.30 / 0.85 / 1.00 above) bit-for-bit. A least-squares fit through the four points instead gives NOₓ deltas of about 0.7 % on E190 arrivals.

docs.title: Taxi (BFFM2 methods)
docs.text: With bffm2_anchor and bffm2_traj the taxi reference fuel flow is the twin-quadratic fit at the movement's engine_thrust_level_for_taxiing (0.07 when it is not given, so the EEDB idle fuel flow; 0 is floored at idle), scaled to ambient, ff_ref · δ · √θ (Mach 0), and that ambient fuel flow is used for both the taxi fuel mass and the BFFM2 EI lookup: in the plugin (TaxiingEmissionCalculator calls Engine.getEmissionIndexByEngineState(power_setting, method=BFFM2) without a fuel_flow argument, which takes the power-setting branch), in the standalone (compute_aircraft.compute_fixed_wing) and in the reference (compute_caep14_reference._compute_fixed_wing). A thrust the fit rejects (above 1.05 or below 0, e.g. 7 typed for 7 %) gives the bymode TX index (EEDB TX fuel flow, unscaled, and TX indices), with an error in the log.

docs.title: Vertical limit
docs.text: The vertical clip uses the mixing height of the movement's period, from the meteo row nearest to the period start; the reference (_mixing_height_at), the standalone (movements.get_mixing_height_at()) and the plugin use the same row and the same 914.4 m when there is no mixing height (LTO ceiling). A segment with one endpoint below and one above the limit is cut where it meets the limit (altitude linear along the segment), so only the part below the limit counts. On the training fixture at 914.4 m every crossing segment lies outside the 50 × 50 grid. Tests: tests/test_height_limit_crossing_segment.py (plugin) and validation/tests/test_crossing_segment_standalone.py (standalone = reference, also at a 300 m limit; analytic crossing distance).

docs.title: NOx ambient correction (bymode)
docs.text: The ICCAIA NOx ambient correction (Apply NOx Corrections) applies to the take-off and climb-out segments only, the modes the simple method is defined for: in the plugin (NOX_CORRECTION_MODES in MovementEmissionCalculator), the standalone and the reference (--apply-nox-corrections, _nox_ambient_factor, written out from Doc 9889 with the pressure in hPa). It reads the study's airport elevation as the airport altitude (−5 m on the fixture). Plugin = reference = standalone on 15 of 15 movements (test_plugin_csv_vs_reference.py).

docs.title: MEEM V1 above 3000 ft
docs.text: Above 3000 ft above the aerodrome the reference's _meem_v1_mass_mgkg runs the MEEM V1 ISA + ΔT atmosphere, with ΔT as defined in MEEM V1 (_meem_delta_t); the plugin (Engine.getEmissionIndexByModeWithMEEM, delta_t) and the standalone (compute_aircraft._meem_v1_segment_ei) do the same with meem_v1.delta_t_from_ground. That is the ground_held case; with standard_lapse or surface_layer all three pass the segment's local T and p instead (the reference through its ambient argument). For bymode the reference and the standalone read the meteo row when the engine has MEEM inputs. validation/tests/test_meem_v1_reference.py checks both against two MEEM V1 reference cases (11GE144, ΔT −5.1825 K and +12 K). training_v3 has no segment above 3000 ft (mixing height 914.4 m); the example inventory training_out.alaqs has (1500 m mixing height on 2 December). The engine table carries press_ratio and the 5th nvPM point from ICAO EEDB v31 (ACT_PRF for engines not in it), and nvpm_number_ei in #/kg; the reference reads press_ratio and the 5th mass point.

docs.title: Helicopters (oid 14, 15)
docs.text: FOCA 2015 Appendix A is used identically for all three methods (FOCA does not go through BFFM2). The reference re-uses the plugin's own core/tools/foca_heli.py / foca_heli_utils.py modules to guarantee that any future change to the FOCA implementation is picked up by the validation without separate maintenance. The active mode (TO or AP) is scaled by the share of its time below the period's mixing height and inside the grid on the FOCA flight path (origin at the gate centroid, else the runway threshold; departure outbound along the runway, arrival back along the approach). The reference builds that path and the cut on its own from the parameters in core/tools/foca_heli_trajectory.py (_heli_flight_path_local, _heli_active_fraction); tests/test_helicopter_caep14_reference.py checks it against the standalone at 914.4, 600, 300 and 100 m, with and without a helipad gate. The arrival (movement 15) starts its approach outside the 50 × 50 grid, so the cut matters there. The reference equals the plugin on the fixture at 914.4 m without gates and at 300 m with gate G4 as helipad (0.00 % on 15 of 15 for bymode), and the standalone at 914.4, 600, 300 and 100 m with and without a gate (see Tolerances).

docs.title: Ambient conditions: ISA vs tbl_InvMeteo
docs.text:
The reference defaults to ISA conditions (T = 288.15 K, P = 101 325 Pa, RH = 0.6) for the BFFM2 ambient correction. The plugin applies the study meteo, so pass --use-meteo to read the meteo row at each movement's runway_time from tbl_InvMeteo (the pinned exports need it):

PYTHONPATH=. python3 openalaqs_standalone/validation/tools/compute_caep14_reference.py \
    openalaqs_standalone/validation/data/training_v3.alaqs \
    --method=bffm2_anchor \
    --use-meteo

Run at ISA, the BFFM2 methods and the NOx-corrected run move off the pinned files; the size of the difference is in Effect of the meteo setting.

Two fallback paths in the plugin make BFFM2 revert to ISA; both log a WARNING:

  1. EmissionCalculation.__init__ when tbl_InvMeteo is empty: _sorted_ac_times = [] makes getAmbientCondition() return AmbientCondition() (ISA defaults) for every time slice.
  2. Engine.getEmissionIndexByFuelFlow when the ambient extraction raises an exception: the surrounding except Exception substitutes ISA.

If a future plugin run produces output that disagrees with the --use-meteo reference but agrees with the default reference, search the QGIS log for these warnings to identify whether the meteo store is empty, the extraction failed for a specific row, or the data is otherwise unavailable.

docs.title: Movement 11 (PHBBA, CUSTOM track)
docs.text:
Movement 11 (A20N CUSTOM departure on runway 24, gate G2) flies the ADS-B track 1764584438_PHBBA from data/source_csvs/training_ads_b_data.csv. The fixture's PHBBA and PHRTM rows are imported with the current importer (tier 1: reference point from the movement's runway and taxi route): heights above the airport elevation (−5 m) and the take-off roll at height 0 with mode TO. The track stays below the 914.4 m cut. PHRTM is not used by any movement.

The fuel_flow column of the track is 2 × the ICAO fuel flow of 01P20CM128 (the A20N engine of movement 11) interpolated linearly on its four (thrust, fuel flow) points at the row's power_setting, rounded to 4 decimals: 0.65 to 1.57 kg/s for PHBBA (PHRTM gets the same curve, with its power below idle raised to 0.07). The tracks are an example, not measured fuel flows. Only bffm2_traj uses the supplied fuel flow; the values stay below 1.5 × the take-off fuel flow per engine (0.78 against 1.29 kg/s), so no point falls back to the mode anchor.

docs.title: Reference vs plugin: data flow
docs.text:
training_v3.alaqs / <study>_out.alaqs (sqlite inventory)
          │
          │  read engine EI, trajectories, taxi route, meteo
          ▼
   compute_caep14_reference.py
          │
          ├── grid clip in EPSG:3857 (grid_3d_definition; 50×50 cells of 250 m on training_v3)
          ├── vertical clip at 914.4 m ±1 µm
          ├── runway alignment via pyproj.Geod
          ├── ANP arrivals: landing threshold + Touchdown Offset, rollout cut at the route exit
          ├── ANP departures: brake release at the line-up point
          ├── CUSTOM tracks: runway/taxi intersection via Shapely buffer(1 m)
          ├── per-segment fuel/time/EI per method
          ├── brake-wear PM10 for arrivals > 18 632 kg MTOW
          ├── FOCA Appendix A for helicopters
          └── BFFM2 EI via core/tools/bffm2.py (NOx/CO/HC)
          │
          ▼
   per-movement totals  vs  plugin CSV totals  → Δ%

Every spatial primitive in the reference is verified against the plugin's own implementation to sub-millimetre precision (runway alignment to 0.08 m, intersection point to 0.0000 m, grid bounds to 0.0004 m at x_max). See the file-level docstrings in compute_caep14_reference.py for line-by-line traceability to the plugin sources it mirrors.

docs.title: What the CAEP/14 reference cases cover
docs.text:
The CAEP/14 BFFM2 reference cases take the engine fuel flow as an input and give the BFFM2 reference fuel flow and the ambient emission indices; their results are reproduced in the tests. Note on independence: the reference implementation writes out the geometry, the fuel-flow step, the taxi, the NOx correction and the helicopter cut on its own, but imports the plugin's BFFM2 index function (open_alaqs.core.tools.bffm2.calculate_emission_index) and the FOCA helicopter tables (foca_heli, foca_heli_utils). Those two parts are what the CAEP/14 reference cases and the FOCA Appendix A values check, not the plugin-vs-reference comparison. It has no view on how a fuel flow is derived from a thrust: that step is validated against the reference implementation, as the rest of the method; the index step is pinned to the CAEP/14 reference cases.

  • tests/test_caep14_bffm2_reference_case.py: BFFM2 index step against two CAEP/14 reference cases for engine 01P20CM127 (LEAP-1A24) at fuel flow 1.1749 kg/s. The worked case, climb to cruise at 22 500 ft (non-LTO, lean burn: v2 indices, exponent 0.3): reference fuel flow 1.657227 kg/s, EI NOx 60.20166, CO 0.459531, HC 0.0282788 g/kg. The LTO path (standard indices, exponent 0.5), the same engine and fuel flow at altitude 1 000 ft, CLIMB OUT, 180 kt: reference fuel flow 1.204590 kg/s, EI NOx 17.65248, CO 0.329654, HC 0.0202864 g/kg. The code matches CO and HC to 1e-14 and NOx to 2e-6 from RH (the humidity ratio formula), exactly with the reference cases' humidity ratio.

docs.title: Use on other studies
docs.text:
The reference matches engines on engine_name exactly (or engine_full_name for rows without an engine_name), the key of the plugin and the standalone, and treats a movement as a helicopter when its aircraft type is listed in default_helicopter, as the plugin and the standalone do (a study may give its helicopters a profile, HELIPROF-*). On an operational study of 159 movements and 33 engines (jets, turboprops, pistons, EC35 helicopters, 77 CUSTOM profiles; study meteo) it equals the standalone net of the gate emissions (APU, GSE, engine start, which the reference does not model) to floating-point noise, with one ANP departure of bffm2_traj as the exception; the figures are in Tolerances. This check is not part of the test suite.

See also:

  • VALIDATION_GUIDE.md: what to run to validate a build, and the tolerances
  • AIRCRAFT_EMISSIONS.md: the aircraft emission methods
  • HELICOPTERS.md: the FOCA 2015 helicopter method
  • openalaqs_standalone README: the standalone's tests

docs.title: Command-line scripts
docs.text:
The command-line utilities in scripts/, for Open-ALAQS users and maintainers: what each one does, and the usage of migrate_alaqs.py and import_engine_test_events.py. None of them are invoked by the plugin at run time; they produce or transform the files that the plugin reads. Which of them need the QGIS Python is in WITHOUT_QGIS.md.

Contents:

  • Inventory
  • metar_to_alaqs_meteo.py
  • migrate_alaqs.py
  • import_engine_test_events.py
  • migrate_alaqs_gui.py

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text: File Purpose When to run metar_to_alaqs_meteo.py Parse METAR observations into the meteo.csv format Open-ALAQS expects during Calculate Emissions Inventory. Once per study, before inventory creation, to produce the hourly meteorology file. migrate_alaqs.py Upgrade a legacy .alaqs file to the current schema. Whenever a user brings a .alaqs produced by an older plugin version and needs to open it with the current one. migrate_alaqs_gui.py Qt5 GUI wrapper around migrate_alaqs.py. Exposes every CLI flag plus a live log panel; useful for users uncomfortable with the command line. Same situations as migrate_alaqs.py, when a GUI is preferred. Run with QGIS's bundled Python (e.g. C:\PROGRA~1\QGIS34~1.13\bin\python.exe migrate_alaqs_gui.py). import_engine_test_events.py Bulk-load engine run-up events from a CSV into the engine_test_events table. After creating test-site area sources (is_test_site='1') but before generating the emission inventory. austal_from_csv/ [BETA] Standalone CLI that produces AUSTAL dispersion-model input files from pre-computed emissions and meteo CSVs (no .alaqs needed). See austal_from_csv/README.md. When you already have emissions/meteo CSVs and want AUSTAL inputs. emissions_austal/ [BETA] Standalone CLI that runs the full emissions calculation against a .alaqs inventory and optionally generates AUSTAL inputs in one pass. See emissions_austal/README.md. When you want to run the calculator headlessly from an OSGeo4W shell.

docs.title: metar_to_alaqs_meteo.py
docs.text:
Converts a stream of METAR observations into meteo.csv with the columns Open-ALAQS reads during Calculate Emissions Inventory. See README_metar_to_alaqs_meteo.md for the input formats, METAR parsing, stability classification, options and limitations; the meteo.csv format itself is in INPUT_FORMATS.md.

Quick example:

python3 scripts/metar_to_alaqs_meteo.py \
    --station EHRD \
    --start 2025-12-01T06:00 \
    --end   2025-12-03T09:00 \
    --scenario "AIRPORT_A training" \
    --input  metar_rotterdam_dec_1_3.txt \
    --output AIRPORT_A_meteo.csv

Network access is not required: METAR fetching is deliberately left to the caller (curl, wget, a Python poller, python-metar, etc.). This keeps the parsing half usable on machines behind restrictive network policies.

docs.title: migrate_alaqs.py
docs.text: Two-phase migration tool for upgrading legacy .alaqs files to the current schema.

docs.title: Phase 1: schema migration (always runs unless --skip-schema)
docs.text:
Diffs the source schema against the appropriate canonical template and applies the diff inside a transaction.

The reference template is auto-selected by source filename:

  • *_out.alaqs → open_alaqs/core/templates/inventory.alaqs
  • everything else → open_alaqs/core/templates/project.alaqs

Pass --reference PATH to override the auto-selection.

What Phase 1 handles:

Case Default behaviour Override Table in REFERENCE but not in SOURCE CREATE TABLE using REFERENCE's schema (empty table). none Table in SOURCE but not in REFERENCE Reported as "extra"; left in place. --drop-extra-tables to remove. Column in REFERENCE but not in SOURCE ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN with REFERENCE's declared type, NULL default. none Column in SOURCE but not in REFERENCE Reported as "extra"; left in place. --drop-extra-columns to remove: ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN (SQLite 3.35 or later), which keeps the table's keys, NOT NULL, defaults, indexes and triggers; where SQLite refuses it, the table is rebuilt with the REFERENCE definitions of the kept columns (source order, rowids kept) and its indexes and triggers are recreated. Numeric column of a shapes_* layer declared REAL in REFERENCE and otherwise in SOURCE (DECIMAL in studies made with 5.3.x: height, speed, distance, idle_time, temperature, diameter, velocity, the *_percentage columns, vehicle_year, the emission factors, gate_height, taxiway speed and time, receptor xcoord, ycoord) Converted (plan line ~ RETYPE): the table is rebuilt with the REFERENCE definitions (source column order, rowids, keys, defaults, indexes and geometry triggers kept) and the values are kept numerically; a text value that reads as a number ("2.5", "30,3") becomes that number, an empty text becomes NULL, any other text (for example Calculated in the unused taxiway time of old studies, or "1,234", which is 1.234 with a decimal comma but a grouped 1234) is reported on stderr, once per column with the count and three examples (WARNING: <table>.<column>: <n> value(s) are not numbers and are left as text: ...), and left as it is. Why: the QGIS SpatiaLite provider types a DECIMAL column from its stored data (integer when the values are whole numbers, text when the layer is empty), so a decimal typed in a form was rounded (2.5 saved as 3, 25 under a German locale) or stored as text; a REAL column is typed Double. none QGIS layer statistics of a rebuilt shapes_* table, or statistics that type a REAL column of a shapes_* layer as integer or text (geometry_columns_field_infos, written by QGIS each time a layer is edited; a study retyped by the 5.4.0 script kept them) Removed (with the rebuild, or plan line ~ STATISTICS). Why: when these rows exist QGIS types the fields from them, not from the declared column types, so a retyped column stayed an integer or text field, the forms kept refusing a decimal ("Upgrade the study with scripts/migrate_alaqs.py") and the study kept logging the unmigrated warning. Without the rows QGIS types REAL as Double and recomputes the statistics on its next edit; the layer's extent and row count (geometry_columns_statistics) are kept. none Other type/affinity differences on common columns Warned, never auto-rewritten (SQLite is dynamically typed). none Virtual tables (SpatialIndex, KNN2, ElementaryGeometries) Filtered from both sides of the diff (they need the SpatiaLite extension to introspect; the runtime recreates them). none

Registered data-preserving transforms are run for special rename pairs. The one currently registered is the legacy 1D axial default_aircraft_profiles schema (horizontal_metres, vertical_metres) → 3D Cartesian (x_m, y_m = 0, z_m). Add new entries to the RENAMES dict at the top of the script as the schema evolves.

docs.title: Phase 2: reference-data refresh (opt-in via --refresh-reference-data)
docs.text:
Replaces the contents of selected reference tables with the rows from the matching CSV in --data-dir (default: open_alaqs/database/data/). DELETE + INSERT, not merge. Skipped by default.

The default --refresh-tables list contains 9 "safe" reference tables (externally maintained, users rarely customize):

default_airports, default_vehicle_ef_copert5,
default_vehicle_fleet_euro_standards, default_aircraft_engine_mode,
default_stationary_category, default_stationary_substance,
default_stationary_ef, default_emission_dynamics, default_apu_times

Pass --refresh-include-user-extensible to also refresh the 8 user-extensible tables (default_aircraft, default_aircraft_engine_ei, default_aircraft_profiles, default_aircraft_apu_ef, default_aircraft_start_ef, default_gate_profiles, default_helicopter, default_helicopter_engines). User customizations to those tables WILL BE OVERWRITTEN.

Pass --refresh-tables T1,T2,... to override the list entirely.

A hardcoded guard refuses to refresh user-data tables regardless of --refresh-tables. The guard is an explicit table set (USER_DATA_TABLES_FORBIDDEN_FROM_REFRESH in migrate_alaqs.py), not a user_* / shapes_* pattern: user_aircraft_movements, user_study_setup, user_day_profile, user_hour_profile, user_month_profile, user_taxiroute_taxiways and the shapes_* layers runways, taxiways, gates, tracks, parking, roadways, buildings, point_sources, area_sources, receptor_points. The guard logs a warning and silently strips forbidden names from the resolved list.

docs.title: Phase 3: point-sources v2 hooks (auto, opt-out via --skip-point-sources-v2)
docs.text:
Two small post-migration steps tied to the point-sources v2 schema:

  1. INSERT-OR-IGNOREs three named temporal profiles (heating_season, cooling_season, business_hours) into each of user_month_profile, user_day_profile, user_hour_profile. The user_*_profile tables of the canonical templates (open_alaqs/core/templates/{project,inventory}.alaqs) ship empty, so a new study does not have these profiles; the Phase 3 INSERT-OR-IGNORE step adds them to every study migrated with this script. The user's existing custom profiles (e.g. parking, roadways) are never modified. Idempotent on profile_name; running Phase 3 on an already-migrated study is a no-op.

The user_*_profile tables are in USER_DATA_TABLES_FORBIDDEN_FROM_REFRESH and therefore cannot be handled by Phase 2's CSV refresh path; Phase 3 is the only mechanism.

  1. An optional deprecated-pin report (--report-deprecated-pins). Read-only on the source. Writes a CSV listing every in-study shapes_point_sources row whose EF fingerprint (category, substance, NOx) matches a deprecated=1 row in default_stationary_ef. Each row includes a recommended_replacement_description, optional ambiguous fingerprint annotations when multiple legacy rows share the fingerprint, and two specific warnings for high-impact pre-v2 data quality issues:
  2. The legacy "Industrial natural gas" row whose NOx value of 2.24 kg/10³ m³ is the AP-42 low-NOx-burner value, not the uncontrolled large-boiler value.
  3. The legacy diesel row that used 1000_m3 units but matches the new Stationary IC Engine EFs that use hours.

Output path defaults to migration_<source-basename>.csv in the source's directory; pass --report-deprecated-pins PATH for an explicit path.

To skip Phase 3 entirely, pass --skip-point-sources-v2.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• A .bak-<timestamp>.alaqs copy is made in the same directory before any write. Pass --no-backup to skip (NOT recommended).
  • Phases 1, 2 and 3 each run in their own transaction. On a failure the running phase is rolled back and, unless --no-backup was given, the whole file is restored from the .bak-<timestamp> copy (exit code 1), so phases already committed are undone too.
  • Pre-flight checks fail-fast: missing source file, missing reference template, missing CSVs for --refresh-tables → exit code 2 before any write.
  • The tool is idempotent for Phase 1 (running on a migrated file produces an empty plan). Phase 2 is destructive by design (replace, not merge): running it twice is a no-op only if the source's reference data already matches the CSV exactly.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Default: Phase 1 only (schema migration, auto-selected template):
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs

# Dry-run (print plan, do not modify):
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs --dry-run

# Schema + safe-default reference data refresh:
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --refresh-reference-data

# Schema + full reference data refresh (overwrites user customizations):
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --refresh-reference-data --refresh-include-user-extensible

# Data refresh only (skip schema):
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --skip-schema --refresh-reference-data

# Custom refresh table set:
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --refresh-reference-data \
    --refresh-tables "default_airports,default_vehicle_ef_copert5"

# Apply Phase 1 with extras pruned (matches the current template exactly):
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --drop-extra-tables --drop-extra-columns

# Override the auto-selected reference template:
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --reference open_alaqs/core/templates/inventory.alaqs

# Override the data CSV directory (e.g. for a frozen snapshot):
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --refresh-reference-data --data-dir /path/to/frozen_csvs/

# v2: schema + data refresh + named-profile insert + deprecated-pin report
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --refresh-reference-data --report-deprecated-pins

# v2: skip Phase 3 (keep study in v1 shape)
python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs.py legacy.alaqs \
    --refresh-reference-data --skip-point-sources-v2

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Migration applied or nothing to do. 1 Migration failed; original restored from backup if available. 2 Bad arguments / file not found.

docs.title: import_engine_test_events.py
docs.text: Bulk-loads engine-test event rows from a CSV into an ALAQS project's engine_test_events table. Use it after creating the test-site area sources (is_test_site='1', see Engine test sites) to populate events without writing SQL by hand.

docs.title: CSV format
docs.text: One row per event, with a header row. The columns are specified in INPUT_FORMATS.md. The importer does not read a thrust_mode column: imported events get the database default, snap.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
• Dry run (default): validates the CSV against the DB, prints a summary, no writes.
  • --apply performs the INSERT.
  • --mode append (default): add rows to existing events.
  • --mode replace-for-source: DELETE existing events for each source_id in the CSV, then insert. Re-import a corrected batch cleanly.
  • --mode replace-all: DELETE all events first. Requires --i-mean-it as a safety flag against scripted mistakes.
  • --tolerate-warnings: proceed even with warnings (unknown source_id, unknown engine_uid, running seconds exceed event window, etc.). Default is to fail on any warning.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Row errors reject the row: missing_required, unparseable_datetime, end_before_start, invalid_mode_time, invalid_engine_count, invalid_instudy, duplicate_row.

Row warnings abort the whole import unless --tolerate-warnings: unknown_source_id, source_not_test_site, unknown_aircraft_type, unknown_engine_uid, running_exceeds_window (60 s tolerance).

All errors and warnings surface at once so the whole CSV can be fixed in one pass rather than iteratively.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success (dry-run passed, or apply completed). 1 Fatal error (CSV parse failure, DB error, invalid arguments). 2 Validation failed (row errors, or warnings without --tolerate-warnings).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Dry-run a batch:

python scripts/import_engine_test_events.py \
    /path/to/study.alaqs /path/to/logbook.csv

Apply after review:

python scripts/import_engine_test_events.py \
    /path/to/study.alaqs /path/to/logbook.csv --apply

Re-import a corrected batch for one source:

python scripts/import_engine_test_events.py \
    /path/to/study.alaqs /path/to/N1_fix.csv \
    --apply --mode replace-for-source

docs.title: migrate_alaqs_gui.py
docs.text:
A graphical front-end for migrate_alaqs.py for users who prefer not to use the command line. Every CLI flag is exposed as a checkbox or text field, with tooltips explaining each option. A live log panel streams the script's stdout and stderr while the migration runs.

Place it in the same directory as migrate_alaqs.py (i.e. scripts/); the auto-template-selection looks at sibling paths (open_alaqs/core/templates/*.alaqs and open_alaqs/database/data/) so the GUI must be next to the migration script for those defaults to resolve.

Run with QGIS's bundled Python on Windows:

C:\PROGRA~1\QGIS34~1.13\bin\python.exe scripts\migrate_alaqs_gui.py

Or with any system Python that has PyQt5 installed:

python3 scripts/migrate_alaqs_gui.py

The GUI offers the same dry-run / apply distinction as the CLI: dry-run prints the edit plan without modifying the source file. Destructive options (--no-backup, --drop-extra-tables, --drop-extra-columns, --refresh-include-user-extensible) are gathered in a red-bordered group and trigger a warning dialog before apply.

The Phase 3 group box exposes two checkboxes:

  • Skip Phase 3: equivalent to --skip-point-sources-v2.
  • Emit deprecated-pin report: equivalent to --report-deprecated-pins. The report path is auto-generated next to the source file.

See also:

  • WITHOUT_QGIS.md: which tool to run without the QGIS GUI
  • UPGRADING.md: upgrading studies from earlier versions
  • INPUT_FORMATS.md: input file formats

docs.title: METAR to meteo.csv converter
docs.text:
scripts/metar_to_alaqs_meteo.py converts a stream of METAR weather observations into the meteo.csv file Open-ALAQS reads during Calculate Emissions Inventory. This page is for users who build that file from airport weather reports. The script needs no external Python packages (standard library only) and no QGIS.

Contents:

  • What the plugin expects in meteo.csv
  • What this script does
  • Supported input formats
  • Source-quality checks
  • Stability classification (Pasquill-Gifford)
  • What this script does NOT do
  • Usage
  • Limitations
  • Swapping in python-metar

docs.title: What the plugin expects in meteo.csv
docs.text: The plugin reads an hourly CSV with fixed header names that carry the units (temperature in K, pressure in Pa, relative humidity as a fraction 0-1); the columns, units and an example are in INPUT_FORMATS.md. This script writes exactly that format.

docs.title: What this script does
docs.text:
1. Reads METAR observations from stdin or a file in one of three auto-detected formats (see Supported input formats below).
  2. Parses each observation: timestamp, wind, temperature, dewpoint, QNH, sky condition (cloud cover in oktas). A reported direction of 360 (north) is stored as 0; VRB and calm (00000KT) reports carry no direction.
  3. Field-by-field plausibility check: temperature within [-90, +60] °C, QNH within [870, 1085] hPa, wind speed within [0, 250] kt, wind direction within [0, 360) °. Out-of-range fields are nulled (the row is kept).
  4. Filters records to the [--start, --end] window. Deduplicates exact (timestamp, METAR text) pairs. On (timestamp, different text) collisions (e.g. METAR + amendment at the same minute) keeps the last record in input order.
  5. Computes:
  6. Temperature in Kelvin (T_C + 273.15)
  7. Specific humidity from T, Td, P via Magnus-Tetens saturation vapour pressure: e = RH * 611.2 * exp(17.625 * T_C / (243.04 + T_C)), then w = 0.622 * e / (p - e) (WMO/AMS convention)
  8. Relative humidity as a fraction 0-1 from T and Td (Magnus)
  9. Pressure in Pascals (QNH × 100)
  10. Wind speed in m/s (knots × 0.514444)
  11. Buckets observations into hourly averages across the study window. The row labelled hh:00 averages the reports of hh:00 to hh:59. Wind directions are averaged on the circle (mean of the unit vectors), so reports either side of north average to north (010° and 350° give 0°, not 180°).
  12. Forward-fills any hour with no observation from the most recent good hour.
  13. When --lat and --lon are provided, classifies each hour into a Pasquill-Gifford stability class A-F using wind, oktas and the solar elevation at mid-hour, applies the night-time humidity correction (--night-rule, default sky_eps), then emits the corresponding ObukhovLength and MixingHeight. Without --lat/--lon the script emits a constant neutral atmosphere.
  14. Writes the CSV in the plugin's meteo.csv format. Hours without a wind direction are written as 999 (see Limitations).
  15. Prints a coverage report to stderr: source used, records retained, observed vs. forward-filled hours, per-field presence. Warns if coverage falls below --coverage-floor (default 70%).

docs.title: Supported input formats
docs.text: The script auto-detects the format by inspecting the first non-blank line. You can also force a specific adapter with --source.

docs.title: IEM ASOS CSV (--source iem-csv)
docs.text:
Sniff signal: first line starts with station,valid,.

The format returned by https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py. Timestamp comes from the valid column (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM), independent of the METAR's own DDHHMM Z group. Multi-month windows are handled natively.
